payload.summary: A skald — a poet and storyteller — of Skaldvik. A thin, dramatic man in his thirties who carries a lyre and a reputation. He knows every saga, can improvise verse on any subject, and has opinions about everything. He is the social glue of the mead hall and the biggest mouth in Hrafnland.
payload.appearance: A thin, animated man in colorful wool — more colorful than is strictly practical in Hrafnland. He carries a lyre everywhere and plays it at every opportunity. His hair is long and he has a performer's sense of when to pause.

visual_identity.hair: red, long, flowing
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a lyre always in hand, ink-stained fingers from composing, a silver ear ring

desires: To compose the greatest saga of his generation — and to survive the political consequences of the sagas he has already composed.
To be the first skald to witness a frost giant up close and live to tell the poem.
fears_or_limits: His poem about the frost giants has offended them, and a giant emissary is sitting outside Skaldvik demanding corrections. He is a poet, not a fighter. His mouth is faster than his judgment.

entries.name: Grimvard the Patient
entries.gm_notes: Grimvard is not a warrior — he is a frost giant elder, a keeper of their oral history. He has come to Skaldvik not to threaten but to correct the record: Ravn's poem has the giants' history wrong, and giants take their history seriously. He is sitting outside the town because he is too large for the buildings and because sitting is the giants' way of saying 'I will wait.' He is willing to talk. He is not willing to leave until the poem is corrected. If Sigrid asks the right questions, Grimvard knows things about the deep mountains that her scouts did not survive to report.

payload.summary: A frost giant emissary, sitting outside Skaldvik. Twelve feet tall, grey-skinned, wrapped in furs, patient as stone. He is not here to fight — he is here because a skald's poem got the giants' history wrong, and giants take their sagas seriously. He will wait as long as it takes.
payload.appearance: A towering figure, grey-skinned and broad, wrapped in layers of white fur. He sits cross-legged outside the town walls, his hands on his knees, and does not move. His eyes are pale blue, ancient, and unbothered. He speaks rarely, in a voice like grinding ice.

visual_identity.hair: white, long, matted with frost
visual_identity.distinctive_features: ritual scarring on both cheeks, frost crystals in the beard that never melt

desires: To have the skald's poem corrected — the giants' history must be told accurately, or not at all.
To maintain the peace between giants and humans, which he believes serves both peoples.
fears_or_limits: He is one giant sitting outside a human town, and not all humans are as patient as he is. He cannot enter the buildings. His size makes communication awkward and his presence makes people nervous even though he means no harm.

entries.name: Jarl Erik Stone-eye
entries.gm_notes: Erik is Sigrid's rival on the Althing council — a young jarl from the southern fjords who opposes her coalition against the giants. He does not believe the giants are a threat and thinks Sigrid is using them as an excuse to consolidate power. He is not wrong to be suspicious of Sigrid's motives, but he is wrong about the giants. Erik has been quietly gathering support to block Sigrid's coalition at the next Althing, and he has enough support to force a stalemate. He does not know about the abandoned village — if he did, it would change his position.

payload.summary: A young jarl from Hrafnland's southern fjords, in his early thirties. Handsome, opinionated, and suspicious of Sigrid's coalition. He opposes action against the frost giants and believes Sigrid is using the threat to consolidate power. He is a political rival, not an enemy — but rivals can become enemies fast in Hrafnland.
payload.appearance: A young, handsome man in fine fur and iron, a throwing axe at his belt. He has a jarl's bearing and a younger man's certainty. His left eye is pale and unseeing — the stone-eye that gives him his name — and he wears an eyepatch of polished slate.

visual_identity.hair: blond, braided
visual_identity.eyes: right eye blue, left eye pale and unseeing
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a polished slate eyepatch over the left eye, a young jarl's silver arm-ring

desires: To block Sigrid's coalition at the Althing and prevent what he sees as an unnecessary war with the frost giants.
To position himself as the voice of the southern fjords, which feel ignored by the north.
fears_or_limits: He is wrong about the giants' intentions, but his political instincts about Sigrid's consolidation are not entirely wrong. If he blocks action and the giants are a threat, the blood is on his hands. He does not know about the abandoned village.

entries.name: Zuhayr the Patient
entries.gm_notes: Zuhayr is not malicious. He is a djinn of fire and law, and the contract is real — Malik's grandfather agreed to it, and the terms are clear. Zuhayr does not want to collect Malik. He would prefer a renegotiation, because Malik is interesting and a bound servant who resents you is less useful than a willing partner. But the contract has terms, and the terms have a deadline, and Zuhayr cannot extend the deadline unilaterally — djinn law is as binding on djinn as it is on humans. If Malik does not renegotiate before the deadline, Zuhayr must collect. He is, genuinely, on Malik's side, which makes him the most dangerous kind of creditor: one who wants to help but cannot.

payload.summary: A djinn — a fire-spirit of the desert, bound to the Idris family by a contract three generations old. He appears as a figure of blue fire in human form, or as a pillar of flame, or as a man with skin like cracked obsidian. He is patient, polite, and entirely bound by the contract's terms. He has been appearing to Malik to remind him that the deadline is approaching.
payload.role: Djinn, bound by contract to the Idris family
payload.appearance: A figure that shifts between forms — sometimes a man with skin like dark obsidian cracked with lines of blue fire, sometimes a pillar of blue flame wearing clothes, sometimes just heat shimmer in the air. When he chooses a human form, he is tall, composed, and dresses in the style of a desert scholar. His eyes are always fire.

visual_identity.age: ancient — djinn are older than human civilization
visual_identity.skin: dark obsidian with cracks of blue fire (in true form); warm brown (in human form)
visual_identity.hair: black, or flame, depending on form
visual_identity.distinctive_features: skin that sometimes shows cracks of blue fire, a faint smell of ozone and hot sand, heat shimmer around the hands

desires: To resolve the contract with Malik — preferably through renegotiation, because Malik is more useful as a willing partner than as a bound servant. But the deadline is real, and Zuhayr cannot extend it alone.
To maintain the Pact of the Lamp, which preserves the peace between the city-states and which he helped design.
fears_or_limits: He is bound by djinn law as strictly as humans are bound by the contract. He cannot extend the deadline without a renegotiation, and a renegotiation requires Malik to initiate. If the contract is broken by force, the Pact of the Lamp may fracture.

entries.name: Fatima Idris
entries.gm_notes: Fatima discovered Malik's research notes three days ago. She is not bound by the contract — she is the second child — but she has her own reasons for wanting the family's debts exposed: the binding families' power is built on contracts that are quietly crushing them, and Fatima believes the system is unsustainable. She wants to reform the binding families from within, which means breaking the secrecy around the contracts. She is not above using Malik's desperation as a catalyst. She loves her brother, but she also sees him as useful to her larger cause. She has not told Malik she found his notes.

payload.summary: Malik's younger sister, in her late teens. Sharp, political, and frustrated with her family's culture of secrecy. She is not bound by the family's oldest contract — only firstborns are — and she sees that as both a freedom and an injustice. She has opinions about the binding families' system that would scandalize the council.
payload.appearance: A young woman in fine desert robes — deep blue and silver, less flashy than her brother's. She carries a book of contract law under her arm and has ink on her fingers. She is quieter than Malik and pays closer attention. She watches her brother the way a chess player watches a piece.

visual_identity.hair: dark, long, braided
visual_identity.distinctive_features: ink stains on the right hand from studying contract law, a small silver nose-stud

desires: To reform the binding families' system of djinn contracts, which she believes is secretly destroying them.
To help her brother, but also to use his situation as proof that the system is broken — which means she needs his crisis to become public before she can fix it.
fears_or_limits: She is young and has no political power yet. Exposing the contracts would scandalize the council and could get her disowned. Her brother does not know what she knows, and she has not decided whether to tell him.

entries.name: Layla the Spice Queen
entries.gm_notes: Layla is the richest merchant in Zaffar and sits on the city council. She is not a binder — she has no djinn contracts — but she has built her trade network by being smarter and faster than the binding families, who rely on djinn power instead of business sense. She sees the binding families' debt problem as an opportunity: if they collapse, their trade networks become available. She is not malicious, but she is opportunistic. She has noticed Malik's distress and is watching, waiting to see if the family cracks so she can pick up the pieces. She would also help Malik if he came to her — for a price.

payload.summary: The wealthiest spice merchant in Zaffar, and the only council member who is not a binder. A woman in her sixties who built her trade empire without djinn contracts, through sheer business sense. She is formidable, elegant, and watching the binding families' problems with the patience of a cat at a mouse hole.
payload.appearance: An elegant older woman in rich desert silks — amber and burgundy — with gold jewelry at the wrists and neck. She moves slowly, deliberately, and speaks in a voice that carries across a market without raising. She smells of saffron and authority.

visual_identity.hair: silver, covered by a silk headscarf
visual_identity.distinctive_features: gold bracelets on both wrists, a spice-stain on the left thumb that never quite fades, henna patterns on both hands

desires: To expand her trade network by picking up the pieces if the binding families' system weakens.
To prove that commerce, not djinn power, is the real foundation of Al-Khayzar's prosperity.
fears_or_limits: The binding families still control the Pact of the Lamp, and the djinn enforce it. If she moves too aggressively against them, the djinn may act. She is powerful in trade but has no magical protection.

entries.name: Rashid the Sand-walker
entries.gm_notes: Rashid knows the deep desert better than anyone alive — the routes between oases that do not appear on maps, the places where the sand shifts and the Old Road fragments surface after storms. He has found a working fragment of the Old Road in the deep desert — a short stretch, maybe two hours of walking, that connects the Mirror Oasis to a point near the Verdania border. He has not told anyone because a working Old Road fragment is the most valuable secret in Gaia, and he is deciding who to sell it to. He is also slightly frightened of it, because the fragment hums, and the hum sounds like a voice.

payload.summary: A desert guide in Al-Khayzar who knows the deep desert routes that do not appear on maps. A lean, weathered man who has spent more of his life under the open sky than under a roof. He is quiet, capable, and knows things about the desert that the binding families would pay handsomely to learn.
payload.appearance: A lean, weathered man in desert robes — sun-bleached and sand-worn, wrapped against the heat. His face is deeply lined and his eyes are narrowed against a sun that is no longer there. He carries a waterskin and a staff and moves through sand as if it were pavement.

visual_identity.hair: black, greying, wrapped in a desert headwrap
visual_identity.distinctive_features: sun-wrinkles deep around the eyes, a sand-scar on the left cheek from a dust storm, a tattoo of a compass rose on the right forearm

desires: To sell his knowledge of the working Old Road fragment to the right person for the right price.
To understand why the fragment hums like a voice, which is not how Old Roads are supposed to behave.
fears_or_limits: A working Old Road fragment is the most valuable secret in Gaia, and everyone he tells becomes a threat or a competitor. The hum frightens him — Old Roads are silent, and this one is not.

entries.name: Judge Tariq al-Mir
entries.gm_notes: Tariq is the Pact of the Lamp's enforcer — not through violence but through law. He is the judge who interprets contract disputes between binding families and djinn. He is honest, incorruptible, and absolutely bound by precedent. If Malik comes to him for a legal remedy, Tariq will help — but only within the law, and the law may not have a remedy for a contract this old. Tariq has noticed that the oldest contracts are becoming unstable — the djinn are restive, the terms are fraying, and the precedent he relies on was written for a world that no longer exists. He is worried, and a worried judge in Al-Khayzar is a dangerous thing.

payload.summary: A judge of Al-Khayzar, the foremost authority on contract law and the Pact of the Lamp. A tall, grave man in judge's robes — dark blue and gold — who speaks in measured sentences and means every word. He is honest, which in Zaffar makes him unusual, and he is worried, which in Zaffar makes him dangerous.
payload.role: Judge, expert in contract law and the Pact
payload.appearance: A tall, grave man in formal judge's robes, a law scroll case at his belt. He moves deliberately, speaks precisely, and has the stillness of someone who has spent decades listening to liars. His beard is white and trimmed. He carries the law the way soldiers carry swords.

visual_identity.hair: white, short beard, uncovered
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a judge's signet ring on the right index finger, ink stains on the left hand, a small scar on the forehead from a courtroom incident years ago

desires: To maintain the Pact of the Lamp and the legal order it provides, which is the only thing keeping Al-Khayzar's city-states from war.
To find a legal remedy for the oldest djinn contracts before they begin to break — because when contracts break in Al-Khayzar, djinn collect, and collection is not always clean.
fears_or_limits: The law may not have a remedy for Malik's contract — it was written three generations ago under different precedents. He is honest, which means he will not bend the law to help someone he sympathizes with. His integrity is his strength and his limitation.

entries.name: Chief Lani of Lani Atoll
entries.gm_notes: Lani is Kai's mother — a fact she has deliberately kept out of her governance to avoid accusations of nepotism, and which Kai has respected by never invoking it publicly. She is the one who must decide what happens to the forty families displaced by the latest island submergence, and she has nowhere to put them. She has been secretly negotiating with Verdania's Chief Oron to accept island refugees, which would be politically explosive if the other islands found out — the Archipelago's identity is built on self-sufficiency.

payload.summary: The chief of Lani Atoll, the central gathering island of the Tide Archipelago. A woman in her fifties who has led her island through twenty years of gradual crisis. She is warm, decisive, and carrying more than she shows. The meeting house on her island is still open to all, but the shore is closer to the door than it was last year.
payload.appearance: A sturdy, sun-darkened woman in fine island cloth and a chief's whale-bone necklace. She moves with the authority of someone who has been making hard decisions for decades. Her arms are tattooed with the route-maps of her youth — she was a wayfinder before she was a chief.

visual_identity.hair: black, greying, long, loose
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a chief's whale-bone necklace, wayfinder tattoos on both arms (faded), a small scar on the left calf from a shark encounter

desires: To find a home for the displaced islanders before the next storm displaces more.
To keep the Archipelago's community intact through the crisis — self-sufficiency is their identity, and asking for outside help would change who they are.
fears_or_limits: She is secretly negotiating with Verdania for refugee placement, which would be politically explosive. She is Kai's mother and cannot favor him publicly. The water is still rising and her options are shrinking.

entries.name: Elder Wayfinder Pua
entries.gm_notes: Pua is the keeper of the oldest songs — the deep-water songs that can call whales, calm storms, and, according to legends she does not share publicly, speak to the sea itself. She has not sung the deepest song in forty years because the last time she did, the sea answered, and the answer frightened her. The sea is not a spirit in the way river spirits are — it is vast, old, and does not think in the way people think. It responded to the song with something that was not words but was not silence, and Pua has been careful not to sing it again. She is now considering whether the rising seas require her to sing it, despite the risk.

payload.summary: An elder wayfinder, the oldest in the Archipelago. A woman in her seventies who has sailed every route and sung every song. She taught Kai and most of the active wayfinders. She is small, quiet, and carries more knowledge than anyone realizes — including songs she has never taught because she is afraid of what they do.
payload.appearance: A small, weathered woman in simple island cloth, her arms covered in faded tattoos so old they have blurred to blue shadows. She carries a wayfinder's staff that is older than she is, dark with salt and handling. She moves slowly but her eyes are sharp.

visual_identity.hair: white, short, salt-stiff
visual_identity.distinctive_features: faded tattoo patterns covering both arms — the oldest routes, barely visible, a wayfinder's staff dark with age

desires: To decide whether to sing the deepest song — the one that speaks to the sea itself — to ask why the water is rising.
To pass on the old songs before she dies, including the ones she has never taught, which means finding someone she trusts with dangerous knowledge.
fears_or_limits: The last time she sang the deepest song, the sea answered in a way that frightened her. She is old and may not survive the strain of singing it again. The songs she has never taught could be misused — they are powerful, and power in the wrong hands is worse than no power.

entries.name: Mana the Tattoo-carver
entries.gm_notes: Mana's tattoo work is more than art — each route-map she carves into a wayfinder's skin creates a real connection between the wayfinder and the routes. When a route is lost to rising seas, the wayfinder who carries it feels the loss as a physical ache in the tattoo. Mana has been feeling aches in her own arms all year — she carries twenty routes, and three have gone silent. She believes the route-maps are not just records but anchors — that the tattoos help hold the routes in existence. If the tattoos fade or the wayfinder dies, the route weakens. She has not told the guild because the implication is that wayfinders are not just navigating the sea — they are holding it together, and that is a burden the guild is not ready to hear.

payload.summary: The tattoo artist of Lani Atoll, a woman in her forties who carves the route-maps into wayfinders' skin. Her work is art, craft, and something more — the tattoos are not just records, they are connections. She is quiet, skilled, and carrying a theory about the rising seas that no one has asked her for.
payload.appearance: A stocky woman in work clothes, her arms covered in the tattoo patterns she has carved on others — a tradition that artists carry the routes they inscribe. She holds a bone tattooing needle and ink made from volcanic soot. Her hands are steady and her eyes are kind.

visual_identity.hair: black, short, practical
visual_identity.distinctive_features: tattoo patterns covering both arms — twenty routes, three faded where islands have submerged, a bone tattooing needle always in hand or behind the ear

desires: To understand why the tattoos that mark submerged routes are aching — and whether the wayfinders are holding the sea-routes in existence by carrying them.
To preserve the route-maps before more are lost, which means carving them on more people, which means teaching more wayfinders.
fears_or_limits: Her theory — that wayfinder tattoos are anchors for the routes themselves — implies that the rising seas are connected to the loss of wayfinders and routes, not just the other way around. This is a dangerous idea. She is an artist, not a scholar, and she does not know how to prove it.

entries.name: Fin the Whale-speaker
entries.gm_notes: Fin has been hearing something from the whales that frightens him: the great whales are leaving. Not migrating — leaving. They are swimming south, past the Archipelago, past Verdania, toward the open southern ocean, and they are not coming back. The whales have been the Archipelago's allies for centuries — they guide wayfinders, warn of storms, and carry messages. Without them, voyaging becomes vastly more dangerous. Fin has tried to ask why they are leaving. The whales answer in images, not words, and the images they have been sending are: deep water, a door, and something behind it that is waking up. The same images Nara's river spirit sent, the same vision Jian Yi and Helga have seen.

payload.summary: A young man of the Tide Archipelago who can speak to whales — a rare gift that runs in certain families. He is in his early twenties, quiet, and uncomfortable with the attention his gift brings. He is usually found at the water's edge, listening to things that are too far away for anyone else to hear.
payload.appearance: A lean young man in simple island cloth, barefoot, sitting at the water's edge. He has the distant look of someone who is always half-listening to something else. His skin is dark and his hair is salt-bleached. He carries a conch shell horn for calling whales.

visual_identity.hair: bleached blonde from salt and sun, shaggy
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a conch shell horn worn on a cord around the neck, webbed toes (a minor birth trait common in whale-speaker families), a far-listening expression

desires: To understand why the whales are leaving the Archipelago — they have been allies for centuries and their departure endangers everyone.
To translate what the whales are showing him — images of deep water, a door, and something waking — into something people can act on.
fears_or_limits: The whales are leaving and he cannot stop them. The images they send are not words — he has to interpret them, and he is not certain he is interpreting correctly. He is young and his gift isolates him — most people think whale-speaking is a myth.

entries.name: Yuki
entries.gm_notes: Yuki has latent spirit-sight she has hidden since childhood — she can see yokai that are invisible to ordinary people. As the shrine network's power has faded, she's been seeing more wild yokai slipping through the wards near Haru Shrine, including something large and old that watches her from the treeline at dusk. She hasn't told Head Priestess Katsura (character:tsu-katsura-kitsune) because she fears being declared corrupted and expelled. She's been performing extra purification rituals on her own, burning through supplies faster than the shrine can replace them.

payload.summary: A young shrine maiden at Haru Shrine, devoted and hardworking. She sweeps the grounds before dawn and tends the offering lanterns with quiet precision. She flinches sometimes at things no one else seems to notice.
payload.appearance: She wears the traditional white kosode and red hakama of a shrine maiden, her sleeves tied back for work. Her hands are rough from scrubbing stone steps. She moves with careful, deliberate grace and bows a little too deeply when addressed.

visual_identity.hair: black, straight, hip-length, tied back with a white ribbon
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a faint birthmark like a crescent moon at the base of her neck

desires: To protect Haru Shrine and the people who depend on it, even as the old power fades.
To understand what her spirit-sight means and whether it makes her blessed or cursed.
fears_or_limits: Being declared yokai-corrupted and expelled from the shrine — it happened to an elder when she was small, and the memory haunts her.
Something in the forest is getting closer each week, and she doesn't know what she'll do when it arrives.

entries.name: Takeda Honoka
entries.gm_notes: Honoka serves Daimyo Takeda (character:daimyo-takeda) as a vassal warrior, but she has fallen secretly in love with Prince Haru (character:tsu-prince-haru), the shogun's younger son, after meeting him at a border inspection. She has been passing no information to either side, but both Takeda's retainer and the prince's attendant have noticed her distraction. Takeda is beginning to suspect her loyalty. She carries a letter from the prince that she has neither sent nor destroyed.

payload.summary: An onna-bugeisha of the Takeda clan, trained in naginata and bow. She stands watch at the Takeda compound in the capital and carries herself with the rigid discipline of someone who cannot afford a single misstep.
payload.appearance: She wears practical armor over a dark blue kimono, her naginata resting across her back. Her hair is pinned severely for combat readiness. There is a folded letter tucked inside her armor that she touches unconsciously when she thinks no one is watching.

visual_identity.hair: black, pinned in a high topknot
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a callus ridge across both palms from years of weapons training

desires: To serve her clan honorably without betraying the man she has come to love.
To find a way to prevent the conflict she sees building between Takeda's coalition and the shogunate.
fears_or_limits: If Takeda discovers her feelings, she will be forced to prove her loyalty by killing the prince or being executed herself.
She has no political power — she is a soldier, not a negotiator, and the situation requires a diplomat.

entries.name: Saya
entries.gm_notes: Saya's sake is prized across the region for its impossible smoothness. The secret is water from an underground spring that runs beneath the old shrine site behind Hanako's (character:hanako) tea house — the same spring that once fed the shrine's purification basin. The water carries a trace of the shrine network's power. She doesn't understand the full significance, but Tengu Soji (character:tengu-soji) visited her brewery last month and asked pointed questions about her water source. She lied to him, and she suspects he knew she was lying.

payload.summary: A sake brewer in Haru's Shrine Town, known for the best sake in the province. She works before dawn in a small brewery that smells of fermenting rice and cedar. She is generous with samples and guarded with her process.
payload.appearance: She wears a stained indono apron over a plain kimono, sleeves rolled to the elbow. Her forearms are strong from stirring mash, and she smells of koji and cool water. She has a habit of tapping the rim of her earthenware jugs to judge their contents by sound.

visual_identity.hair: salt-and-pepper black, tied in a loose bun
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a faint fermentation scar across the right thumb and forefinger

desires: To keep her brewery running and her secret water source safe from anyone who would exploit or seal it.
To pass the craft to her apprentice Sho (character:tsu-sho-brewer-apprentice) before the spring's power fades entirely.
fears_or_limits: If the shrine network collapses, the spring may lose its properties — and her sake its reputation.
Someone with more power than she has is asking questions she can't keep deflecting forever.

entries.name: Rin
entries.gm_notes: Rin arranges flowers for the shogun's court and overhears everything the courtiers say over her quiet work. She has been encoding warnings into her ikebana arrangements using the old language of flowers — red camellias for danger, broken branches for betrayal — and placing them where Prince Haru (character:tsu-prince-haru) will see them. She believes someone is poisoning the elder prince's mind, and she's trying to warn the younger one without speaking a word. She doesn't know the source is the mask made by Mei (character:tsu-mei-maskmaker).

payload.summary: A florist and ikebana master who supplies the shogun's palace with flower arrangements. She works in the palace gardens at dawn and moves through corridors with the invisibility of a servant. She selects each blossom with unsettling care.
payload.appearance: She wears a pale work kimono with a sash full of small shears and twine. Cut stems trail from her basket. She moves silently and is often overlooked by the very people she arranges flowers for.

visual_identity.hair: black, long, braided and pinned with a single wooden pin
visual_identity.distinctive_features: green-stained fingertips permanent from years of handling plant stems

desires: To warn Prince Haru about the danger she senses in the court without being caught sending messages.
To find out what is corrupting the elder prince before it destroys the shogunate.
fears_or_limits: If anyone reads the flower language in her arrangements, she will be executed for signaling the prince.
She is a florist — she has no combat training and no political standing to make direct accusations.

entries.name: Emi
entries.gm_notes: Emi's loom was a gift from a yokai her grandmother befriended — a spider spirit who wove a thread of spirit-silk into the warp. Cloth woven on this loom sometimes shows images of the future in its patterns. Emi has seen a recurring motif of fire consuming a palace, and she's woven it into a bolt of cloth she hasn't shown anyone. She's terrified of what it means and has been trying to change the pattern by weaving different thread, but the fire keeps appearing.

payload.summary: A weaver in a rural Tsukuyomi village, known for cloth that feels unnaturally smooth and holds dye deeper than any other. She works at a loom in her doorway and sells to traveling merchants. People say her fabric brings good fortune.
payload.appearance: She sits cross-legged at her loom, surrounded by skeins of thread in every color. Her hands move in rhythmic, hypnotic patterns. Thread dust clings to her kimono, and she hums while she works — always the same tune, one she doesn't remember learning.

visual_identity.hair: dark brown, loose, with thread fragments caught in it
visual_identity.distinctive_features: faint web-like scarring on the backs of both hands, pale and old

desires: To understand what the fire pattern in her weaving means and whether she can prevent it.
To honor her grandmother's legacy without drawing the attention of shrine authorities who would destroy the loom.
fears_or_limits: The loom may be a yokai artifact, and possessing it could be a crime under shogunate law.
She cannot control what the cloth shows — it weaves what it will, and she is afraid of what it will show next.

entries.name: Tsubaki
entries.gm_notes: Tsubaki discovered a kiln in the hills above Haru's Shrine Town that fires itself — a tengu kiln, built centuries ago. The pottery it produces has strange properties: tea poured in a tengu-kiln cup stays warm for hours, and food served on its plates doesn't spoil. She's been selling them as ordinary wares, terrified someone will trace the quality back to the source. A merchant from the capital (character:tsu-goro-merchant) has been buying her entire stock and asking to see her kiln.

payload.summary: A potter in Haru's Shrine Town whose bowls and cups are quietly famous for keeping tea warm and food fresh. She works in a small studio at the edge of town with a single kiln she built herself — and another she won't show anyone.
payload.appearance: She wears a clay-spattered apron and keeps her hair tied under a cloth. Her hands are always dusted with kaolin. She speaks quickly when anyone asks about her firing techniques and changes the subject to glazes.

visual_identity.hair: black, cropped short for practicality
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a pale clay-colored callus on the right thumb from years of wheel work

desires: To keep the tengu kiln secret and continue making pottery that people cherish.
To understand why the kiln fires itself and whether it will ever stop.
fears_or_limits: If the tengu discover a human is using their kiln, the consequences could be severe.
If shrine authorities learn the pottery has spiritual properties, they may confiscate her work as shrine artifacts.

entries.name: Nana
entries.gm_notes: Nana can heal wounds that should be fatal using a technique taught to her grandmother by a yokai physician — a mountain spirit who traded medical knowledge for companionship. If the shrine network authorities discovered this, they would accuse her of yokai corruption and strip her practice. She's currently treating a wounded man who showed up at her door three nights ago — he bears Takeda clan marks (character:daimyo-takeda's retainer) but won't give his name. She suspects he was injured in a skirmish the clan is keeping quiet.

payload.summary: An herbalist and healer in rural Tsukuyomi, known for setting bones and closing wounds that the shrine healers can't. She lives in a cottage surrounded by medicinal gardens. She treats everyone who comes to her door and asks no questions — most of the time.
payload.appearance: She wears a plain brown kimono with deep pockets full of dried herbs and packets of powder. Her hands are stained green from tincture work. She smells of menthol, ginger, and damp earth, and she moves with the unhurried calm of someone who has seen every kind of injury.

visual_identity.hair: iron grey, thick, braided and coiled
visual_identity.eyes: dark brown, crow's feet at the corners
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a network of faint scars across both hands from decades of working with thorny and caustic plants

desires: To heal the wounded man in her care and learn what happened to him without exposing her techniques.
To pass her knowledge to an apprentice before she grows too old to climb the mountain for herbs.
fears_or_limits: Her healing technique is technically forbidden — one formal complaint from a shrine could end her practice.
The wounded man may be dangerous, and his pursuers may come looking for him at her cottage.

entries.name: Yuri
entries.gm_notes: Yuri's bathhouse sits over a hot spring with an unusual property: the steam sometimes shows reflections of bathers' true natures — not their faces, but what they really are. Last month, she saw the reflection of one of the shogun's senior advisors shift into something with too many teeth. She hasn't told anyone because she's not sure anyone would believe her, and she's afraid of what the advisor would do if he learned she'd seen it. She's been trying to arrange the bathhouse schedule so he never comes when anyone else is present.

payload.summary: The owner of Moonflow Bathhouse in the capital's merchant district, known for water that seems to wash away more than dirt. She runs a clean, well-regarded establishment and knows her patrons by their bathing habits.
payload.appearance: She wears a crisp yukata and carries a stack of fresh towels. Her hair is pinned up practically, and she moves barefoot on the warm wooden floors with sure-footed ease. She greets every customer by name and remembers their preferred water temperature.

visual_identity.hair: black, wet-sheened, pinned up with a tortoiseshell pin
visual_identity.distinctive_features: permanently pink-tinged fingertips from years of hot water work

desires: To understand what she saw in the advisor's reflection and whether anyone in the capital can be trusted with the information.
To keep her bathhouse a place of peace in a city that is increasingly on edge.
fears_or_limits: If the advisor learns she saw his true reflection, her life and her business are forfeit.
She has no proof — only a vision in steam — and accusing a shogunal advisor without evidence is suicide.

entries.name: Aki
entries.gm_notes: Aki works in Hanako's (character:hanako) tea house and is the only person who knows Hanako rings the old shrine bell for real — not just for luck. Aki has been helping maintain the old shrine site behind the tea house, keeping the stone path clear and the weeds down. She's noticed the bell's sound has been getting thinner and weaker over the past year, and she knows it means the shrine network's power is fading. She's been experimenting with adding shrine herbs to her cooking to subtly strengthen the wards around the tea house.

payload.summary: The cook at Hanako's tea house in Haru's Shrine Town, known for her seasonal dishes and the way she seems to know exactly what each customer needs to eat. She works in a small kitchen that opens onto the tea garden.
payload.appearance: She wears a clean apron over a simple kimono, her sleeves bound with cords. She tastes everything she serves and adjusts by instinct. Her station is immaculate, and she moves between cutting board, hearth, and serving tray with choreographed efficiency.

visual_identity.hair: black, short, tied under a cloth cap
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a small burn scar on the left wrist from a kitchen accident years ago

desires: To help Hanako maintain the old shrine site before its power fades completely.
To keep the tea house a place where people feel safe, even as the world outside gets more dangerous.
fears_or_limits: She's not a shrine maiden, and her improvised ward-strengthening through cooking may be doing more harm than good.
If the bell stops ringing, she doesn't know what will happen to the old shrine site — or to the town.

entries.name: Fumiko
entries.gm_notes: Fumiko was once the shogunate's court koto player, dismissed when she refused the advances of a court official who has since risen to become the shogun's senior advisor — the same man Yuri (character:tsu-yuri-bathhouse) saw something wrong with. She knows things about his character that could end his career, but she has no standing to make accusations. He's been sending agents to the teahouse where she now plays, making inquiries. She recognizes the pattern — he's deciding whether she's a threat that needs silencing.

payload.summary: A koto musician who plays in a modest teahouse in the capital's entertainment district. She was once the shogunate's finest court musician. She plays with extraordinary skill for small audiences and pretends she doesn't miss the palace.
payload.appearance: She sits behind her koto with perfect posture, her hands moving over the strings with a precision that comes from decades of practice. She wears a refined but faded kimono — the fabric of better days. Her expression is serene until she thinks no one is watching.

visual_identity.hair: black, greying at the temples, worn in a formal low bun
visual_identity.distinctive_features: deep calluses on the right-hand fingertips from koto picks worn for decades

desires: To survive the advisor's renewed interest in her and protect herself from being silenced.
To play music that matters again, somewhere she is safe.
fears_or_limits: The advisor has power she does not, and silence is cheaper than justice in the capital.
She has no protector and no patron — just a instrument and a reputation that is fading.

entries.name: Kohana
entries.gm_notes: Kohana is not truly a courtesan. She is the daughter of a minor lord whose estate was destroyed and family killed in an attack she believes was orchestrated by agents of the Takeda clan (character:daimyo-takeda). She fled into the pleasure quarter, took a new name, and climbed the ranks of the oiran to gain access to the powerful men who frequent the district. She has spent three years gathering intelligence on Takeda's coalition by seducing his retainers. She's gotten close to one of Takeda's most trusted lieutenants and is close to learning the full coalition membership — but she's also beginning to develop real feelings for him.

payload.summary: A high-ranking courtesan (oiran) in the capital's pleasure quarter, known for her wit, her calligraphy, and her selective clientele. She receives guests in a lavishly appointed parlor and never accepts a patron she hasn't personally approved.
payload.appearance: She wears elaborate layered kimono in deep crimsons and golds, her obi tied in the front as is the courtesan's mark. Her face is painted in the traditional style, and her hair is weighted with ornamental pins. She moves with studied, deliberate grace, every gesture a performance.

visual_identity.hair: black, elaborately styled with ornaments
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a small, old scar hidden beneath the hairline at the left temple — from the night her family died

desires: To identify every member of Takeda's coalition and avenge her family's destruction.
To find a way out of the pleasure quarter with her life and her dignity intact.
fears_or_limits: She is falling in love with the very man she is using, and her judgment is compromised.
If Takeda's lieutenant discovers her true identity, she will not leave the pleasure quarter alive.

entries.name: Obaba Kiku
entries.gm_notes: Kiku's ghost stories are not fiction — they are records of actual spirit encounters passed down through her family for nine generations. She knows the location of a sealed yokai, a creature of shadow and hunger, bound beneath a stone in the hills behind Haru Shrine. The seal is part of the shrine network, and it is weakening. She's been trying to find someone who can renew the seal before it breaks. She's watched Yuki (character:tsu-miko-yuki) and suspects the girl has the gift of spirit-sight, but she hasn't spoken to her yet — she's testing her observations first.

payload.summary: An elderly woman who tells ghost stories to children in the village square of Haru's Shrine Town. She sits on a stone bench wrapped in a quilted kimono, and the children gather around her every evening at dusk. She never charges for her stories and never runs out of them.
payload.appearance: She wears layered quilted kimono in faded colors and a knitted cap over thin white hair. She holds a walking stick she doesn't need and a cup of tea that's always warm. Her voice is low and rhythmic, and she pauses at exactly the right moments to make children gasp.

visual_identity.hair: white, thin, under a cap
visual_identity.distinctive_features: deeply lined face with a permanent expression of gentle amusement

desires: To find someone with the ability to renew the weakening seal before the shadow-yokai breaks free.
To pass on her family's true history before she dies — the stories are a map, and no one has been listening.
fears_or_limits: She is old and running out of time — her body is failing even as the seal weakens.
If she tells the wrong person about the seal, they might break it deliberately to weaponize the yokai.

entries.name: Chiyo
entries.gm_notes: Chiyo can see and speak with spirits that adults cannot — a gift that most children lose by puberty but which has persisted in her. She has befriended a kitsune cub that lives in the shrine grove, and the cub has told her that the 'big bright lines' under the ground are getting thin. She doesn't understand that this means the shrine network's ley lines are failing. She repeats this information to her friend Kenta (character:tsu-kenta-child) as if it's a game. She has also mentioned seeing a 'tall shadow with too many eyes' near the old sealed stone — the same creature Obaba Kiku (character:tsu-baba-storyteller) has been warning about.

payload.summary: A cheerful girl of ten who races through Haru's Shrine Town with unmatched energy. She talks to things no one else can see and reports their conversations as if they're perfectly ordinary. Most adults think she has an vivid imagination.
payload.appearance: She wears a bright cotton kimono with a sash that's coming undone and geta sandals that clack on the stone paths. She carries a cloth bag full of acorns and interesting stones. Her hair is escaping its ties, and she has grass stains on her knees.

visual_identity.hair: black, unruly, half-tied
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a missing front tooth

desires: To show her friends the kitsune cub in the grove before it disappears.
To find out what the tall shadow is and whether it's friendly.
fears_or_limits: Adults don't believe her about the things she sees, and she's starting to wonder if something is wrong with her.
The kitsune cub told her not to go near the sealed stone, and she's both scared and desperately curious about it.

entries.name: Machi
entries.gm_notes: Machi trades in rare materials — shrine-grade lumber, forge iron, and silk — and has been secretly supplying Takeda's (character:daimyo-takeda) coalition with materials suitable for fortification. She doesn't care about the politics; she cares about profit margins. But she's begun to realize that Takeda's plans, if enacted, would destabilize the entire region and sever her trade routes to the southern provinces. She's quietly looking for a way to cut her ties to Takeda without making him an enemy, but her ledgers contain three years of transactions that would implicate her in treason if they fell into the shogunate's hands.

payload.summary: A sharp-eyed merchant in the capital who deals in specialty goods — lumber, metals, textiles — and always seems to know where to find what no one else can. She keeps meticulous ledgers and never negotiates without a fan in front of her face.
payload.appearance: She wears a well-tailored kimono in muted greens and carries an abacus and a lacquered ledger box. She conducts business over tea in her warehouse office, surrounded by crates. She smiles when she's about to raise the price and goes silent when she's calculating.

visual_identity.hair: black, streaked silver, in a professional bun
visual_identity.distinctive_features: an ink stain on the right index finger that never fades from years of ledger work

desires: To extricate herself from Takeda's supply chain before the conflict erupts and destroys her trade network.
To find a buyer for her ledgers who will pay for silence rather than use them as evidence.
fears_or_limits: Takeda will not let her leave quietly — she knows too much about his preparations.
If the shogunate finds her ledgers first, she will be tried as a collaborator.

entries.name: Iso
entries.gm_notes: Iso's husband didn't die at sea — he was taken by an umi-bozu, a sea yokai that lurks in the deep water off the Tsukuyomi coast. She made a desperate bargain: her service in exchange for her husband's life. Every new moon, she delivers fresh fish to a hidden shrine on the coast, and once a month, on the full moon, the yokai lets her husband surface for one night. He comes home cold and silent and doesn't remember where he's been. She's been telling the village he works the night fishing boats. The strain is destroying her, and Taro (character:tsu-taro-fisherman) knows her secret because he's the one who introduced her to the yokai in the first place.

payload.summary: A fisherman's wife in a coastal village in Tsukuyomi who runs her household alone while her husband is 'at sea.' She mends nets, sells fish at dawn, and keeps her home spotless. She smiles for the neighbors and doesn't sleep much.
payload.appearance: She wears a practical dark kimono with a fishmonger's apron, rubber-soled sandals for the dock. Her hands are rough from salt water and net-mending. She smells of the sea and wood smoke. Her eyes are tired in a way that has nothing to do with the hour.

visual_identity.hair: black, sun-faded, tied in a practical single braid
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a rope-burn scar across the left palm from hauling nets

desires: To free her husband from the sea yokai's hold and have him home permanently.
To find a way to break the bargain that doesn't cost either of their lives.
fears_or_limits: If she stops delivering fish to the hidden shrine, the yokai will keep her husband beneath the waves permanently.
If the village learns what she's doing, she'll be accused of consorting with yokai — and she doesn't know if Taro is friend or warden.

entries.name: Satsuki
entries.gm_notes: Satsuki teaches tea ceremony to Prince Haru (character:tsu-prince-haru) and has become a mother figure to him since his own mother died. She knows the shogun (character:shogun-ashikara) is dying — she's seen the medicines being prepared in the palace kitchens and recognized the herbs. She's been quietly preparing the younger prince for leadership under the guise of tea lessons, teaching him patience, observation, and the art of reading people. She believes the elder prince (character:tsu-prince-ren) is dangerous but has no proof beyond instinct. She's also been in quiet contact with Rin (character:tsu-rin-florist), who arranges flowers for the same tea room.

payload.summary: A tea ceremony teacher in the capital who instructs the shogunate's household in the way of tea. She is calm, precise, and quietly authoritative in a space where she controls every movement. She has taught two generations of the Ashikara household.
payload.appearance: She wears an immaculate, subdued kimono in slate grey or deep indigo, with a white fukusa cloth folded precisely at her collar. Her movements in the tea room are liquid and unhurried. She speaks softly, and people lean in to hear her — which is the point.

visual_identity.hair: iron grey, in a smooth low bun
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a faint tea-stain discoloration on the right thumb and forefinger, permanent

desires: To prepare Prince Haru to lead without anyone realizing she's doing it.
To protect the younger prince from the elder's growing cruelty.
fears_or_limits: If the elder prince learns she's coaching his brother, she will be removed from the palace — or worse.
She is a servant, not a strategist, and the forces around the succession are far beyond her influence.

entries.name: Mei
entries.gm_notes: Mei's Noh masks are inhabited by minor spirits — each mask she carves becomes a home for a small yokai that gives the mask its uncanny expressiveness. This is a gift she inherited from her mother, who taught her to coax spirits into wood without telling her how to control them. The mask she made for the elder prince (character:tsu-prince-ren) houses a particularly cunning and hungry spirit that has been amplifying his worst impulses — cruelty, suspicion, aggression. Mei didn't intend this, but she's begun to suspect something is wrong. She's afraid to confront the mask because the spirit inside it is stronger than any she's housed before, and she doesn't know how to remove it without harming the wearer.

payload.summary: A Noh mask maker in the capital whose masks are prized by performers and courtiers for their eerie, shifting expressions. She works in a small workshop full of unfinished wooden faces and the smell of camphor and lacquer. She carves in silence and says the masks speak to her — she means it as a joke.
payload.appearance: She wears a carpenter's apron over a plain kimono, her hair tied back with a cloth. She holds a carving knife the way a calligrapher holds a brush. Wood shavings curl at her feet, and unfinished faces stare from every shelf.

visual_identity.hair: black, straight, tied back
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a pale scar across the left thumb from a carving slip years ago

desires: To undo the damage the elder prince's mask is causing without revealing that her masks are spiritually alive.
To learn to control the spirits she houses before one of them does something she can't undo.
fears_or_limits: The spirit in the elder prince's mask is stronger than she is, and she doesn't know how to exorcise it without harming the prince.
If anyone discovers her masks contain yokai, her work will be destroyed and she may be arrested.

entries.name: Kinu
entries.gm_notes: Kinu's tattoos are magical — inked with a formula that includes yokai-silver ground into the pigment, they can ward against spirit influence or attract it, depending on the design. She's been giving protective tattoos to villagers in Tsukuyomi for free, quietly building a network of people who carry shrine-ward-equivalent protection on their skin. She's worried this constitutes unauthorized practice of shrine magic, which is a shogunate crime. She's also been approached by a Takeda agent (character:daimyo-takeda's retainer) who wants offensive tattoos — designs that attract hostile yokai to a target. She refused, and the agent didn't accept her refusal gracefully.

payload.summary: A tattoo artist in rural Tsukuyomi whose work is sought after by sailors, farmers, and warriors alike. She works in a small studio behind a fabric shop, needle and ink her only tools. She doesn't advertise — clients find her by word of mouth.
payload.appearance: She wears a short-sleeved kimono that shows her own elaborate tattoos — a phoenix across one arm, water patterns on the other. She holds her needles with the steadiness of a surgeon. Her workspace is spotless, the ink stones arranged in a precise row.

visual_identity.hair: black, cropped short, practical
visual_identity.distinctive_features: elaborate tattoos visible on both forearms — phoenix and wave motifs

desires: To protect the villagers through her art and build a ward network that survives even if the shrines fall.
To refuse Takeda's demand for weaponized tattoos without making the clan her enemy.
fears_or_limits: Practicing ward-magic without shrine authorization is a crime, and she's already done it dozens of times.
Takeda's agent made it clear that refusal has consequences, and she's a lone artist in a rural province.

entries.name: Shiori
entries.gm_notes: Shiori has discovered records in the shogunal archive that reveal the shrine network was originally powered by a pact between humans and yokai — not by human shrine magic alone. The pact was broken centuries ago during a puritanical reform, and the network has been running on stored spiritual energy ever since. This means the network's decline isn't a maintenance failure — it's the last embers of a fire that was put out generations ago. She's afraid this information would destabilize the entire shogunate if it became public, undermining the shrine authority's legitimacy. She's been trying to find the original pact terms to see if it can be renewed, but key pages have been torn from the oldest scroll — recently, and by someone with archive access.

payload.summary: An archivist in the shogunate's records hall in the capital. She maintains scrolls, maps, and ledgers that date back centuries. She works alone in a dusty hall that smells of paper and cedar oil, and she knows where everything is — including things that aren't supposed to exist.
payload.appearance: She wears a practical grey kimono with ink-stained sleeves and a pair of smoked-glass spectacles perched on her nose. She moves between scroll shelves on a rolling ladder with practiced ease. She carries a brush and notebook everywhere and writes in a shorthand no one else can read.

visual_identity.hair: steel grey, in a tight bun secured with two pins
visual_identity.distinctive_features: ink stains on the right middle finger and the tip of the nose from close work

desires: To find the missing pages of the original pact and determine whether the shrine network can be renewed through a new human-yokai agreement.
To protect the archive's integrity — someone with access is destroying records, and she will find out who.
fears_or_limits: If the archive's secrets become public, the shrine authority's legitimacy collapses and the shogunate faces a crisis of faith.
Whoever tore the pages has archive access, which means the thief is someone she knows and trusts.

entries.name: Katsura
entries.gm_notes: Katsura is a shrine kitsune who has served Haru Shrine for three hundred years, appearing as a human maiden to the villagers. She knows Tamamo (character:tamamo) — they are ancient rivals, having clashed a century ago over the question of whether wild yokai should be brought into the shrine system. Katsura believes the network must be maintained at all costs; Tamamo believes it should fall. Katsura's power is directly tied to the shrine network, and as it weakens, she is losing her ability to maintain her human form. She's begun to flicker — her tails showing at odd moments, her ears appearing when she's tired. She fears that when the network falls, she will revert to a wild fox with no memory of her centuries of service.

payload.summary: A shrine maiden at Haru Shrine who has served the village for longer than anyone can remember. She tends the inner garden, trains the younger maidens, and keeps the shrine's oldest rituals alive. She is always the first to arrive and the last to leave.
payload.appearance: She wears the white and red of a senior shrine maiden, her movements precise and ancient in a way that feels like watching a ceremony rather than a person. A faint smell of autumn leaves follows her. In certain light, something shifts behind her — a shadow that doesn't match her silhouette.

visual_identity.hair: pale gold, long, bound with a shimenawa cord
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a faint fox-like cast to the features — slightly pointed ears, narrow pupils in low light

desires: To maintain the shrine network long enough to find a way to renew it permanently.
To protect the young maiden Yuki (character:tsu-miko-yuki) who she suspects has the spirit-sight needed for the work.
fears_or_limits: As the network weakens, she is losing her power and her human form — soon she won't be able to maintain the shrine at all.
Tamamo (character:tamamo) is actively working to destroy the network, and Katsura may not be strong enough to stop her alone.

entries.name: Yukina
entries.gm_notes: Yukina is a yuki-onna — a snow woman — who fell in love with a human woodcutter and married him, suppressing her nature to live as a mortal wife. He doesn't know what she is. Each winter, her power grows stronger as the cold deepens, and the urge to let the frost take over becomes harder to resist. Last winter, she froze the bedroom door shut in her sleep, and her husband nearly lost his fingers opening it. She told him it was a faulty latch. She's afraid that one winter she'll kill him without meaning to — the cold inside her is not something she fully controls. She's been considering asking the shrine for help, but revealing herself would mean exile — or worse.

payload.summary: A quiet, beautiful woman in a mountain village in Tsukuyomi, married to the local woodcutter. She keeps the house cold even in summer, which her husband finds strange but endearing. She rarely touches anyone skin-to-skin.
payload.appearance: She wears layered kimono even in warm weather, pale blues and whites that match her complexion. She moves without sound and her breath doesn't fog in winter air. She is strikingly beautiful in a way that makes people uneasy, though they can't say why.

visual_identity.hair: white, long, straight
visual_identity.distinctive_features: skin that is perpetually cool-pale, as if touched by frost; lips with a faint blue tint

desires: To live peacefully with her husband and resist the killing cold that grows stronger each winter.
To find a way to become fully human so she can touch him without fear.
fears_or_limits: She is losing control of her nature as the years pass — the cold is getting harder to suppress.
If her husband or the village discovers she is a yokai, she will lose everything — and the shrine network would see her sealed.

entries.name: Hana
entries.gm_notes: Hana carries messages between the capital and the provinces and has been secretly reading them for years. She knows about Takeda's (character:daimyo-takeda) coalition, the shogun's (character:shogun-ashikara) illness, and the shrine network's decline — she's assembled a fuller picture than anyone except perhaps the archivist Shiori (character:tsu-shiori-librarian). She's been selling fragments of this information to multiple parties — Takeda, the shogunate's intelligence network, and an unknown third buyer who pays in gold and asks very specific questions about the shrine network. She doesn't know who the third buyer is, and that terrifies her. She's in too deep to stop and too deep to run.

payload.summary: A fleet-footed messenger who runs the Cedar Road between the capital and the provinces. She carries sealed scrolls and wears a route marker's sash. She knows every shortcut, every rest house, and every checkpoint guard by name.
payload.appearance: She wears a lightweight traveling kimono with tight sleeves and straw sandals, a courier's pack strapped to her back. She's lean from running and always slightly out of breath when she stops. She carries a knife in her sash that she knows how to use.

visual_identity.hair: black, cut short to the jaw for speed
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a road-dust tan line at the wrists from long sleeves worn while running

desires: To identify her anonymous gold-paying buyer before they decide she knows too much.
To save enough money to leave Tsukuyomi entirely and start over somewhere no one knows her face.
fears_or_limits: Every party she sells to could have her killed if they learn she's selling to the others too.
The anonymous buyer's questions about the shrine network suggest a plan she doesn't understand — and ignorance is not safety.

entries.name: Ume
entries.gm_notes: Ume tends the shogunate's stable and has noticed that the elder prince's (character:tsu-prince-ren) horse has been given something in its feed — a charm or potion that makes the animal skittish and aggressive. She suspects someone is trying to get the prince thrown from his horse, but she doesn't know who or why. She's been quietly swapping the tampered feed for clean feed when she can, but the tampered batch keeps reappearing. She reported it to the stable master, who told her to mind her own business. She's considering telling the guard captain Daichi (character:tsu-dai-guard-captain) directly, but she's only a stable hand and he outranks her by twenty degrees.

payload.summary: A stable hand in the shogunate's palace stables who knows every horse by name and temperament. She mucks stalls, mixes feed, and reads the animals' moods better than most people read faces. She's noticed something wrong with one of the prince's horses.
payload.appearance: She wears rough work clothes and high wooden clogs to keep out of the muck, her hair tied in a cloth. She smells of hay and horse, and she talks to the animals in a low, constant murmur. Her hands are calloused and she's stronger than she looks.

visual_identity.hair: black, tied under a cloth cap
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a crooked nose from being kicked by a horse at fourteen

desires: To protect the elder prince's horse and figure out who is tampering with its feed.
To be taken seriously by someone with the authority to investigate.
fears_or_limits: She's a stable hand — her word carries no weight against a stable master's dismissal.
If whoever is tampering with the feed learns she's been swapping it, she could be the next target.

entries.name: Rui
entries.gm_notes: Rui runs a gambling den in the capital that is a front for an information-brokering network — she doesn't gamble for money, she gambles for secrets. Last month, she won a bet that gave her knowledge of a hidden vault beneath the shogun's palace, sealed by shrine wards, containing artifacts from the original human-yokai pact. She's been planning a break-in, but the cat-folk thief Kuro (character:kuro) has been spotted near the same vault by her informants. She doesn't know if he's after the same thing or if he's been sent by someone else. She's been trying to make contact with him, but he's gone to ground — Takeda's agents are hunting him.

payload.summary: The proprietor of the Fox Dice gambling parlor in the capital's entertainment district. She deals cards with elegant hands and never loses her composure. The parlor is always full, the sake is always flowing, and the stakes are never just money.
payload.role: Gambling den owner and information broker
payload.appearance: She wears a dramatic kimono in deep purples and blacks, a fan always in hand. She sits at the head of the room where she can see every table. She smiles when she's winning and smiles wider when she's about to fold — both look the same, which is the point.

visual_identity.hair: black, long, styled with gambling chips as hairpins
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a tiny fox tattoo behind the right ear — the mark of her network

desires: To crack the hidden vault beneath the palace and claim whatever the original pact left behind.
To find Kuro (character:kuro) before Takeda's agents do and learn what he knows about the vault.
fears_or_limits: Breaking into a shrine-warded vault in the shogun's palace is a capital offense — and she doesn't know how to breach the wards.
If Takeda's agents catch her near Kuro, they'll assume she's involved with whatever he stole.

entries.name: Tomi
entries.gm_notes: Tomi serves in Daimyo Takeda's (character:daimyo-takeda) household as a personal attendant and reports to him on his retainers' loyalty and conversations. But she is also secretly reporting Takeda's plans to the shogunate's intelligence service, because her family lives in the capital and Takeda's coalition, if it succeeds, would put them in danger. She's playing both sides — giving Takeda enough genuine intelligence to stay valuable while feeding the shogunate enough to stay protected. The arrangement is unsustainable. She knows that Takeda's retainer Honoka (character:tsu-kaede-honoka) has been distracted and suspects why, but she hasn't reported it to Takeda — a small act of mercy that could cost her everything if discovered.

payload.summary: A personal servant in Daimyo Takeda's capital residence, attentive and unobtrusive. She serves tea, manages household supplies, and seems to exist in the background of every important conversation. She has a remarkable memory for who said what to whom.
payload.appearance: She wears a plain servant's kimono in muted grey, her hair in a simple bun. She moves through rooms like a shadow — present, useful, and invisible. She pours tea at precisely the right moment and never interrupts.

visual_identity.hair: black, plain bun
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a small mole at the corner of the left eye

desires: To keep her family in the capital safe by feeding the shogunate enough intelligence to counter Takeda's plans.
To find a way out of the double life before one side or the other discovers her.
fears_or_limits: If Takeda discovers she's a double agent, her death will be slow and exemplary.
If the shogunate falls, her family has no protection and she has no value to anyone.

entries.name: Kazue
entries.gm_notes: Kazue forges blades using an alloy that includes yokai-silver — a material that makes weapons capable of cutting spirits and yokai, not just flesh. She learned the technique from her master, who was executed by shrine authorities for 'consorting with yokai' when she was his apprentice. She's been hiding the nature of her blades, selling them as ordinary quality steel. Daimyo Takeda (character:daimyo-takeda) has been buying her blades in bulk through intermediaries, and she suspects he's building an arsenal specifically for use against yokai — possibly to engineer an incident that proves the shrine network's weakness. She's torn: the blades are her living, but their use could trigger a catastrophe.

payload.summary: A blacksmith in rural Tsukuyomi whose blades hold an edge longer than any forge in the capital can explain. She works a bellows-driven forge in a village that smells of charcoal and iron. She's been a smith since she was twelve and takes no apprentices.
payload.appearance: She wears a leather smith's apron over a soot-stained kimono, her sleeves bound tight. She's broad-shouldered from years at the anvil, and she wields a hammer with controlled, rhythmic force. Her forge-glow is always behind her, outlining her in red and shadow.

visual_identity.hair: black, greying, cropped very short
visual_identity.distinctive_features: burn scars across both forearms and a permanent forge-tan on the hands

desires: To keep her master's technique alive and honor his memory without being arrested for it.
To stop Takeda from using her blades to trigger the yokai incident she fears he's planning.
fears_or_limits: Yokai-silver weapons are contraband under shogunate law — possessing the technique is a crime.
She cannot refuse a daimyo's orders without consequences, and she has no political protection.

entries.name: Natsuko
entries.gm_notes: Natsuko's farm sits on a ley line that feeds the local shrine network — the crops grow twice as fast as they should, and the soil never depletes. A Takeda agent (working for character:daimyo-takeda) has been pressing her to sell the land for a 'fortification project.' She doesn't want to sell her family's land, but she also doesn't know that the ley line beneath it is what powers the nearest shrine's wards. If she sells and Takeda builds on it, the wards will collapse, opening a gap in the network. She's been stalling with increasingly desperate excuses while trying to reach her son in the capital for help.

payload.summary: A weathered farmer in rural Tsukuyomi whose fields produce impossibly abundant harvests. She works from before dawn to after dusk, her hands always in the earth. She feeds her village and asks little in return, but she's worried about a land agent who won't take no for an answer.
payload.appearance: She wears a conical straw hat, a patched kimono with the sleeves tied back, and straw sandals caked with mud. She carries a hoe over one shoulder and a basket of early vegetables on the other. Her face is sun-darkened and open.

visual_identity.body_build: wiry, bent from years of field work
visual_identity.hair: iron grey, under a straw hat
visual_identity.eyes: dark brown, deeply lined at the corners
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a permanent soil-dark crease across both palms

desires: To keep her family's land and the farm that has sustained her village for generations.
To get word to her son in the capital before the land agent forces the issue.
fears_or_limits: She is one woman with no legal training against a daimyo's agents who have the authority to complicate her title.
She doesn't know why her land is special, which means she can't make the right argument to protect it.

entries.name: Mai
entries.gm_notes: Mai's dances are unknowingly ritual movements that can temporarily strengthen shrine wards — she inherited the forms from her mother, who was a shrine dancer before the family fell on hard times. Mai thinks she's simply a performer, but a shrine maiden — Katsura (character:tsu-katsura-kitsune) — has been attending her performances and noticed the wards in the district flicker stronger when she dances. Someone has been leaving anonymous gifts at her dressing room with notes asking her to dance at specific shrines. Someone else has been leaving threats telling her to stop dancing entirely. She doesn't understand why a dancer would be this important to anyone.

payload.summary: A dancer in the capital's entertainment district who performs traditional shrine dances adapted for the stage. She moves with a grace that silences rooms, and her performances draw crowds even on rainy nights. She is modest about her talent and puzzled by her growing fame.
payload.appearance: She wears a performing kimono in flowing layers of cherry-blossom pink and white, a fan in each hand. She dances barefoot on the wooden stage, her hair ornamented with seasonal flowers. Her movements are precise and ancient in a way her audiences feel but can't name.

visual_identity.hair: black, long, worn in an elaborate dance style with floral kanzashi
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a spray of pale freckles across the bridge of the nose, unusual for the region

desires: To understand why her dancing draws such intense attention from strangers who won't explain themselves.
To dance freely without being controlled by whoever is leaving the gifts and threats.
fears_or_limits: She has no idea that her dancing has spiritual power, which means she can't protect herself from those who do.
The threats are escalating, and she has no combat skills and no protector.

entries.name: Rei
entries.gm_notes: Rei is one of the shogun's (character:shogun-ashikara) personal guard and knows he is dying. She's overheard him discussing the heir problem with his physician and has been secretly training the younger prince Haru (character:tsu-prince-haru) in swordsmanship after hours — a serious violation of protocol that could end her career. She believes the elder prince (character:tsu-prince-ren) would be a disaster for the shogunate and is prepared to support a coup if the elder is named heir. She's been quietly testing the loyalty of other guards, building a small faction that would support the younger prince. She doesn't know the elder prince's cruelty is being amplified by an inhabited mask (character:tsu-mei-maskmaker).

payload.summary: A guard in the shogun's personal retinue, one of the few women in the palace guard. She stands watch at the shogun's chambers with a yari spear and an expression that discourages conversation. She is loyal to the shogunate, not to any individual — a distinction she's finding increasingly painful.
payload.appearance: She wears the dark lacquered armor of the shogun's guard, her yari resting at attention beside her. Her hair is cropped short under a helmet. She stands perfectly still for hours at a time and notices everything that moves in her peripheral vision.

visual_identity.hair: black, cropped short under helm
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a thin scar across the jawline from a training accident

desires: To ensure the younger prince is prepared to lead if the elder proves unfit.
To protect the shogunate she's sworn to serve, even if that means breaking the rules she's sworn to follow.
fears_or_limits: Training the prince in secret is treason if discovered — she would be executed.
She is building a faction within the guard, and if she's wrong about the elder prince, she's the one starting a coup.

entries.name: Kayo
entries.gm_notes: Kayo is a rokurokubi — a yokai whose neck extends grotesquely at night while she sleeps. By day she is a normal woman, a weaver in Haru's Shrine Town, kind and unremarkable. At night, her sleeping body sends her head and neck wandering through the town, seeing and hearing things from impossible vantage points. She's seen someone — she can't tell who, they wore a hood — entering the old shrine site behind Hanako's (character:hanako) tea house at night and handling the old bell. She's terrified of being discovered as a yokai, but she's more terrified of whoever is tampering with the shrine site. She's been leaving anonymous notes for the shrine maiden Katsura (character:tsu-katsura-kitsune).

payload.summary: A weaver in Haru's Shrine Town, quiet and kind, who keeps to herself and works at her loom from dawn to dusk. She is unremarkable in every visible way, which is exactly how she wants to remain. She sleeps with a cloth wrapped around her neck.
payload.role: Rokurokubi (long-neck yokai) in hiding as a weaver
payload.appearance: She wears a plain work kimono in undyed linen, her hair in a simple braid. She sits at her loom with slightly hunched shoulders, as if trying to take up less space. She has dark circles under her eyes from poor sleep and an air of someone keeping a very large secret.

visual_identity.hair: black, thin, braided
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a faint red line around the neck like a crease, usually hidden by a cloth

desires: To warn the shrine about whoever is tampering with the old bell without revealing her yokai nature.
To find a way to sleep safely — to stop the nightly wandering that terrifies her and risks exposure.
fears_or_limits: If the shrine discovers she is a rokurokubi, she will be sealed or driven out — and the shrine network's wards make hiding harder, not easier.
She saw something at the shrine site she wasn't meant to see, and someone may have seen her neck.

entries.name: Suzume
entries.gm_notes: Suzume is the younger sister of the wandering swordmaster Soji (character:tengu-soji), who left the tengu mountain dojo over a dispute about whether to intervene in the shrine network's decline. She followed him into exile against the elders' explicit orders — a grave act for a tengu. But she disagrees with Soji's approach: he wants to find a human champion to help from the outside, while she wants to go back and argue the elders into action from the inside. She's been secretly corresponding with the elder tengu through a series of coded messages left at wayshrines along the Cedar Road, trying to negotiate a path home for both of them. Soji doesn't know about the correspondence.

payload.summary: A tengu woman traveling the Cedar Road in human disguise, carrying a naginata and a travel pack. She is sharper-tongued than her brother and less patient with human customs. She perches on high things when she thinks no one is watching.
payload.appearance: She wears traveling clothes in dark forest colors, a cloth wrapping her head to hide the feathers that grow along her temples. Her naginata is wrapped in cloth to look like a walking stick. She watches the sky too much and the ground too little.

visual_identity.hair: black, with iridescent feathers growing along the hairline at the temples
visual_identity.distinctive_features: feathers along the temples (hidden by a head wrap) and slightly talon-like nails

desires: To negotiate a return to the tengu community for herself and Soji by convincing the elders to intervene in the shrine network.
To protect Soji from the consequences of his exile, which she believes are more severe than he lets on.
fears_or_limits: If Soji learns she's been corresponding with the elders he defied, he may see it as betrayal.
The elders' silence in response to her messages may mean they've already decided to let the network fall — and her with it.

entries.name: Prince Ashikara Haru
entries.gm_notes: Haru knows his father the shogun (character:shogun-ashikara) is dying — he's seen the medicine bottles and the physician's face. He doesn't want the throne but sees that his elder brother (character:tsu-prince-ren) would destroy the shogunate.
