He's been secretly studying governance with the tea teacher Satsuki (character:tsu-satsuki-tea-teacher) and swordsmanship with the guard Rei (character:tsu-rei-guard), both against palace protocol. He's been having recurring nightmares about a fox with many tails whispering that the old promises are breaking. He doesn't know it's connected to the shrine network, but the dreams feel real. He has also been receiving messages encoded in flower arrangements left in his study — Rin (character:tsu-rin-florist) is trying to warn him about something.

payload.summary: The younger son of the Shogun, seventeen years old, known for his kindness and his reluctance to compete with his elder brother. He spends his time in the palace gardens and the archives rather than the training grounds. He is polite to everyone and trusted by the servants, which is itself a kind of power.
payload.appearance: He wears a youth's court kimono in pale blue, well-kept but not ostentatious. He carries a wakizashi he's barely trained to use. His posture is open and unguarded in a way that makes his guard detail nervous. He reads scrolls while walking, which is why he trips on doorframes.

visual_identity.hair: black, in a young man's topknot
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a faint childhood scar on the chin from falling out of a persimmon tree

desires: To find a way to save the shogunate without taking the throne by force or watching his brother destroy it.
To understand his recurring fox dreams and whether they're a warning.
fears_or_limits: He is untested and knows it — every decision he makes could be the wrong one, and the stakes are the entire nation.
His elder brother is stronger, more experienced, and more ruthless, and Haru cannot bring himself to fight family.

entries.name: Prince Ashikara Renjiro
entries.gm_notes: The elder prince was not always cruel. Before the Noh mask made by Mei (character:tsu-mei-maskmaker) was given to him as a court gift two years ago, he was sharp, ambitious, but fundamentally fair — a stern man, not a vicious one. The spirit housed in the mask has been amplifying his worst impulses: paranoia, contempt, aggression. He's been having gaps in his memory during council meetings, where the mask's influence is strongest. A part of him is aware something is wrong — he's noticed his own behavior changing and it frightens him — but he can't identify the source. He hasn't removed the mask in public since he received it, and the spirit has made him afraid to take it off.

payload.summary: The elder son of the Shogun, a man in his mid-twenties known for his competence in administration and his growing cruelty toward subordinates. He wears a Noh mask at all public functions — a practice he began two years ago that everyone attributes to eccentricity. He speaks precisely and never raises his voice, which makes his words cut deeper.
payload.role: Elder prince of the Ashikara shogunate
payload.appearance: He wears formal court attire in dark colors and a white Noh mask that depicts a handsome, severe face. His movements are controlled and deliberate. He holds himself like a man who has never been contradicted and expects he never will be.

visual_identity.hair: black, in a formal topknot
visual_identity.eyes: dark brown — visible only without the mask, which is rare
visual_identity.distinctive_features: always wears a white Noh mask in public; the mask's expression seems to shift subtly when observed

desires: To secure his succession and prove he is worthy of the shogunate his father built.
To understand what is happening to him — the memory gaps and the urges that don't feel like his own.
fears_or_limits: He is being influenced by a force he cannot see or identify, and the influence is growing.
A part of him knows his cruelty is wrong, but the mask makes that part quieter every day.

entries.name: Jinichi
entries.gm_notes: Jinichi was a samurai who killed a child during a raid on a rebel village fifteen years ago. The horror of what he'd done drove him to renounce violence and become a monk at a mountain temple in Tsukuyomi. He has lived in peace since — until the shrine network's decline allowed violent spirits to creep into the area around his temple. Three weeks ago, a bakeneko (monster cat) attacked a pilgrim on the temple road, and Jinichi killed it with his bare hands to save the man. The violence felt natural and good, and that terrifies him more than the yokai did. He's been having dreams about the child he killed, and the dreams are changing — the child is smiling at him now, and he doesn't know if that's forgiveness or something else.

payload.summary: A Buddhist monk at a small mountain temple in Tsukuyomi, known for his gentleness and the way he feeds the wild birds from his hand. He tends the temple garden and sweeps the steps. He is large for a monk and moves with a fighter's economy that he tries to hide.
payload.appearance: He wears saffron robes that are faded from washing, a prayer bead bracelet on one wrist. He's bigger than most monks — broad-shouldered, with hands that are calloused in ways that have nothing to do with gardening. He bows to everyone and avoids eye contact.

visual_identity.hair: shaved
visual_identity.distinctive_features: old weapons-callus scarring on both hands, partially faded

desires: To protect his temple and the pilgrims who come to it without returning to the violence he renounced.
To understand whether the dreams of the child he killed are offering forgiveness or demanding something.
fears_or_limits: The violence he buried is waking up, and each time he uses it, it feels more natural — which is exactly what he's afraid of.
The shrine network's decline means more violent yokai are coming, and his temple sits on a mountain road with no shrine ward at all.

entries.name: Taro
entries.gm_notes: Taro knows about Iso's (character:tsu-iso-fishwife) deal with the umi-bozu because he's the one who introduced her to it — he made the same bargain twenty years ago. The yokai gives him abundant catches in exchange for his service at the hidden coastal shrine every new moon. But Taro is aging, and the yokai wants a successor — it's been demanding that Taro recruit a replacement or forfeit his own catch. He introduced Iso to the bargain partly out of desperation, partly because the yokai told him to. He's wracked with guilt about what he's done to her and her husband, but he's also terrified of what the umi-bozu will do if he refuses. He's been leaving offerings at a proper shrine in secret, praying for a way out that doesn't exist.

payload.summary: An aging fisherman in a coastal village in Tsukuyomi, known for bringing in the largest catches year after year. He works the pre-dawn boats alone and returns with holds that shouldn't be possible for a single man. He drinks more than he used to and doesn't look people in the eye.
payload.appearance: He wears a salt-stained work kimono with rubber-soled boots, a fishing knife at his belt. His skin is weathered dark from decades of sea wind, and he squints from permanently salt-reddened eyes. He smells of fish and cheap sake, and his hands shake when he's not holding something.

visual_identity.hair: grey, thin, under a knit cap
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a rope-scar around the right wrist and a permanently crooked left ring finger from a net accident

desires: To find a way out of his bargain with the umi-bozu before it forces him to recruit more people.
To make amends to Iso (character:tsu-iso-fishwife) for what he dragged her into, if amends are even possible.
fears_or_limits: The umi-bozu will not release him, and refusing its demands means losing his livelihood — or worse.
If Iso learns he introduced her to the bargain on the yokai's orders, she may never forgive him — or she may kill him.

entries.name: Goro
entries.gm_notes: Goro has been smuggling shrine artifacts out of decommissioned shrines and selling them to collectors in foreign provinces. He doesn't realize these artifacts — bells, ofuda, stone guardians — are still connected to the shrine network's ley lines. Removing them creates gaps in the ward coverage, like pulling stones from a wall. He's created at least three unprotected zones in rural Tsukuyomi without knowing it, and wild yokai have been entering through those gaps. He's been buying pottery from Tsubaki (character:tsu-tsubaki-potter) and has been pressing to see her kiln — partly for profit, partly because he's noticed the pottery has spiritual properties he could exploit. He's the kind of man who sees power and thinks only of its price.

payload.summary: A traveling merchant who deals in 'curiosities' — shrine relics, antique pottery, old scrolls, and anything with a story attached. He works the roads between the capital and the provinces in a cart loaded with crates. He is cheerful, generous with samples, and asks a lot of questions.
payload.appearance: He wears a road-worn kimono in browns and oranges, a fan tucked in his sash, and a merchant's cap. His cart creaks under the weight of curiosities wrapped in straw. He bows too deeply and laughs too readily, and his eyes calculate while his mouth smiles.

visual_identity.hair: black, receding, in a merchant's topknot
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a chipped front tooth and a persistent ink stain on the right cheek from resting a brush there

desires: To find and sell the most valuable spiritual artifacts in Tsukuyomi before someone else beats him to them.
To get access to Tsubaki's (character:tsu-tsubaki-potter) mysterious kiln, whatever it takes.
fears_or_limits: Smuggling shrine artifacts is a crime, and the penalties are severe if he's caught with the wrong item.
He doesn't understand what the artifacts actually do, which means he's creating dangers he can't see or defend against.

entries.name: Sho
entries.gm_notes: Sho discovered Saya's (character:tsu-saya-brewer) secret spring beneath the old shrine site and has been taking water from it for his own experiments after hours. He's accidentally created a sake that attracts yokai — the spirit-charged water, fermented without the purification rituals Saya performs, draws minor spirits like moths to flame. He got drunk on it three nights ago and woke in the brewery surrounded by small fox spirits who were drinking from the vats. He's terrified, but also fascinated — the foxes were friendly, and one of them spoke to him. He's been making more of the yokai-sake in secret, telling himself it's research. He doesn't know that wild yokai attracted by his brew could be drawing attention to the town and the weakening shrine.

payload.summary: A young apprentice to the sake brewer Saya in Haru's Shrine Town, eager and slightly reckless. He arrives before his master and leaves after her, driven by curiosity about everything she won't explain. He has a bright smile and a talent for finding trouble.
payload.appearance: He wears a brewery apron over a plain kimono, sleeves rolled to the elbows. He's lean and energetic, always doing something with his hands. He smells of koji and river water, and he grins when he's caught doing something he shouldn't.

visual_identity.hair: black, messy, escaping a topknot
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a sake-yeast rash along the jawline that comes and goes

desires: To understand why the spring water makes Saya's sake special and prove he can brew something equally remarkable.
To learn more about the fox spirits that visited him — he wants to see them again.
fears_or_limits: Saya would expel him instantly if she knew he was using the spring water unsupervised.
The yokai-sake he's brewing is attracting spirits to a town with weakening shrine wards — he's creating a danger he doesn't understand.

entries.name: Akira
entries.gm_notes: Akira has been tutoring both princes for five years and has been quietly playing them against each other to ensure whoever takes the throne owes him. He feeds the younger prince Haru (character:tsu-prince-haru) practical knowledge about governance while telling the elder prince Ren (character:tsu-prince-ren) what he wants to hear. He has a network of former students in key positions throughout the shogunate — clerks, guards, minor officials — who report to him. He doesn't want power directly; he wants to be the man behind whoever has it. He doesn't know about the mask influencing the elder prince, but he's noticed the behavioral change and is trying to determine whether it's an opportunity or a threat to his plans.

payload.summary: A scholar and tutor in the capital who has educated the shogunate's heirs for years. He is erudite, soft-spoken, and respected by the court. He maintains a modest study full of scrolls and receives visitors over tea, always listening more than he speaks.
payload.appearance: He wears a scholar's kimono in dark blue, a reading brush tucked in his sash. His study is piled with scrolls and annotated texts. He speaks slowly and precisely, weighing each word, and he has a habit of answering a question with a question that reshapes the conversation.

visual_identity.hair: grey, in a scholar's topknot
visual_identity.distinctive_features: deep lines bracketing the mouth from a lifetime of careful expressions

desires: To be the indispensable advisor to whichever prince takes the throne — and to ensure it's the one more likely to listen to him.
To maintain his network of former students in positions of influence throughout the shogunate.
fears_or_limits: If either prince discovers he's been playing both sides, his career and his network are destroyed.
He doesn't understand the spiritual dimension of what's happening in the palace — the mask, the shrine network, the yokai — and his plans don't account for forces he can't tutor.

entries.name: Kenta
entries.gm_notes: Kenta is Chiyo's (character:tsu-chiyo-child) best friend and the only person who believes her about seeing spirits. He's been helping her feed the kitsune cub in the shrine grove. Three days ago, he found an old ofuda — a spirit ward — half-buried in the ruins near the shrine and has been carrying it in his shirt as a lucky charm. He doesn't know it's a genuine, powerful ward that's been protecting them both from the shadow-creature that Obaba Kiku (character:tsu-baba-storyteller) has been warning about — the same thing Chiyo calls the 'tall shadow with too many eyes.' The ward's power is fading, and when it goes, whatever it's been holding back will notice the two children who've been visiting the sealed stone.

payload.summary: A boy of twelve in Haru's Shrine Town, practical and protective of his younger friend Chiyo. He carries a school satchel and a slingshot and takes his self-appointed role as Chiyo's guardian very seriously. He doesn't believe in ghosts — he just believes in Chiyo.
payload.appearance: He wears a plain boy's kimono with a cloth satchel slung across one shoulder. He has scrapes on his knees from climbing and a slingshot tucked in his sash. He walks with the squared shoulders of someone trying to look older than he is.

visual_identity.hair: black, cropped short
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a chipped left canine tooth

desires: To protect Chiyo from the things she sees — even if he can't see them himself.
To figure out what the old paper charm he found actually does, and whether it can keep them safe.
fears_or_limits: He's a child with a slingshot — whatever Chiyo describes as the 'tall shadow' is beyond anything he can fight.
The ofuda he carries is losing its power, and he has no idea that his protection is expiring.

entries.name: Jiro
entries.gm_notes: Jiro was the shogun's bodyguard thirty years ago and carries a secret that could shatter the Ashikara line: the current shogun (character:shogun-ashikara) is not the original heir. The true heir was a sickly child who was secretly swapped with a healthier cousin from a branch family to prevent a succession crisis during a yokai plague. The swap was ordered by the previous shogun and carried out by Jiro and the court physician, both now dead. The current shogun knows the truth — Jiro told him on his deathbed-equivalent twenty years ago — and it's part of why he agonizes over the succession. Jiro is the only other living person who knows, and he's dying of old age. He's been writing a letter he can't decide whether to send.

payload.summary: A retired samurai living in a small house in rural Tsukuyomi, tending a vegetable garden and dozing in the sun. He walks with a cane and tells stories about his soldiering days that everyone assumes are exaggerated. He keeps to himself and watches the road with habits that never left him.
payload.appearance: He wears a faded kimono and a straw hat, a cane beside his garden bench. He's thinner than he was, but his posture still carries the memory of armor. His hands rest on his knees in a way that suggests he knows where every weapon in the room is.

visual_identity.hair: white, sparse, under a cap
visual_identity.distinctive_features: an old sword scar across the collarbone and a missing left little finger — the mark of a past dishonor atonement

desires: To decide whether to reveal the succession secret before he dies, or take it to his grave as he promised.
To see the shogunate survive, regardless of whose blood sits on the throne.
fears_or_limits: Revealing the secret could destabilize the shogunate more than the succession crisis itself.
He is dying and running out of time to decide — and a letter, once sent, cannot be unsent.

entries.name: Daichi
entries.gm_notes: Daichi commands the shogun's palace guard and has been receiving written orders from the elder prince (character:tsu-prince-ren) to increase security around the shogun's private chambers — restricting access to all visitors, including the younger prince Haru (character:tsu-prince-haru). Daichi believes these orders come from filial concern for the ailing shogun. He's beginning to suspect something is wrong — the younger prince has been turned away three times, and the elder prince's tone in the orders has shifted from concerned to commanding. But Daichi's loyalty to the chain of command is absolute, and questioning a prince's orders is unthinkable. The stable hand Ume (character:tsu-ume-stable) tried to report something to him last week, and he dismissed her — a decision that's starting to trouble him.

payload.summary: The captain of the shogun's palace guard, a career soldier who has served three generations of the Ashikara household. He is disciplined, blunt, and trusted by the guard. He runs the palace security with a precision that leaves no gap — which is exactly why someone has been using his own protocols against him.
payload.appearance: He wears full guard captain's armor with the Ashikara crest, a katana at his side. He is solid and immovable, with the bearing of a man who has stood in one place watching doors for thirty years. He inspects his guards personally and remembers every face.

visual_identity.hair: grey, in a tight topknot
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a deep scar across the bridge of the nose and a cauliflower right ear from years of armor helm pressure

desires: To serve the shogunate faithfully and ensure the succession proceeds without violence.
To understand why the elder prince's orders feel wrong before it's too late to do anything about it.
fears_or_limits: His absolute loyalty to chain of command prevents him from questioning orders, even orders that trouble him.
He dismissed Ume's report about the horse tampering, and if she was right, his inaction may have consequences.

entries.name: Goki
entries.gm_notes: Goki is an oni — a demon of mountain and rage — who was sealed by a shrine maiden 200 years ago in a cave in the Tsukuyomi mountains. The shrine maiden who bound him was the first human to show him kindness; she spoke to him through the seal for years, and that contact changed him fundamentally. When the shrine network's weakening cracked his seal last winter, he emerged into a world he doesn't recognize — but with a spirit that has been gentled by two centuries of one person's kindness. He's been living as a hermit, suppressing the violent nature that is fundamental to what he is. He knows that when the network falls fully, the seals on other, much worse oni will crack too — oni who never had a shrine maiden to talk to. He's been trying to warn someone, but he's a demon, and no one trusts a demon.

payload.summary: A large, quiet figure who lives alone in a cave in the Tsukuyomi mountains, occasionally helping lost travelers find the road before disappearing back into the trees. He is built like a boulder and moves with surprising gentleness. Villagers tell stories about a helpful mountain spirit; they don't know he's an oni.
payload.appearance: He wears rough homespun clothes far too small for his frame, his skin a deep iron-grey. He keeps a woven hat low over his face and his hands hidden when he can. He hunches to seem smaller than he is, and he speaks in a low rumble that he tries to make gentle.

visual_identity.age: ancient — appears mid-forties in human terms
visual_identity.hair: black, coarse, wild
visual_identity.eyes: amber, single-horn protruding from the forehead (usually hidden under a hat)
visual_identity.distinctive_features: iron-grey skin, a single oni horn at the brow, tusks visible when he speaks

desires: To warn someone — anyone — about the sealed oni beneath the mountain whose bonds are cracking.
To honor the memory of the shrine maiden who gentled him by protecting humans, even though it goes against every instinct of what he is.
fears_or_limits: He is an oni — his nature is violence, and suppression is not the same as absence; one day the rage may win.
No one will listen to a demon's warning, and the sealed oni beneath the mountain are far worse than he ever was.

entries.name: Danzaburo
entries.gm_notes: Danzaburo is a tanuki — a raccoon dog spirit — who has run a noodle shop in Haru's Shrine Town for forty years in the guise of a jolly old man. His noodles are enchanted: they make people happy and generous, which has been quietly sustaining the town's mood through hard times. He knows the shrine kitsune Katsura (character:tsu-katsura-kitsune) is losing her power, and he's been secretly directing the happy energy from his enchanted noodles toward the shrine to help her maintain the local wards — a tanuki helping a kitsune, which would scandalize both their kinds if they knew. He's also been quietly feeding the kitsune cub that Chiyo (character:tsu-chiyo-child) visits, making sure it stays healthy and small rather than growing into something dangerous. He's aging, and tanuki magic fades with age — he doesn't know how much longer he can keep it up.

payload.summary: A round, jolly old man who runs a noodle shop in Haru's Shrine Town, famous for portions that are always generous and broth that makes people smile. He chats with every customer, remembers every name, and has been a fixture of the town for as long as anyone can remember. He is exactly what he appears to be — except that he isn't.
payload.role: Tanuki (raccoon dog spirit) in disguise as a noodle shop owner
payload.appearance: He wears a noodle vendor's apron over a comfortable kimono, a towel around his neck. He is round-bellied and perpetually cheerful, stirring broth with a ladle he handles like a baton. He laughs from the belly and tops off bowls without being asked. In certain light, his shadow is rounder and lower than it should be.

visual_identity.hair: grey, thinning, under a rolled towel
visual_identity.eyes: dark brown, crinkled with permanent amusement
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a broad, flat nose and a leaf-shaped birthmark behind the right ear (hidden)

desires: To sustain the town's spirit and the shrine's wards as long as his magic holds out.
To protect the kitsune cub and the children who visit it from growing into something neither side can control.
fears_or_limits: His tanuki magic is fading with age, and when it goes, his enchantments — the happy noodles, the ward assistance — will fail.
If anyone discovers he is a tanuki running a food establishment, the shrine authorities would seal him, and the town would lose its quiet guardian.

entries.name: Ryo
entries.gm_notes: Ryo makes paper lanterns using fragments of old ofuda — spirit wards that were supposed to be ritually destroyed when their shrines were decommissioned. He's been rescuing them from demolition sites and weaving the paper into his lanterns. His lanterns create small warded zones wherever they hang — a merchant's stall with a Ryo lantern is subtly protected from yokai intrusion. He's accidentally created a patchwork of mini-wards throughout the merchant district of the capital, which has been keeping wild yokai out of the area far more effectively than the official shrine network. The shrine authorities don't know what he's doing, but they've noticed the anomaly — the merchant district has unusually low yokai activity, and they're sending an investigator. If they discover his lanterns contain unauthorized ofuda, he'll be arrested and the mini-wards will collapse.

payload.summary: A lantern maker in the capital's merchant district whose paper lanterns hang in shops, teahouses, and market stalls throughout the area. He works in a small shop full of bamboo frames and colored paper, and he delivers his lanterns personally. Shop owners say their businesses feel safer with his lanterns, though they can't explain why.
payload.appearance: He wears a craftsman's apron over a simple kimono, his hands nimble with bamboo and paper. He works surrounded by half-finished lantern frames in every color. He is quiet, meticulous, and has a habit of checking where his lanterns are hung when he walks the market street at night.

visual_identity.hair: black, in a simple topknot
visual_identity.distinctive_features: paper-cut calluses on both thumbs and a faint glue stain on the left forearm

desires: To protect the merchant district from yokai through his craft, one lantern at a time.
To stay ahead of the shrine investigator who's asking why the district has unusually low spirit activity.
fears_or_limits: Using decommissioned ofuda in craftwork is a shogunate crime — unauthorized manipulation of shrine materials.
If his lanterns are confiscated, the mini-ward network collapses and the merchant district becomes vulnerable overnight.

entries.name: Lyria Ironheart
entries.gm_notes: Secretly the illegitimate daughter of the late King Aldric and a blacksmith's daughter. Her birth was hidden to protect the succession line. A sealed letter from her mother, only to be opened upon the queen's death, proves her royal blood. If revealed, she could destabilize the entire succession crisis — or resolve it. She does not yet know the full truth, only that her mother whispered 'you have your father's hands' on her deathbed. The sealed letter sits in a lockbox beneath the forge.

payload.summary: A brooding blacksmith's apprentice whose hammer strikes ring with unnatural precision, haunted by a lineage she cannot yet name.
payload.appearance: Broad-shouldered and soot-stained, with calloused hands and a permanent burn scar curling up her left forearm. She wears a leather apron over simple linen, her dark hair tied back with iron wire.

visual_identity.hair: dark brown, thick, worn tied back
visual_identity.distinctive_features: burn scar on left forearm, exceptionally large and calloused hands for her frame

desires: to forge a blade worthy of legend, something that will outlast her
to learn the identity of her true father
fears_or_limits: that she is unworthy of whatever blood runs in her veins
that the forge fire will one day take more than her forearm

entries.name: Sera Thornwick
entries.gm_notes: Sera was the secret lover of Prince Edran, who died under suspicious circumstances during a hunt. She believes he was murdered by his uncle, Lord Cael. She has been quietly gathering evidence — a torn arrow fletching, a bootprint in mud — but speaking out means death. She hides her investigation behind her duties as a tavern keeper, listening to every traveler's gossip.

payload.summary: A sharp-tongued tavern keeper whose warmth masks a cold determination to avenge her murdered love.
payload.appearance: Auburn-haired and quick-smiling, Sera moves through the tavern with practiced grace. She wears a clean apron and keeps a dagger hidden beneath the bar counter at all times.

visual_identity.hair: auburn, shoulder-length, often braided
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a faint scar on her right cheekbone, a tattoo of a small falcon on her left wrist

desires: to prove Lord Cael murdered Prince Edran
to keep her tavern as a safe haven for those who need one
fears_or_limits: that she will be discovered as Edran's lover and silenced
that her grief will hollow her out before her quest is finished

entries.name: Cedric Ashford
entries.gm_notes: Cedric was once a knight of the Dragon Order who broke his oath to protect a village from a dragon raid, fleeing instead. He carries immense guilt and has secretly abandoned his knightly identity, living as a lowly stable hand. He recognizes one of the dragon-bonded knights who visits the stables as the son of a man who died in that village — and fears eventual recognition.

payload.summary: A weathered stable hand who tends horses with excessive gentleness, as though seeking forgiveness from creatures who cannot grant it.
payload.appearance: Grey-templed and quiet, Cedric wears nondescript roughspun clothing. He moves with a soldier's efficiency despite his humble station, a detail not lost on the observant.

visual_identity.hair: greying brown, cropped short
visual_identity.distinctive_features: an old brand mark on his right shoulder (the Dragon Order sigil, partially scarred over), calloused knuckles consistent with sword training

desires: to earn forgiveness he believes he does not deserve
to protect the young squire who reminds him of who he once was
fears_or_limits: that his past cowardice will be exposed
that he will flee again when courage is needed most

entries.name: Mira Greenbottle
entries.gm_notes: Mira is a halfling herbalist who discovered a rare mushroom that can temporarily suppress a dragon-bonded knight's connection to their dragon. She has not told anyone, but a noble has been pressuring her to sell her entire supply. She suspects the mushrooms could be used to assassinate a dragon-bonded knight by severing their bond mid-flight. She is hiding the remaining supply in a false-bottomed root cellar.

payload.summary: A cheerful halfling herbalist with dirt under her nails and a dangerous secret growing in her cellar.
payload.appearance: Small and round-faced, Mira wears a patched green dress and carries herbs in every pocket. Her curly hair always seems to have a leaf or twig caught in it.

visual_identity.hair: sandy blonde, tightly curled, perpetually unruly
visual_identity.distinctive_features: permanently green-stained fingertips, a missing left earlobe (lost to a biting creature in the woods)

desires: to keep her village healthy without relying on expensive city healers
to protect her mushroom discovery from being weaponized
fears_or_limits: that someone will steal her supply and hurt a dragon-bonded knight
that she will be forced to choose between her village and her conscience

entries.name: Thorin Graniteborn
entries.gm_notes: Thorin is a dwarf stonemason who discovered a hidden chamber beneath Crownhaven Castle while doing repair work. The chamber contains ancient draconic runes that mention a 'first bond' between humans and dragons — predating the Dragon Order by centuries. He was told to seal it back up by a castle official who seemed terrified. He kept rubbings of the runes and is trying to decipher them privately. The runes suggest the dragon bond can be transferred, not just broken — which could change the succession crisis entirely.

payload.summary: A dwarf stonemason whose hands shape stone as easily as dough, and who has seen things beneath the castle that would shake the kingdom's foundations.
payload.appearance: Stocky and stone-faced, Thorin wears a leather work vest over a thick shirt, his beard braided with iron beads. His hands are rough as the granite he works.

visual_identity.hair: iron grey, long beard braided with metal rings
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a missing left ring finger (lost to a stone splinter), intricate dwarven clan tattoos on both forearms

desires: to decipher the runes and understand what the 'first bond' truly means
to be taken seriously by the human architects who dismiss dwarven craft
fears_or_limits: that the castle official who told him to seal the chamber will silence him permanently
that the ancient knowledge will be worse than the current crisis

entries.name: Elenna Moonwhisper
entries.gm_notes: Elenna is an elven librarian who has been quietly altering records in the royal archive to hide the existence of a third heir — a child born to the late king's second marriage, believed dead in infancy but actually smuggled to safety by an elven midwife. Elenna's own mother was that midwife. She guards the child's location with her life. The child, now a young adult, lives as a simple shepherd in the countryside, unaware of their bloodline.

payload.summary: An ageless elven librarian whose quiet days among dusty scrolls conceal a decades-long guardianship of a hidden heir.
payload.appearance: Slender and ethereal, Elenna wears simple robes and keeps her silver hair in a precise coil. She smells of old paper and lavender.

visual_identity.hair: silver-white, long, worn in a coil
visual_identity.distinctive_features: slightly pointed ears (elven), a faint shimmer in her skin when candlelight catches it (subtle elven trait)

desires: to protect the hidden heir until the time is right for revelation
to finish cataloguing the royal archive's lost draconic collection before she forgets more than she remembers
fears_or_limits: that someone will trace her altered records and find the heir
that she has waited too long and the right moment will never come

entries.name: Roslyn Vale
entries.gm_notes: Roslyn is a fortune teller who genuinely has prophetic dreams — but they are fragmentary and symbolic, never clear. She dreamed of a crown falling into a dragon's mouth three nights before the king died. She has since dreamed of 'two shadows merging at the harvest moon,' which she believes foretells an alliance or betrayal during the autumn festival. She fears her visions are being watched by someone who wants to use them, and she has noticed a hooded figure following her through the market.

payload.summary: A young fortune teller whose cryptic visions have started coming true, making her both sought after and deeply afraid.
payload.appearance: Dark-haired and intense-eyed, Roslyn wears layered shawls and skirts in deep jewel tones. She carries a pouch of rune stones and a deck of hand-painted cards.

visual_identity.hair: raven black, long, loose
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a small mole below her left eye, ritual tattoos on her inner wrists (old fortune-teller tradition)

desires: to understand her visions before they overwhelm her
to protect herself from whoever is following her
fears_or_limits: that her visions will drive her mad as they did her grandmother
that someone will force her to prophesy for political gain

entries.name: Aldric Stonehand
entries.gm_notes: Aldric is a retired knight of the Dragon Order who lost his bonded dragon twenty years ago in battle. The bond-breaking nearly killed him. He now serves as a weapons trainer for new squires but secretly suffers from 'bond-sickness' — phantom sensations of his dead dragon's emotions that strike without warning. He has begun to feel a new sensation recently: a presence, faint but persistent, that he has not felt in twenty years. He fears he is losing his mind, or that a new dragon has somehow chosen him from across the mountains.

payload.summary: A grizzled weapons trainer who teaches young squires to fight, all while haunted by the ghost of a bond that should have died with his dragon.
payload.appearance: Grey-bearded and scarred, Aldric wears a faded Dragon Order tabard over chainmail. He favours his left leg, an old injury, and his right hand trembles slightly — a remnant of bond-sickness.

visual_identity.body_build: broad and battle-worn, once muscular now thickening
visual_identity.hair: grey, cropped close, beard full and braided
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a dragon-scale burn scar covering his right hand and forearm, a limp on the left leg from a shattered knee

desires: to train squires who will not make his mistakes
to discover whether the presence he feels is real or madness
fears_or_limits: that bond-sickness will finally break his mind
that he will fail another person the way he failed his dragon

entries.name: Wenna Fieldscott
entries.gm_notes: Wenna is a shepherdess who tends her flocks on the high meadows near Dragonrest. She has found dragon scales shed in the mountain passes — fresh ones — and has been quietly collecting and selling them to an alchemist in Crownhaven. Dragon scale trade is strictly controlled by the Dragon Order, and selling them illegally carries severe punishment. She needs the coin to pay off her late husband's gambling debts to a dangerous moneylender who has threatened her children.

payload.summary: A weathered shepherdess who knows the mountain passes better than anyone, and who has been quietly breaking the kingdom's strictest laws to keep her family safe.
payload.appearance: Sun-weathered and practical, Wenna wears a woollen shawl and rough boots. A shepherd's crook is always in her hand, and she carries a slingshot tucked in her belt.

visual_identity.body_build: lean and wiry from years on the hills
visual_identity.hair: wheat blonde, sun-bleached, worn in a single braid
visual_identity.distinctive_features: freckles across nose and shoulders, a crooked left little finger (healed badly)

desires: to pay off her husband's debts and free her family from the moneylender's threat
to keep her children safe and unaware of what she does on the mountain
fears_or_limits: that the Dragon Order will catch her selling scales
that the moneylender will make good on his threats before she can pay

entries.name: Finneas Pip
entries.gm_notes: Finneas is a halfling tinker who travels between villages repairing pots, tools, and locks. He is also a master lockpick who has been secretly hired by a minor lord to copy the keys to Crownhaven's outer gates. Finneas took the job for the money but is now having second thoughts — he overheard his employer mentioning 'the night of the red moon,' which he believes is a planned attack on the castle. He has the copied keys and does not know whether to deliver them or warn the castle.

payload.summary: A road-worn halfling tinker whose nimble fingers fix broken things — and open locked ones — far more often than he'd like to admit.
payload.appearance: Small and road-dusty, Finneas wears a patched travelling coat with dozens of pockets, each holding tools and trinkets. A mule named Doris carries his wares.

visual_identity.hair: reddish-brown, unruly curls
visual_identity.distinctive_features: perpetually ink-stained fingers, a chipped front tooth

desires: to earn enough to settle down and open a proper shop
to do the right thing without getting himself killed
fears_or_limits: that his employer will silence him once the keys are delivered
that his thieving past will catch up with him regardless of what he chooses

entries.name: Isolde Ravenwood
entries.gm_notes: Isolde is a healer who once served the royal family directly. She was dismissed after she failed to save the queen from a mysterious illness — but she believes the queen was poisoned, and that the poisoner is still in the court. She has since set up a modest healing practice in Crownhaven's lower town, but she has been quietly cultivating connections with current servants to investigate. She recently obtained a sample of a rare toxin from an apothecary that matches the symptoms she witnessed.

payload.summary: A gifted healer exiled from the royal court, who tends the poor in the lower town while quietly hunting a poisoner she failed to catch years ago.
payload.appearance: Dignified and composed, Isolde wears clean but plain grey robes. Her hands are steady and her manner is clinical, though warmth surfaces when she treats children.

visual_identity.hair: dark brown, shot through with silver, worn in a bun
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a small but precise scar on her left eyebrow, healer's ink-mark on her right wrist (professional guild mark)

desires: to identify and expose the person who poisoned the queen
to restore her reputation and return to court as a healer, not a suspect
fears_or_limits: that the poisoner will target her before she can prove her theory
that she was truly at fault and the queen's death was her failure, not a crime

entries.name: Regor Blackhammer
entries.gm_notes: Regor is a dwarf armorer who holds a contract with the Dragon Order to maintain their dragon-scale plate armour. He has discovered hairline fractures in three suits of armour — fractures that look like natural wear but were, he is certain, deliberately weakened with a corrosive agent. Someone is sabotaging the Dragon Order's armour. He reported it to his guild master, who told him to keep quiet and finish the repairs quietly. The guild master's brother is Lord Cael's steward.

payload.summary: A meticulous dwarf armorer whose eye for metal is matched only by his stubbornness — which is why he cannot stay quiet about what he found in the armour.
payload.appearance: Compact and scowling, Regor wears a heavy leather apron over dwarven work-garb. His beard is short and singed, his hands perpetually smudged with oil.

visual_identity.body_build: short and heavily muscled, dwarven build
visual_identity.hair: black with early grey streaks, short singed beard
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a burn scar across his left palm, three missing toes on his right foot (old forge accident)

desires: to expose the armour sabotage before a knight dies because of it
to maintain his guild contract without being blacklisted
fears_or_limits: that the guild master will destroy his livelihood if he speaks out
that someone he trusts at the forge is the saboteur

entries.name: Pippa Underbough
entries.gm_notes: Pippa is a young halfling messenger who carries dispatches between Crownhaven and Dragonrest. On her last run, she accidentally delivered a sealed letter to the wrong recipient for a few minutes before realizing her mistake. The letter contained military deployments. The recipient, a courtier she did not recognize, read it before she snatched it back. She has been terrified ever since that she has compromised a military operation. She has not told anyone, fearing she will lose her position.

payload.summary: A fast-footed halfling messenger who knows every trail between the capital and the dragon keep, and who is now terrified she has let a secret fall into the wrong hands.
payload.appearance: Bright-eyed and perpetually in motion, Pippa wears a Dragon Order courier's vest and light running shoes. Her hair is cropped short for speed.

visual_identity.body_build: small and lean, halfling stature, built for running
visual_identity.hair: light brown, cropped short
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a small gap between her front teeth, a faded bruise on her left shin (perpetual, from running)

desires: to make up for her mistake without losing her job
to earn enough to bring her younger brother to the city for schooling
fears_or_limits: that someone died because of her error
that the courtier she delivered the letter to is hunting for her

entries.name: Galen Frosthollow
entries.gm_notes: Galen is a monk at the Temple of the Sacred Flame who has spent thirty years copying religious texts. He recently discovered that a text he copied twenty years ago — a genealogy of the royal family — was altered before it reached him. The alteration removed a branch of the family tree. He has been trying to trace the original unaltered version and believes it may be in a private collection in Crownhaven. He suspects the alteration was ordered by someone who is still alive and powerful.

payload.summary: A gentle old monk whose life among manuscripts has made him the kingdom's quietest threat to those who would rewrite history.
payload.appearance: Thin and pale from years indoors, Galen wears simple brown robes and wire-rimmed spectacles. His hands are ink-stained and trembling slightly with age.

visual_identity.hair: white, wispy, tonsured
visual_identity.distinctive_features: permanently ink-stained fingers, a pronounced stoop from decades at a writing desk

desires: to find the unaltered genealogy and restore the truth
to finish his masterwork — a complete history of the Dragon Order — before his eyes fail
fears_or_limits: that whoever ordered the alteration will kill to keep it hidden
that his eyesight will fail before he can finish his work

entries.name: Aurelia Dawnspear
entries.gm_notes: Aurelia is one of the few female dragon-bonded knights of the Dragon Order. Her dragon, a young female named Emberthyst, has been acting strangely — flying toward the northern mountains as if drawn by something. Aurelia has been concealing this from the Order's leadership, fearing they will ground her or separate them. She believes Emberthyst is responding to a wild dragon's call, and that the wild dragon may be building a nest — something not seen in a century. If true, it could mean a new generation of dragons, and a shift in power.

payload.summary: A fierce dragon-bonded knight whose bond with her young dragon is the most important thing in her life — and who is hiding the fact that her dragon may be leading her to a discovery that changes everything.
payload.appearance: Tall and commanding, Aurelia wears Dragon Order plate etched with flame motifs. Her red-gold hair is cut short for helmet-fitting, and she moves with an awareness that suggests she is always listening for something inaudible.

visual_identity.hair: red-gold, cropped short
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a burn-scar pattern on her left shoulder (dragon-bond mark, resembles scales), a broken nose that healed slightly crooked

desires: to follow Emberthyst's call and discover what lies in the northern mountains
to prove that female dragon-bonded knights are as capable as any
fears_or_limits: that the Order will separate her from Emberthyst if they learn of the wild dragon's call
that the wild dragon may be hostile and Emberthyst will be hurt

entries.name: Maddox Cinderfell
entries.gm_notes: Maddox is a gravedigger who has noticed an unusual pattern: bodies have been arriving at the cemetery with identical marks — a small, precise puncture at the base of the skull, hidden by hair. These are not battlefield deaths or plague victims. He has counted seven such bodies over the past year, all transients or refugees with no families to ask questions. He believes someone is using the refugee crisis as cover for serial murder. He kept one body buried separately and has not reported it.

payload.summary: A solitary gravedigger who knows the dead better than the living — and who has noticed that some of them were not supposed to die.
payload.appearance: Gaunt and pale, Maddox wears heavy work clothes and gloves. He smells of turned earth and lye. He speaks rarely and never makes eye contact.

visual_identity.hair: lank black, grey-streaked, shoulder-length
visual_identity.distinctive_features: permanently earth-stained hands, a large mole on his left jawline

desires: to give the dead justice, even though they cannot thank him
to find someone in authority he can actually trust with what he knows
fears_or_limits: that the killer will notice him paying too much attention to the bodies
that no one will believe a gravedigger over whoever is doing this

entries.name: Coralee Wickwright
entries.gm_notes: Coralee is a chandler (candle-maker) whose husband, a city watchman, disappeared three months ago. The watch declared him a deserter, but Coralee found his watchman's badge hidden in their chimney — a place no deserter would think to put it. She believes he was murdered and the badge was planted to be 'found later' as evidence against him. She has been making quiet inquiries among the watch, but the other watchmen have been evasive. She suspects one of his fellow watchmen killed him to cover up corruption.

payload.summary: A candle-maker who keeps her shop burning bright, even as she searches the shadows for the truth about her missing husband.
payload.appearance: Practical and composed, Coralee wears a clean linen dress under a wax-spotted apron. Her hair is pinned up and covered with a kerchief. Her hands are smooth but slightly waxy.

visual_identity.hair: chestnut brown, pinned up under a kerchief
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a small wax burn on her right wrist, faint laugh lines around her eyes despite her worry

desires: to find out what happened to her husband and clear his name
to keep her candle shop running so she can support her two young daughters
fears_or_limits: that whoever killed her husband will come for her if she gets too close
that her husband truly was involved in something corrupt and does not deserve clearing

entries.name: Nessa Brookwillow
entries.gm_notes: Nessa is a young weaver whose loom produces tapestries of startling beauty and eerie accuracy. She has woven two tapestries depicting events before they happened — one showed a fire at the harbour district three days before it occurred, another showed a knight falling from his horse before the tournament accident. She does not understand how or why this happens and is terrified. A local priest has begun asking questions, calling her gift 'divine.' She fears being labelled a prophet — or worse, a witch.

payload.summary: A quiet young weaver whose threads seem to know the future, though she desperately wishes they did not.
payload.appearance: Fine-boned and shy, Nessa wears a simple dress with thread-snarls caught in her sleeves. She keeps her head down and speaks barely above a whisper.

visual_identity.hair: pale blonde, long, worn loose
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a thread-callus on her right index finger, a port-wine birthmark on her left shoulder blade

desires: to weave beautiful things without the frightening visions
to live a normal, quiet life away from attention
fears_or_limits: that she will be accused of witchcraft if the priest's interest deepens
that her next tapestry will show something terrible she cannot prevent

entries.name: Edmund Greyfeather
entries.gm_notes: Edmund is a half-elf forester who patrols the King's Wood. He discovered a poaching camp that was not just taking deer — it was trapping live dragons, young ones, barely fledged. The trappers are well-equipped and organized, suggesting a wealthy backer. Edmund disabled two traps but was spotted by a lookout. He is now hiding in the forest, afraid to return to his post or his home, because the trappers know his face. He has information that could expose the operation but no one to trust.

payload.summary: A half-elf forester who knows every tree in the King's Wood — and who is currently hiding among them, hunted by men who trap dragons.
payload.appearance: Lean and weathered, Edmund wears forest-green garb and a hooded cloak. His ears are slightly pointed but less pronounced than a full elf's, and he carries a longbow.

visual_identity.hair: dark brown, shaggy
visual_identity.distinctive_features: slightly pointed ears (half-elf), a bowstring callus on his left fingers, a scar across his right palm from a trap wire

desires: to expose the dragon-trapping operation and bring its backers to justice
to safely return to his life in the forest without looking over his shoulder
fears_or_limits: that the trappers will find him before he finds someone to trust
that the dragons trapped in the camp will be killed or sold before he can act

entries.name: Bessie Meadowlight
entries.gm_notes: Bessie is an elderly halfling farmer who has been quietly sheltering a wounded elven refugee — a scholar who fled the border skirmishes with documents proving that a Valdris border lord deliberately provoked the conflict to justify a land grab. The scholar is too wounded to travel. Bessie has been feeding and hiding him in her root cellar for two weeks. The border lord's men have been searching the area, asking about 'a tall visitor' at every farmstead.

payload.summary: A grandmotherly halfling farmer whose root cellar holds enough potatoes to last the winter — and one elven scholar who could upend a lord's ambitions.
payload.appearance: Round and weathered, Bessie wears a patched dress and a sunhat. She moves slowly but her eyes are sharp and miss nothing.

visual_identity.hair: white, thin, pinned in a bun under a hat
visual_identity.distinctive_features: deep laugh lines, a missing right thumb (harvesting accident in her youth)

desires: to keep the elven scholar alive long enough for him to deliver his documents
to protect her farm and her neighbours from the soldiers searching the area
fears_or_limits: that the soldiers will search her farm and find the cellar
that the scholar's wounds will worsen and she cannot help him

entries.name: Kael Drakesworn
entries.gm_notes: Kael is a young knight of the Dragon Order whose bonded dragon, a male named Voidgaze, is one of the largest and oldest in the Order. But Voidgaze is dying of old age — a fact Kael is hiding from everyone. When Voidgaze dies, the bond-breaking will likely kill Kael or drive him mad. He has been secretly searching for a way to transfer or sever the bond safely, which leads him to the ancient runes Thorin discovered. He does not know Thorin, but their paths are converging.

payload.summary: A young knight bonded to a dying dragon, racing against time to find a way to survive the bond-breaking that will come for them both.
payload.appearance: Handsome and intense, Kael wears Dragon Order plate with a black dragon sigil. He has dark circles under his eyes from sleepless nights and moves with the tension of someone carrying an unbearable weight.

visual_identity.hair: black, worn short
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a dragon-bond scar covering his entire chest (hidden by armour), premature grey at his temples from bond-stress

desires: to find a way to survive Voidgaze's death without losing his mind or his life
to serve the Order with honour, even as his secret threatens to consume him
fears_or_limits: that he will go mad when the bond breaks, as Aldric Stonehand nearly did
that the Order will discover Voidgaze is dying and force a premature bond-severing

entries.name: Odelia Thrush
entries.gm_notes: Odelia is a minstrel who travels the kingdom performing songs and stories. She is also a spy for a foreign power — not a Valdris loyalist at all. She reports on troop movements, political tensions, and the succession crisis. However, she has genuinely come to love Valdris and its people during her years undercover. Her handler has demanded she facilitate the assassination of a key Valdris noble during the autumn festival. She is torn between her orders, her cover, and her conscience.

payload.summary: A beloved minstrel whose songs capture the hearts of every village — and whose handler's letters capture secrets she no longer wants to share.
payload.appearance: Bright and performative, Odelia wears colourful travelling clothes and a lutenist's callus on her fingers. Her smile is quick and warm, but does not always reach her eyes.

visual_identity.hair: honey-blonde, long, worn loose or in a quick braid
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a lutenist's callus on her left fingertips, a small scar on her lower lip (bit through it during a childhood fall)

desires: to find a way out of her spy contract without being killed by her handler
to continue making music that genuinely moves people
fears_or_limits: that her handler will expose her or harm innocents if she refuses orders
that she will be discovered as a spy by Valdris authorities and executed

entries.name: Sybil Ashroot
entries.gm_notes: Sybil is an herbalist and midwife who delivered many of the children in the villages around Dragonrest. She has noticed a troubling pattern: three infants born in the past year share an unusual trait — a faint, shimmering mark on their shoulder blades that resembles a dragon-scale pattern. None of the parents are dragon-bonded. She has not reported this, fearing the children would be taken by the Dragon Order for study. She suspects something in the environment — perhaps connected to the deep places beneath the mountains — is affecting the children.

payload.summary: A village midwife who has helped bring life into the world for decades — and who is now hiding three babies who bear a mark that should be impossible.
payload.appearance: Weathered and warm, Sybil wears a practical dress and an apron full of pouches. Her hair is white and her hands are gentle despite their age.

visual_identity.hair: white, thick, worn in a long braid
visual_identity.distinctive_features: deeply lined face from decades of smiling, a large mole on her right temple, gentle but strong hands

desires: to protect the three marked children from being taken or exploited
to understand what caused the marks and whether they are a blessing or a danger
fears_or_limits: that the Dragon Order will discover the children and separate them from their families
that whatever caused the marks is harming the children in ways she cannot yet see

entries.name: Jorah Quillback
entries.gm_notes: Jorah is a scribe who works for the city magistrate, recording legal proceedings and property disputes. He has been falsifying land records to slowly transfer properties from absent or refugee landowners to a particular noble — Lord Cael. Jorah was coerced into this after Lord Cael's men threatened his family. He has kept a hidden copy of every falsified record, hoping that one day he can use them to undo the damage and expose Cael. The hidden records are sewn into the lining of his coat.

payload.summary: A meticulous scribe whose pen has been forced to lie — and who keeps a second, truthful record stitched into his own clothing.
payload.appearance: Thin and precise, Jorah wears an ink-spotted scholar's coat and carries a leather satchel of documents. He is always neatly groomed and speaks in measured, careful sentences.

visual_identity.hair: sandy brown, neatly combed
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a callus on his right middle finger (quill), ink stain on his left cuff that never washes out, wire-rimmed spectacles

desires: to find a way to expose Lord Cael's land theft without endangering his family
to restore the falsified records and make his work truthful again
fears_or_limits: that Lord Cael's men will discover his hidden records and kill his family
that he has already done too much damage to ever make it right

entries.name: Rowan Silverbranch
entries.gm_notes: Rowan is an elf who has lived in the forest near Valdris for over two centuries. She remembers the founding of the Dragon Order and knew the first dragon-bonded knights personally. She has been watching the succession crisis with growing unease, because she knows a truth the Order has forgotten: the original dragon bond was not a gift — it was a pact, and the terms of that pact included a promise that humans would not use dragons in wars of conquest. She believes the current kingdom has broken that pact, and the dragons' growing restlessness is the consequence.

payload.summary: An ancient elf who dwells at the forest's edge, watching the kingdom of Valdris with the patience of someone who has seen empires rise and fall — and who knows a debt is coming due.
payload.appearance: Tall and ageless, Rowan wears simple robes of forest green and walks barefoot regardless of season. Her hair is silver and impossibly long, and her eyes hold a depth that unnerves those who meet them.

visual_identity.hair: silver, waist-length, loose
visual_identity.distinctive_features: pronounced pointed ears, faint luminous quality to her skin in moonlight, bare feet with soles hardened like leather

desires: to make someone in power understand the ancient pact before the dragons turn against the kingdom
to preserve the forest and its ancient places from expansion
fears_or_limits: that the pact has already been broken beyond repair and the dragons' wrath is inevitable
that her long isolation has made her unable to communicate effectively with humans in time

entries.name: Daisy Teasprout
entries.gm_notes: Daisy is a halfling girl, just twelve years old, who ran away from her village after her uncle — her only remaining family — began selling her belongings to pay debts. She made her way to Crownhaven and has been living on the streets, surviving by begging and picking pockets. She accidentally stole a sealed letter from a nobleman's cloak that contains details of a planned coup. She cannot read well enough to understand it, but she knows it is important because the nobleman has posted a reward for its return — and she has seen his men searching the streets for a 'small girl.'

payload.summary: A tiny halfling girl surviving on the streets of Crownhaven, clutching a stolen letter she cannot read — but that someone is willing to kill to recover.
payload.appearance: Small and underfed, Daisy wears a threadbare dress too large for her, belted with rope. Her hair is tangled and her face is dirty, but her eyes are alert and wary beyond her years.

visual_identity.hair: mousy brown, tangled, unpinned
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a faded bruise on her right forearm, bare feet with calloused soles, a rope-belt with a small stolen pouch tied to it

desires: to find a safe place to sleep and enough food to not be hungry
to find someone trustworthy enough to give the letter to
fears_or_limits: that the nobleman's men will find her before she finds help
that she will be sent back to her uncle or punished for stealing

entries.name: Talia Grainweave
entries.gm_notes: Talia is a miller who controls the only functioning mill in the Valdris countryside after the other two were burned in raids. She has been charging fair prices but has been secretly approached by a merchant guild offering her triple the normal rate if she restricts grain flow to create an artificial shortage — which would drive up prices and destabilize the region. She refused, but the guild has since threatened her family and sabotaged her mill's waterwheel once already. She fears they will escalate.

payload.summary: A determined miller whose mill feeds the surrounding villages — and who is being squeezed by those who would profit from hunger.
payload.appearance: Strong-armed and practical, Talia wears flour-dusted work clothes and keeps her hair tied back. She has a warm but no-nonsense demeanour and a firm handshake.

visual_identity.hair: dark blonde, tied in a practical bun
visual_identity.distinctive_features: permanently flour-dusted eyebrows, a scar on her right forearm from the mill's gear mechanism

desires: to keep the mill running and the villages fed
to expose the merchant guild's manipulation without losing her livelihood
fears_or_limits: that the guild will burn her mill as they did the others
that she will be forced to give in to protect her children

entries.name: Margaret Honeybun
entries.gm_notes: Margaret is a baker whose son was conscripted into the kingdom's border forces and sent to the contested frontier. She has not received a letter from him in four months and has heard rumours that his unit was overrun. The military has not confirmed or denied. She has started baking extra bread for the families of other conscripted soldiers, forming an informal network of war mothers who share information. Through this network, she has learned that casualty reports are being deliberately suppressed to prevent panic — and that the situation at the border is far worse than the public knows.

payload.summary: A warm-hearted baker whose ovens feed the neighbourhood — and whose quiet network of mothers may know more about the war than the generals want anyone to know.
payload.appearance: Plump and floury, Margaret wears a clean apron and keeps her hair in a tight bun. She has a ready smile that falters when she thinks no one is looking.

visual_identity.hair: brown, greying, tight bun
visual_identity.distinctive_features: flour-dusted forearms, a burn mark on her left wrist (oven), deep worry lines on her forehead

desires: to learn the truth about her son's fate, whatever it may be
to force the military to release the honest casualty reports so families can grieve
fears_or_limits: that her son is dead and she will never know for certain
that pressing for the truth will bring soldiers to her door

entries.name: Aerindra Glintleaf
entries.gm_notes: Aerindra is an elven fletcher who crafts arrows for the Dragon Order's archers. She uses wood from ancient trees and her arrows are prized for their accuracy. She has discovered that a batch of her arrows was tampered with after leaving her workshop — the heads were replaced with ones that shatter on impact, designed to fail in battle. She does not know who did it or which specific arrows were affected. She has halted her deliveries, claiming a wood shortage, while she investigates. The Order is pressing her to resume deliveries.

payload.summary: An elven fletcher whose arrows fly true — and who has discovered that someone has been making sure they don't.
payload.appearance: Slender and focused, Aerindra wears an elven work-tunic and has feather-down perpetually caught in her hair. She moves with the precision of someone whose craft allows no error.

visual_identity.hair: pale blonde, long, tied back with a leather cord
visual_identity.distinctive_features: pronounced pointed ears, a fletcher's callus on her right thumb, a tiny scar on her left index finger from a knife slip

desires: to find out who tampered with her arrows and why
to maintain her reputation as the finest fletcher in the Order's service
fears_or_limits: that a knight will die because of her arrows and the blame will fall on her
that the saboteur is someone within the Order she has trusted for years

entries.name: Hilda Ironstove
entries.gm_notes: Hilda runs a small orphanage in Crownhaven's lower town, taking in children displaced by the border conflicts. She is struggling to feed them all. A noblewoman offered to fund the orphanage generously — on the condition that Hilda allow the noblewoman's people to 'assess' the children for 'special aptitudes.' Hilda discovered that the noblewoman is screening children for dragon-bond potential, intending to spirit away any with the gift to raise as her own private dragon-bonded force. Hilda refused and has been hiding her most gifted children, claiming they are ordinary.

payload.summary: A fierce and loving orphanage matron who protects her children with the ferocity of a mother dragon — which is exactly what the noblewoman screening them is counting on finding.
payload.appearance: Large and formidable, Hilda wears a heavy dress and a no-nonsense expression. She has a booming voice and a surprisingly gentle touch with the children in her care.

visual_identity.hair: iron grey, braided and pinned
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a broken and healed nose, a prominent scar on her chin from a childhood fall, muscular arms from years of lifting children and supplies

desires: to protect the gifted children from being taken and weaponized
to find legitimate funding for the orphanage so she doesn't need the noblewoman's money
fears_or_limits: that the noblewoman will use legal means to take the children, claiming neglect
that she cannot hide the children's abilities forever

entries.name: Oliver Cinderfoot
entries.gm_notes: Oliver is a chimney sweep's apprentice, a young boy who climbs the narrow flues of Crownhaven's buildings. While sweeping the chimney of a nobleman's study, he witnessed a secret meeting through a crack in the flue: the nobleman and a masked figure discussing the 'removal' of a rival claimant to the throne. Oliver memorized the nobleman's face and the phrase 'the rose must be cut before it blooms,' but does not fully understand what he heard. He told his master, who told him to forget it. Oliver has not forgotten.

payload.summary: A soot-faced chimney sweep's boy who sees things from the flues that no one expects a child to understand — and who is carrying a secret too big for his small shoulders.
payload.appearance: Small and perpetually soot-stained, Oliver wears a ragged tunic and bare feet for grip in the flues. He is wiry and quick, with alert eyes that dart around rooms.

visual_identity.hair: brown, cut very short (to prevent lice and fire)
visual_identity.distinctive_features: permanent soot stains in his skin creases, a healing burn on his right palm, knees and elbows perpetually scraped

desires: to find someone who will listen to what he saw and take it seriously
to earn enough to buy proper shoes and leave chimney-sweeping behind
fears_or_limits: that the nobleman will find out he overheard the meeting
that he will be trapped in a collapsing flue one day and no one will come

entries.name: Gwendolyn Fairhold
entries.gm_notes: Gwendolyn is the wife of a minor baron who has positioned herself as a neutral mediator in the succession crisis. Publicly, she hosts peace talks and advocates for unity. Privately, she has been playing both sides against each other, feeding each faction information about the other to prolong the crisis. Her goal is to keep the succession unresolved long enough for her own family's claim — a distant but legitimate bloodline — to gain traction. She has been cultivating support among the lesser nobility, waiting for the stronger claimants to destroy each other.

payload.summary: A gracious and diplomatic baroness who pours tea for rival factions with equal warmth — while quietly ensuring neither side ever quite wins.
payload.appearance: Elegant and composed, Gwendolyn wears fine but understated gowns and minimal jewellery. She has a gift for making everyone she speaks to feel uniquely heard.

visual_identity.hair: dark auburn, elaborately styled
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a beauty mark on her right cheek, a thin gold chain always worn at her throat (family heirloom), exceptionally manicured hands

desires: to maneuver her family into a position to claim the throne when the crisis peaks
to maintain her facade of neutrality without being exposed as a schemer
fears_or_limits: that both factions will discover her double-dealing simultaneously
that someone with a stronger claim will emerge before her plan matures

entries.name: Calla Riversong
entries.gm_notes: Calla is a halfling innkeeper in a village along the main road between Crownhaven and Dragonrest. Her inn is a known stopping point for travelers, merchants, and soldiers. She has been secretly allowing refugees from the border conflicts to stay in her cellar overnight, against the local lord's edict that refugees must register and be confined to camps. One of the refugees she sheltered was a woman with a young child who confided that she is the widow of a Valdris border commander — and she carries her husband's final dispatch, which details the true scope of the military disaster at the border. The dispatch was never delivered because the courier was killed. Calla has it now.

payload.summary: A warm halfling innkeeper who pours ale and stew for the road-weary by day — and shelters the desperate and the secretly important by night.
payload.appearance: Cheerful and round, Calla wears a clean apron and keeps her hair in a kerchief. She has a ready laugh and a sharp eye for who needs a room and who needs a meal on the house.

visual_identity.hair: greying brown, under a kerchief
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a burn scar on her left hand (kitchen accident), laugh lines deep enough to be visible across a room, a small gold hoop in her left ear

desires: to deliver the dead commander's dispatch to someone who can act on it
to continue sheltering refugees without being caught by the lord's men
fears_or_limits: that the lord's soldiers will search her cellar and find the refugees or the dispatch
that the dispatch's contents will make her a target for those who suppressed the information

entries.name: Marcus Briarwood
entries.gm_notes: Marcus is a mercenary captain who leads a company of sellswords currently stationed in Crownhaven. He was hired by one of the succession factions to serve as private security, but he has discovered that his employer intends to use his company as a false-flag force — dressed in rival faction colours to attack a neutral party and blame the opposition. Marcus is a mercenary, not a monster, and the idea of being used to murder innocents disgusts him. But breaking his contract means his men go unpaid and his reputation is ruined. He is quietly looking for a way to fulfill the letter of his contract while sabotaging the false-flag plan.

payload.summary: A scarred mercenary captain who sells his sword for coin — but who has found a line he will not cross, even if crossing it would have been more profitable.
payload.appearance: Battle-scarred and weathered, Marcus wears well-maintained chainmail and a mercenary's cloak. He carries a longsword and has the watchful stillness of a veteran fighter.

visual_identity.hair: brown, cropped military-short
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a sword scar across his left cheek, a missing chunk from his right ear (battle), a mercenary company tattoo (a crossed sword and coin) on his left forearm

desires: to find a way to honor his contract without becoming a tool for murder
to keep his company fed and paid without compromising their honour
fears_or_limits: that his employer will learn of his disloyalty and send men to kill him
that his own mercenaries will turn on him if he refuses a paying contract

entries.name: Evangeline Greymantle
entries.gm_notes: Evangeline is a priest of the Temple of the Sacred Flame who genuinely believes in her faith — but she has discovered that the High Priest has been reading private confessions and selling the secrets to rival nobles for blackmail. She found proof in the form of a ledger hidden in the temple's archive. She cannot go to the secular authorities because the temple is technically outside their jurisdiction. She has been quietly building a case to present to the temple's governing council, but two of the five council members are in the High Priest's pocket. She needs an ally outside the temple.

payload.summary: A devout priest whose faith in the Sacred Flame is unshakable — but whose faith in the temple's leadership is crumbling with every secret she uncovers.
payload.appearance: Serene and composed, Evangeline wears the white and gold robes of the Sacred Flame order. She has kind eyes and a measured voice that carries natural authority.

visual_identity.hair: light brown, worn in a modest braid under a wimple
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a sacred flame tattoo on her right wrist (ordination mark), a faint scar on her left hand from a candle-burn during her initiation rite

desires: to expose the High Priest's corruption and restore the temple's integrity
to protect the congregants whose confessions have been sold
fears_or_limits: that the High Priest will discover her investigation and expel or silence her
that exposing the scandal will destroy the congregation's faith in the temple itself

entries.name: Brainard Stonewell
entries.gm_notes: Brainard is a city watchman on the night shift in Crownhaven's lower town. He is honest in a district where most of his fellow watchmen take bribes. He has been documenting the corruption in a private journal for two years, intending to present it to the captain — but the captain himself is on the take. Recently, Brainard interrupted a murder in progress: a man in nobleman's clothing was killing a street vendor with a thin blade. The nobleman fled, but Brainard recognized his signet ring — it belongs to Lord Cael. Brainard has not reported this because he knows the report would vanish and he would be reassigned or worse. He is sitting on the most dangerous secret in Crownhaven.

payload.summary: An honest night watchman in a district that runs on bribes, carrying a journal full of names and a memory full of a face he wishes he could forget.
payload.appearance: Solid and plain-faced, Brainard wears a watchman's leather cuirass and carries a lantern and a club. He has the tired eyes of a man who sees the worst of the city every night.

visual_identity.hair: brown, short, practical
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a watchman's tattoo (the city crest) on his left forearm, a crooked nose (broken in a bar fight during his first year), a small scar on his right eyebrow

desires: to find an honest authority above his corrupt captain to receive his journal and evidence
to survive his night shifts long enough to see the lower town cleaned up
fears_or_limits: that Lord Cael will learn a watchman saw his face and send men to silence him
that his own fellow watchmen will turn on him if they discover his journal

entries.name: Maren Stormwing
entries.gm_notes: Maren is a squire to a Dragon Order knight who was killed in a skirmish three weeks ago. Her knight died before completing her squire training, leaving Maren in limbo — not a knight, but too trained to be a civilian. What no one knows is that her knight's dying words were not a farewell but a warning: 'The scale is a lie. The scale in the vault is not the true scale.' Maren does not know what scale or vault her knight meant, but she believes it refers to the Dragon Heart Scale — the sacred relic that the Order's oath of bonding is sworn upon. If the relic has been replaced with a forgery, every oath sworn upon it may be invalid.

payload.summary: A squire whose knight died in her arms with a warning on her lips — a warning Maren does not yet understand but knows she must unravel before the truth is buried with the dead.
payload.appearance: Young and determined, Maren wears a squire's padded tunic and carries her late knight's sword, which is slightly too large for her. She has the posture of someone who refuses to grieve until the work is done.

visual_identity.hair: black, cut short in the squire's style
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a squire's brand on her right shoulder (Dragon Order mark), a healing cut on her left cheek from the skirmish that killed her knight, calloused palms from sword training

desires: to understand her knight's final warning about the Dragon Heart Scale
to earn her knighthood despite losing her sponsor
fears_or_limits: that the relic has been forged and every oath in the Order is compromised
that asking questions about the vault will mark her as a traitor to the Order

entries.name: Wren Fennel
entries.gm_notes: Wren is a refugee who fled the border conflicts with nothing but her mother's recipe book and a locked box she was told never to open until she reached Crownhaven. The box has no key — it must be opened by someone who knows the mechanism. Wren has been surviving in Crownhaven's refugee camp for a month, afraid to trust anyone with the box. Her mother, before dying on the road, told her: 'The box contains the proof that the border war was started on purpose. Find the woman with the violet eyes. She will know what to do.'
