Wren does not know who the woman with violet eyes is — but Elenna Moonwhisper, the elven librarian, has pale violet eyes.

payload.summary: A young refugee girl in a crowded camp, clutching a locked box she cannot open and a message she cannot yet deliver to a woman she has never met.
payload.appearance: Thin and road-worn, Wren wears travel-stained clothes that are too large for her. She carries the locked box everywhere, even to sleep. Her eyes are wary but not defeated.

visual_identity.body_build: thin from weeks of hardship on the road
visual_identity.hair: dark brown, lank, cut unevenly (done with a knife on the road)
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a burn mark on her right palm (from carrying the box near a campfire), a faded bruise on her left temple, a threadbare scarf worn in all weather

desires: to find the woman with violet eyes and deliver the box as her mother asked
to find a safe home and a life beyond running
fears_or_limits: that soldiers will search the refugee camp and confiscate the box
that the woman with violet eyes will not be who her mother believed — or will be dead

entries.name: Freya Stormcrest
entries.gm_notes: Freya is a castle guard stationed on Crownhaven's outer wall. She discovered that the night watch rotation has been altered to leave a specific section of the wall unguarded for exactly one hour each night. She reported it to her superior, who dismissed it as a scheduling error. Suspicious, Freya began watching that section herself during the gap — and witnessed a rope ladder being lowered from the inside of the wall to the ground below. Someone within the castle guard is deliberately letting people in and out of the castle after dark. She has not reported this higher because she does not know how far the conspiracy reaches within the guard.

payload.summary: A sharp-eyed castle guard who trusted her superior and was dismissed — and who now watches the wall alone, knowing that someone inside the castle is opening its doors to the night.
payload.appearance: Alert and athletic, Freya wears a castle guard's chainmail and a crimson tabard. She carries a halberd and moves with the coiled readiness of someone who expects trouble at any moment.

visual_identity.hair: reddish-blonde, cropped short under a helm
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a guard's brand on her left forearm (castle crest), a scar across her right knuckles (sparring injury), a slightly crooked right index finger (healed break)

desires: to uncover who is inside the castle guard conspiracy and how high it reaches
to prove that her vigilance matters, even when her superiors dismiss her
fears_or_limits: that reporting what she saw will reach the conspirators before it reaches someone honest
that she will be reassigned away from the wall and the gap will go unwatched

entries.name: Becka Honeymead
entries.gm_notes: Becka is a mead brewer and merchant who trades honey and mead across the Valdris countryside. She has discovered that a rival merchant house with ties to Lord Cael has been systematically buying up every beekeeper's output in the region, creating a near-monopoly on honey. Honey is not just food — it is the base for medicinal salves used by the Dragon Order's healers and the only reliable preservative for field rations. By controlling the honey supply, the rival house could choke the Order's medical supply chain. Becka has been secretly organizing independent beekeepers to resist the buyouts, but the rival house has begun threatening them.

payload.summary: A shrewd mead brewer and merchant who knows that controlling honey means controlling medicine, rations, and mead — and who is quietly organizing beekeepers against a monopoly that could strangle the kingdom.
payload.appearance: Vigorous and sharp-eyed, Becka wears a merchant's travelling dress with a honey-stained apron. She carries a ledger as naturally as others carry a sword, and her handshake is firm and deliberate.

visual_identity.hair: golden brown, thick, worn in a practical plait
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a honey-bee tattoo on her left shoulder (brewer's guild mark), a faint scar on her right lip (bee-sting allergy reaction from her youth), permanently honey-stained fingernails

desires: to break the rival house's honey monopoly before it strangles the region's supply chain
to build a cooperative of independent beekeepers strong enough to resist coercion
fears_or_limits: that Lord Cael's men will target her directly once they realize she is organizing resistance
that the beekeepers she has rallied will fold under pressure and sell out

entries.name: Sable Quickthorn
entries.gm_notes: Sable is a bounty hunter and former soldier who deserted the kingdom's border forces after refusing to participate in the massacre of a refugee column. She has been living as a sellsword and bounty hunter ever since, hunting criminals for coin. She was recently offered a lucrative contract to find and capture a young halfling girl who stole a sealed letter from a nobleman in Crownhaven. Sable tracked the girl — Daisy Teasprout — but upon realizing the target is a twelve-year-old child, she stalled. She has reported that she lost the trail, buying time. Her client is growing impatient and has hinted that if she cannot retrieve the girl, others will be sent — and they will not be as gentle.

payload.summary: A deserting soldier turned bounty hunter who has tracked her target to a frightened child — and found, for the second time in her life, an order she cannot follow.
payload.appearance: Lean and hard-eyed, Sable wears worn leather armour and a dark cloak. She carries a short sword and a set of manacles on her belt — the manacles have not been used in weeks. She has the watchful stillness of a hunter, but something in her expression has softened recently.

visual_identity.hair: black, short, uneven (cut with a knife)
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a deserter's brand scratched off her left shoulder (the mark was burned in, then cut away — leaving a ragged scar), a knife scar on her right bicep, a chipped left canine

desires: to find a way to protect Daisy without exposing her own identity as a deserter
to earn enough coin to disappear to a place where no one knows her past
fears_or_limits: that the client will send less scrupulous hunters who will hurt the girl
that her own desertion will be discovered and she will be hanged

entries.name: Elspeth Thistlecorn
entries.gm_notes: Elspeth is an elderly beekeeper who tends the largest apiary in the Valdris countryside. Forty years ago, she witnessed something she has never told anyone: a dragon landed in the meadow beside her hives and simply watched her — not threatening, not bonding, just observing. The dragon had a rider, a woman in ancient armour unlike anything the Dragon Order uses, with runes etched into her plate that glowed faintly. The rider nodded to Elspeth, then flew away. Elspeth has never spoken of it because who would believe a beekeeper? But with the succession crisis and the talk of ancient bonds and forgotten history, she is beginning to wonder if what she saw was a remnant of something older than the Order — and if it matters now.

payload.summary: An old beekeeper who has tended her hives for half a century — and who saw something in the meadow forty years ago that she is only now beginning to understand might matter.
payload.appearance: Weathered and stooped but vital, Elspeth wears a wide-brimmed straw hat and a beekeeper's veil pushed back from her face. Her hands are scarred from decades of stings but still steady as she works her hives.

visual_identity.body_build: small and wiry, bent but energetic
visual_identity.hair: white, thin, under a straw hat
visual_identity.distinctive_features: old bee-sting scars on both hands and forearms, a pronounced stoop, a missing left little finger (hive accident)

desires: to understand what she saw forty years ago and whether it connects to the current crisis
to keep her apiary alive through the coming winter despite the honey monopoly squeeze
fears_or_limits: that she will die before anyone takes her memory seriously
that what she saw was a warning, and the danger it foretold is already here

entries.name: Vesper Ashlight
entries.gm_notes: Vesper is a falconer who tends hunting birds for a minor lord's estate near Dragonrest. Over the past month, her falcons have begun refusing to fly toward the northern mountains — they launch, circle, and return immediately, shrieking and agitated. This behaviour coincides with Aurelia Dawnspear's secret observation that her dragon Emberthyst is being drawn to the same mountains. Vesper does not know about Aurelia's situation, but she has her own theory: something large and predatory has established territory in the northern peaks, something that terrifies even birds of prey. She has tried to warn the local lord, who laughed and told her falcons are skittish creatures. She is now trying to reach the Dragon Order directly, but a falconer has no standing to request an audience with dragon-bonded knights.

payload.summary: A dedicated falconer whose birds refuse to fly north — and who cannot get anyone to listen when she says something terrible has taken residence in the mountains.
payload.appearance: Quiet and watchful, Vesper wears a leather falconer's gauntlet on her left arm and a simple tunic. A peregrine falcon named Ash is usually perched on her wrist. She has an stillness about her that comes from hours of patient stillness with her birds.

visual_identity.hair: dark brown, braided and pinned close to her head
visual_identity.distinctive_features: permanent talon scars on her left forearm (falconer's marks), a burn scar on her right cheek (a spark from a campfire), a calm stillness in her gaze that unsettles some people

desires: to reach the Dragon Order with her warning about whatever lies in the northern mountains
to protect her falcons from whatever is frightening them
fears_or_limits: that whatever is in the mountains is a threat to the dragons as well as the falcons
that no one will listen to a falconer until it is too late

entries.name: Lin Zhiyao
entries.gm_notes: Secretly the illegitimate daughter of the Jin warlord and a Wei court musician. Her mother was quietly 'disappeared' when Zhiyao was seven. The Jin court believes she is the orphaned niece of a minor official. She has been passing Wei military movements to a Chu spymaster named 'Grey Crane' for three years, not for money but because she believes the Jin warlord ordered her mother's death. She does not know Grey Crane is actually her half-brother.

payload.summary: A composed court lady of Jin who plays the guqin at diplomatic functions and is whispered to be the most beautiful woman in the warlord's court.
payload.appearance: Elegant and poised, always in layered silk of jade-green and ivory. Fingers callused from guqin strings. Carries a faint scent of sandalwood.

visual_identity.hair: long black hair worn in elaborate court pins
distinctive_features: a small crescent scar on the left wrist
a beauty mark beneath the right eye

desires: To learn the truth of her mother's disappearance
To one day play the guqin without fear of who is listening
fears_or_limits: Being recognized by someone who knew her mother
That Grey Crane will ask for something she cannot give

entries.name: Cao Mengshi
entries.gm_notes: She is the Wei state's foremost strategist and has authored three military treatises under a male pen name. The Wei warlord knows her true identity and deliberately keeps it secret: if rival states learned a woman commands Wei's war planning, they would underestimate Wei, which is a strategic advantage he exploits. She is slowly dying of a lung ailment from battlefield smoke inhalation and has perhaps two years left. She is training a replacement in secret.

payload.summary: A sharp-eyed scholar in Wei scholar's robes who advises the Wei warlord on military strategy and is never seen without a writing brush behind her ear.
payload.appearance: Plain-faced and practical, robes always ink-stained. Moves with deliberate economy.

visual_identity.hair: graying black, bound in a simple topknot
distinctive_features: ink stains permanently embedded in right index and middle fingers
a persistent dry cough

desires: To finish her fourth treatise before she dies
To find a worthy successor who will not be dismissed for their gender
fears_or_limits: Her illness weakening her mind before her body fails
That her pen name will outlive her real name

entries.name: Hua Suxin
entries.gm_notes: The greatest acupuncturist in Jin-an and secretly a chi-cultivation master who can sense illness in a patient's meridian flow by touch. She learned her arts from a wandering qilin-spirit monk who left her a jade needle that can actually draw corrupted chi out of a body. She has used it twice to cure 'incurable' patients and both times the extracted corruption coalesced into a small black stone she keeps in a sealed box. She fears the stones are accumulating something aware.

payload.summary: A renowned physician-acupuncturist whose clinic in Jin-an is always crowded with patients from every social class.
payload.appearance: Calm and attentive, wearing simple linen healer's robes. Always carries a silk needle roll.

visual_identity.hair: silver-streaked black, practical bun
distinctive_features: hands with unusually steady, long fingers
a faint jade-green glow in her fingertips visible only in dim light

desires: To understand what the black stones are becoming
To train an apprentice worthy of the jade needle
fears_or_limits: That the accumulated corruption in the stones is becoming sentient
Treating someone whose illness is caused by deliberate chi-poisoning

entries.name: Zhou Geha
entries.gm_notes: A river-folk (Mizuhito) canal pilot who knows every underwater passage and current in the canal network connecting Jin, Chu, and Wei territories. She smuggles people, not goods—specifically refugees and defectors fleeing the three states. She charges nothing and lives on fishing. She has personally ferried over two hundred people to safety. The Chu military has a price on her head but does not know her face, only her boat's name: 'Silent Rain.' She recently rescued a Chu noble's son who was fleeing an arranged marriage and has fallen in love with him.

payload.summary: A weathered Mizuhito boat pilot who navigates the canals between the warring states with uncanny knowledge of hidden waterways.
payload.role: Canal pilot and underground smuggler of refugees
payload.appearance: Sun-darkened and river-worn, wearing water-resistant hemp clothing and a wide bamboo hat.

visual_identity.hair: dark brown, cropped short and tied back
distinctive_features: a river-tattoo of a carp on her left forearm (Mizuhito clan mark)
a missing tip of the right ring finger

desires: To get the Chu noble's son to safety without revealing she is the smuggler he seeks
To build a permanent safe house on the marsh islands
fears_or_limits: The Chu military discovering her identity
That the boy she loves will learn she is 'Silent Rain' and feel betrayed by the secret

entries.name: Yan Qiulin
entries.gm_notes: The wife of a Chu general who has been missing on the northern front for eight months. Officially she maintains the household and raises their daughter. Unofficially, she has taken over her husband's intelligence network—the general embedded spies in Wei and Jin under the cover of tea merchants, and she now controls them. She has discovered through this network that her husband is not dead but defected to Wei voluntarily, abandoning his family for a Wei court lady. She is deciding whether to reveal this and destroy his honor or use the knowledge to build her own power base.

payload.summary: A dignified general's wife in Chu who manages her absent husband's household with quiet competence and is respected by the military wives' circle.
payload.appearance: Regal and composed, always in Chu-state crimson and gold. Carries a war-fan given by her husband.

visual_identity.hair: black with early silver threads, in a general's-wife formal coiffure
distinctive_features: a thin gold wedding bangle on the left wrist, never removed
a callus on the right thumb from archery

desires: To build enough leverage that her daughter inherits a title regardless of her husband's fate
To confront her husband face to face
fears_or_limits: Her daughter learning the truth about her father
The Chu warlord discovering she commands the spy network and viewing her as a threat

entries.name: Wei Fengge
entries.gm_notes: A calligrapher of extraordinary talent whose brushwork is said to carry chi that can calm or agitate the viewer. This is not superstition—she is an unconscious chi-cultivator who channels emotional energy into her ink. The Wei warlord has commissioned her to write victory proclamations that inflame patriotism; she has realized the proclamations are making citizens fanatically loyal and willing to die in battle. She is horrified and has begun deliberately corrupting her chi-channeling to neutralize the effect, but this is causing her own emotional numbing.

payload.summary: A celebrated calligrapher in Wei whose work hangs in government halls and is said to stir the heart of anyone who reads it.
payload.appearance: Refined and expressive, wearing flowing Wei-state blue robes. Often has ink on her sleeves and jaw.

visual_identity.hair: long black, loosely pinned with a brush-rest stick
distinctive_features: permanent ink callus on the right middle finger
a fading scar on the left palm from a childhood accident with a knife

desires: To create a work of pure beauty with no chi manipulation whatsoever
To feel genuine emotion again
fears_or_limits: Becoming permanently emotionally deadened
Someone discovering her ability and weaponizing it further

entries.name: Mei Yunlu
entries.gm_notes: A silk weaver whose loom produces fabric with patterns that seem to move in candlelight. She weaves prophetic images into ceremonial robes—a gift from a qilin spirit that visited her mother during pregnancy. She has woven three robes that depicted future battles before they occurred, and all three came true. The Jin warlord's court has noticed. She has been ordered to weave the Jin warlord's coronation robe and is terrified because the pattern forming on her loom shows the warlord's death.

payload.summary: A master silk weaver in Jin whose ceremonial robes are prized across all three states for their shimmering, living patterns.
payload.role: Master silk weaver and unconscious oracle
payload.appearance: Gentle and focused, wearing simple weave-stained clothes. Hands always moving, as if at an invisible loom.

visual_identity.hair: dark brown, braided and pinned up with wooden loom-shuttles
visual_identity.eyes: soft gray-brown, often unfocused as if listening to something distant
distinctive_features: weaver's calluses on both thumbs
a faint shimmer in her hair that catches light like silk thread

desires: To finish the coronation robe without revealing what the pattern shows
To understand and control the prophetic gift
fears_or_limits: The Jin warlord seeing the death-omen in the robe before it is finished
That altering the pattern will change fate in a worse way

entries.name: Tian Baoshan
entries.gm_notes: An iron mine foreman in the Wei mountains who discovered a vein of ore that glows faintly green and seems to strengthen chi in anyone who carries it. He has been secretly mining this 'qilin iron' and forging small ingots, selling them to martial artists at exorbitant prices. He does not know the ore is slowly poisoning the miners—three have developed a wasting sickness he has been hiding by sending them to distant clinics. He is afraid the Wei military will seize the mine if they learn of the ore's properties.

payload.summary: A burly, no-nonsense iron mine foreman in the Wei mountains who keeps his workers productive and his operations discreet.
payload.role: Iron mine foreman and secret qilin-iron dealer
payload.appearance: Stocky and soot-stained, wearing heavy leather work clothes and a miner's leather cap.

visual_identity.hair: shaved head, scarred from mine accidents
distinctive_features: a burn scar across the bridge of the nose
missing the left earlobe from a mining explosion

desires: To sell enough qilin iron to retire far from the mines
To find a cure for the miners he has poisoned before they all die
fears_or_limits: The Wei military discovering and seizing the qilin-iron vein
The poisoned miners' families learning he hid their sickness

entries.name: Su Wanqing
entries.gm_notes: A tea merchant whose tea blends are renowned across all three states. She is also the Great Academy's primary information broker—her tea caravans carry coded messages hidden in the tea packaging. She chose this life after the Academy saved her from a Wei prison where she was held for 'treasonous poetry.' She has a photographic memory for faces and conversations and can recall details from a single meeting years later. She is being courted by both Jin and Chu intelligence services and has been feeding both slightly altered versions of the same information to maintain a balance of power.

payload.summary: A genial, well-connected tea merchant whose caravans travel between all three warring states, welcomed everywhere for her superb blends.
payload.role: Tea merchant and Academy information broker
payload.appearance: Warm and round-faced, always offering tea. Wears travel-worn but quality clothes and carries sample tins.

visual_identity.hair: black streaked with white, in a practical merchant's wrap
distinctive_features: tea-stained fingertips
a small jade pendant of a lotus (Academy signal)

desires: To maintain the balance between the three states until a peace is brokered
To retire to a tea farm and never carry a secret again
fears_or_limits: Both intelligence services realizing she is feeding them manipulated data
A coded message being intercepted and decoded

entries.name: Lu Haichen
entries.gm_notes: A martial arts teacher at the Great Academy who teaches swordsmanship but is secretly a pacifist who has never killed anyone. He won his reputation through tournament fighting—always non-lethal. He was conscripted by the Chu warlord three years ago to lead a raid and refused; he was stripped of his Chu rank and fled to the Academy. He teaches students to defend without killing and has developed a fighting style that disarms and incapacitates. The Chu warlord has sent assassins twice, and both times Lu disarmed them and sent them home alive, which infuriates the warlord more than killing them would have.

payload.summary: A calm, disciplined sword instructor at the Great Academy known for a fighting style that defeats opponents without lethal force.
payload.role: Martial arts teacher and philosophical pacifist
payload.appearance: Centered and unhurried, wearing simple Academy gray. Always has a wooden practice sword at his side.

visual_identity.hair: black, short-cropped for practicality
distinctive_features: a faint scar across the left cheekbone from a tournament bout
hands with knuckles callused from decades of wooden-sword practice

desires: To prove that non-lethal combat can change how the three states wage war
To be left in peace by the Chu warlord
fears_or_limits: Being forced to kill to protect a student
That his pacifism is actually cowardice he has dressed in philosophy

entries.name: Bai Shuyi
entries.gm_notes: An archivist at the Great Academy who has discovered a sealed scroll repository beneath the library containing pre-war records from before the three states split. The records reveal that the original unified kingdom fell not through conquest but through a deliberate chi-ritual gone wrong—a ritual the current warlords' ancestors attempted to harness a qilin spirit's power. The ritual shattered the kingdom and scattered qilin spirits across the land. If this knowledge became public, it would undermine the legitimacy of all three warlords. She has been slowly copying the records and hiding the copies in different locations, preparing for the day she must release them.

payload.summary: A quiet, meticulous archivist at the Great Academy's grand library who knows every shelf, scroll, and secret catalog by heart.
payload.role: Senior archivist and keeper of forbidden history
payload.appearance: Bookish and unobtrusive, always in Academy brown robes. Carries a scroll-case and reading spectacles.

visual_identity.body_build: slight and slightly stooped from years at reading desks
visual_identity.hair: white, in a tight bun
distinctive_features: a large ink-stain birthmark on the right jaw
fingers stained with old ink from handling ancient scrolls

desires: To release the truth when the time is right and end the warlords' false legitimacy
To protect the Academy from retaliation when the truth comes out
fears_or_limits: The warlords learning of the hidden repository and destroying the records
Dying before she finishes copying everything

entries.name: Jiang Niwa
entries.gm_notes: A potter whose clay vessels can hold chi-infused liquids without degrading. She discovered this when a physician asked her to make a vessel for a medicinal chi-potion and the potion retained potency for months instead of days. She has been secretly supplying chi-stable vessels to Hua Suxin the acupuncturist. She does not understand why her clay works this way—she uses river clay from a specific bend in the canal that she suspects is near an old qilin-spirit site. She is illiterate and has never told anyone the location of her clay source.

payload.summary: A skilled village potter whose ceramics are valued for their beauty and inexplicable ability to preserve medicinal chi-potions.
payload.role: Master potter and unknowing qilin-clay guardian
payload.appearance: Earth-stained and practical, wearing clay-spattered work clothes and a kiln-scarred apron.

visual_identity.body_build: strong-armed and compact from years at the wheel
visual_identity.hair: dark brown, tied in a cloth band
distinctive_features: kiln-burn scars on both forearms
clay permanently embedded in the creases of her hands

desires: To keep her clay source secret and safe
To make one perfect vessel worthy of a qilin spirit's attention
fears_or_limits: Someone following her to the clay bend and destroying it
That the clay's power comes at a cost she does not yet understand

entries.name: Shen Wuguang
entries.gm_notes: A Chu court official who has been managing the warlord's treasury for fifteen years. He has been skimming a small percentage of war taxes and funneling the money into a hidden orphanage he runs in a Chu farming village. The orphanage houses forty children orphaned by Chu's wars. He views his embezzlement as moral restitution. The Chu warlord's new auditor is meticulous and getting close to the discrepancy. Shen has a plan to frame a rival official for the theft but it would destroy an innocent man's life.

payload.summary: A meticulous, silver-tongued treasury official in the Chu court who manages war taxes with scrupulous—appearing—precision.
payload.role: Court treasury official and secret orphanage patron
payload.appearance: Immaculate and soft-spoken, wearing Chu-state formal robes of dark red. Always carries a counting frame.

visual_identity.hair: thin gray, oiled and formal
distinctive_features: a wen on the right temple
an abacus-callus on the right thumb

desires: To protect the forty orphans regardless of cost
To outmaneuver the new auditor without destroying an innocent colleague
fears_or_limits: The orphans being discovered and conscripted into the Chu army
That his moral justification for theft is just self-deception

entries.name: Chen Xiuran
entries.gm_notes: A herbalist who lives at the edge of the Wei mountains and gathers rare medicinal herbs. She is the only person who knows the location of the 'Ghost Orchid,' a flower that blooms once every twelve years and can cure any poison—including the chi-wasting sickness afflicting Tian Baoshan's miners. She was the lover of one of the poisoned miners and does not know he is ill because he was sent away. She has been visited by a qilin spirit in the form of a white deer that guards the Ghost Orchid grove and has told her the flower must not be picked for 'petty human wars.' She is torn between the spirit's warning and saving lives.

payload.summary: A solitary herbalist who lives at the forest edge near the Wei mountains, known for rare remedies that no apothecary can replicate.
payload.appearance: Wild-haired and forest-worn, wearing layered patched clothes and carrying baskets of drying herbs.

visual_identity.body_build: lean and weathered from mountain living
visual_identity.hair: long, dark, and untamed
distinctive_features: mud-stained fingers with green herbal stains
a necklace of small animal bones and dried seed pods

desires: To find a way to save the miners without defying the qilin spirit
To be reunited with her poisoned lover
fears_or_limits: The qilin spirit abandoning the grove if she disobeys
That the Ghost Orchid's next blooming will be the last

entries.name: Tan Ruolan
entries.gm_notes: A fortune teller in Jin-an's market district who reads palms and tortoise shells. She is genuinely gifted—her readings are accurate about seventy percent of the time, a gift from a qilin-spirit encounter in childhood. She has read the palms of three of the Jin warlord's inner circle and knows that a coup is being planned for the autumn festival. She has not told anyone because the last time she tried to warn a powerful person, her family was killed in reprisal. She is now weighing whether to warn the warlord (who she despises) to save innocent festival-goers who might die in the violence.

payload.summary: A popular fortune teller in Jin-an's market whose palm readings are eerily accurate, drawing clients from all social classes.
payload.appearance: Mystical and theatrical in market-performers' robes, draped in auspicious charms. Eyes that seem to look through people.

visual_identity.hair: black with gray streaks, loose and talisman-pinned
visual_identity.eyes: very dark, slightly unsettling in their intensity
distinctive_features: a tortoise-shell burn scar on the right palm from divination rites
a white streak in the left temple hair

desires: To warn someone about the coup without endangering herself
To be free of the gift that got her family killed
fears_or_limits: Her warning reaching the coup plotters
That her vision of the coup is one of her thirty-percent wrong readings

entries.name: Duan Lizi
entries.gm_notes: A noodle vendor in Jin-an's market who served a bowl of noodles to a dying man who whispered a military secret into his soup before expiring. The secret: the Wei military is building a fleet of chi-powered war barges on a hidden canal tributary. Duan is illiterate and cannot write the secret down, and he does not understand its significance. He has told no one because he is afraid of being interrogated. He keeps replaying the dying man's words in his head and is increasingly paranoid that someone is watching his stall.

payload.summary: A cheerful, bustling noodle vendor in Jin-an's market whose steaming bowls are a daily comfort to merchants, soldiers, and laborers.
payload.appearance: Round and ruddy, always steaming and wiping his hands on his apron. Laughs easily and loudly.

visual_identity.hair: mostly bald with a fringe of gray
visual_identity.eyes: small, brown, crinkled with laugh lines
distinctive_features: a soup-burn scar on the left forearm
flour permanently dusting his shoulders and sleeves

desires: To forget the dying man's words and go back to just making noodles
To tell someone trustworthy and be rid of the burden
fears_or_limits: Being identified as the last person the spy spoke to
That his stall is being watched and he cannot tell by whom

entries.name: Guo Mingyue
entries.gm_notes: A jade carver whose work is sought after by all three courts. She has discovered that a specific type of jade, when carved with precise geometric patterns, can store and release chi in controlled bursts. She has created three such 'chi-jade' pieces: one amplifies physical strength, one enhances mental clarity, and one accelerates healing. She has given the healing piece secretly to a rebel faction that opposes all three warlords. She is a member of that faction—the 'Jade Restoration'—which seeks to reunify the states through cultural rather than military power. Her faction is small but includes influential scholars and artisans.

payload.summary: A master jade carver in Jin-an whose intricate pieces are prized by all three warring courts for their beauty and rumored spiritual properties.
payload.role: Master jade carver and Jade Restoration operative
payload.appearance: Precise and self-contained, wearing fine craftsman's robes. Hands always still and deliberate.

visual_identity.hair: black, in a neat carver's topknot
distinctive_features: jade-dust stains in the cuticles
a faint white scar on the right thumb from a carving slip

desires: To see the three states reunified without more bloodshed
To create a chi-jade piece powerful enough to end a battle single-handedly
fears_or_limits: The warlords discovering the chi-jade technology and weaponizing it
The Jade Restoration being infiltrated by state agents

entries.name: Feng Qiaomu
entries.gm_notes: A rice farmer whose paddies sit at the border where Jin, Chu, and Wei territories meet. Her farm has been raided by soldiers from all three states, each demanding her rice as 'taxation.' She has developed a system of hidden underground grain stores and has been secretly feeding a growing community of deserters from all three armies who live in the marshlands nearby. The deserters have formed a small settlement they call 'No Flag Village.' She is their sole food supplier and the village would starve without her. She is beginning to dream of the village becoming a true sanctuary—neutral ground.

payload.summary: A weathered rice farmer at the tri-border who feeds soldiers from all three armies and grumbles about every one of them.
payload.role: Rice farmer and secret provider for deserters' sanctuary
payload.appearance: Sun-browned and strong, wearing mud-stained farmer's clothes and a woven rice-straw hat.

visual_identity.body_build: sturdy and broad-hipped from years of field labor
visual_identity.hair: dark brown, gray at the temples, in a tight braid
visual_identity.eyes: warm brown, crow's feet from squinting at the sun
distinctive_features: deep tan lines from the rice-straw hat
a faded scar on the left shin from a plow accident

desires: To see No Flag Village recognized as neutral territory by all three states
To harvest a full season's crop without soldiers taking it
fears_or_limits: The three armies discovering the deserter settlement and slaughtering them as traitors
Her hidden grain stores being found during a military search

entries.name: Mo Chenyu
entries.gm_notes: A Jin palace guard captain who has served the warlord for twenty years. She discovered that the warlord's chief advisor has been replacing palace guards loyal to the warlord with guards loyal to the advisor's own faction—a slow coup. She reported this to the warlord, who dismissed it as paranoia. She now realizes the warlord already knows and is allowing the infiltration to identify the full conspiracy before acting. She is the only guard the warlord trusts, and she has been tasked with quietly gathering evidence. The advisor suspects her loyalty and has assigned two of his own men to watch her.

payload.summary: A stern, battle-scarred captain of the Jin palace guard who is trusted by the warlord and feared by the court for her unflinching discipline.
payload.role: Palace guard captain and the warlord's hidden investigator
payload.appearance: Imposing and armor-ready, wearing Jin-state guard uniform of dark green and black. Always armed.

visual_identity.hair: black, cropped to the jaw, practical
distinctive_features: a sword scar from left brow to cheekbone
a missing tip of the left little finger

desires: To expose the advisor's conspiracy before it turns violent
To protect the warlord despite her private doubts about his leadership
fears_or_limits: The advisor's watchers discovering her evidence before it is complete
That the warlord is using her as bait and will sacrifice her to catch the conspiracy

entries.name: Yun Bixin
entries.gm_notes: A musician at the Great Academy who plays the dizi (bamboo flute) and is one of the few living practitioners of 'spirit music'—melodies that can attract or repel qilin spirits. She learned this art from her grandmother, who was the last court spirit-musician of the unified kingdom before it split. Her flute was carved from bamboo that grew at a qilin-spirit site and can produce notes that make spirits visible to ordinary humans. She has been asked by the Academy to summon a qilin spirit for a research project but fears that summoning spirits for academic purposes is a violation of an ancient compact between humans and qilin.

payload.summary: A gifted Academy musician whose bamboo flute playing is said to make the air shimmer and the heart ache with unnamed longing.
payload.role: Spirit musician and keeper of ancient melodies
payload.appearance: Ethereal and quiet, wearing Academy gray-white robes. Always carries a pale bamboo flute.

visual_identity.hair: long black, loose except when performing
distinctive_features: a faint blue-tinged birthmark on the left collarbone shaped like a musical note
flute-callus on the lower lip

desires: To preserve the spirit-music tradition before it dies with her
To understand the ancient compact between humans and qilin
fears_or_limits: Breaking the compact by summoning a spirit for the Academy's research
That the spirits will stop answering if humans misuse the music

entries.name: Qin Baotian
entries.gm_notes: A Jin army general who has won seven battles and lost none. The secret: before each battle, his sister—a chi-cultivator nun at a mountain monastery—performs a ritual that channels aggressive chi into his soldiers through specially prepared war-banners. The chi makes them fearless and strong but burns out their long-term health; soldiers who survive his battles age rapidly and rarely live past forty. He does not know this. His sister has not told him because she believes the war must be won. He is beginning to notice his veterans wasting away and is investigating.

payload.summary: A celebrated Jin general, tall and commanding, whose string of victories has made him the warlord's most trusted military leader.
payload.role: Jin army general and unknowing beneficiary of chi-warfare
payload.appearance: Commanding and immaculate in Jin-state military uniform of dark green and gold. Carries a legendary war-halberd.

visual_identity.hair: black, cropped short under a military topknot
distinctive_features: a war-halberd scar across the right palm
a gold victory medal tattooed on the left forearm (Jin military tradition)

desires: To understand why his veterans are aging and dying prematurely
To win the war and earn the warlord's promise of land and retirement
fears_or_limits: Discovering his victories are built on his sister's chi-sacrifice of his men
That the warlord views his popularity among soldiers as a threat

entries.name: Ouyang Shuang
entries.gm_notes: A painter whose landscape paintings are so detailed they have been used as military maps by the Chu warlord's scouts—unbeknownst to her. She paints from observation and has traveled the tri-border region extensively. She is a Chu loyalist who believes she is documenting the beauty of the land for posterity. She has unknowingly painted the locations of Jin military supply routes, Wei fortification weaknesses, and the hidden canal paths used by the smuggler 'Silent Rain.' The Jin intelligence service has identified her paintings as a security breach and has dispatched agents to confiscate her work and silence her.

payload.summary: A wandering landscape painter from Chu whose breathtaking scrolls capture the rivers, mountains, and cities of all three states in vivid detail.
payload.role: Master painter and unwitting intelligence source
payload.appearance: Free-spirited and paint-stained, wearing travel-worn scholar-artist robes. Carries a bulky scroll-pack and brush case.

visual_identity.body_build: tall and lean from constant travel
visual_identity.hair: dark, loose, and perpetually paint-flecked
distinctive_features: paint stains in permanent rings around the right wrist
a sun-faded tan line from a hat she rarely wears

desires: To paint a definitive atlas of the three states' landscapes before the war destroys them
To have her work recognized as art, not espionage
fears_or_limits: The Jin agents finding her before she realizes the danger
That her art has already caused military casualties

entries.name: Lin Jiaojiao
entries.gm_notes: An eleven-year-old girl who is the strongest unconscious chi-cultivator the Great Academy has seen in a century. She accidentally shattered a stone table during a tantrum at age eight and has been hidden by her parents—humble paper makers—ever since. The Academy sent a scout who found her and discreetly offered a scholarship, but the Jin warlord's chi-cultivation corps also heard rumors and wants to conscript her as a living weapon. Her parents are trying to get her to the Academy before the warlord's agents arrive. She does not understand her power and is terrified of herself.

payload.summary: A small, quiet girl of eleven with enormous dark eyes who tries very hard to be good and very hard not to break things.
payload.role: Child chi-prodigy and object of a three-way search
payload.appearance: Small for her age and wiry, wearing simple paper-maker's child clothes. Always looks slightly apologetic.

visual_identity.hair: black, in two simple braids
distinctive_features: a faint lattice of hairline cracks across the palms (from channeling chi)
a small chip in the right front tooth

desires: To stop being afraid of her own hands
To stay with her parents and make paper like a normal child
fears_or_limits: Hurting someone she loves with her power
Being taken away and turned into a weapon

entries.name: Zhao Tiegun
entries.gm_notes: A blacksmith who forges weapons for the Chu army and has secretly developed a method to fold qilin-iron into ordinary steel, creating blades that hold a chi-edge three times sharper than normal. He is selling these enhanced weapons on the black market to fighters from all three states. He does not know the qilin-iron comes from Tian Baoshan's mine, and he does not know the iron is poisonous. His enhanced blades are slowly killing their wielders through the same chi-wasting sickness affecting the miners. He is being investigated by the Chu army's quartermaster for quality inconsistencies in army-issue blades.

payload.summary: A broad-shouldered Chu blacksmith whose forge produces army blades by day and secretive high-quality weapons by night.
payload.role: Army blacksmith and secret qilin-iron weapons dealer
payload.appearance: Soot-blackened and taciturn, wearing a heavy leather forge-apron. Arms like tree trunks.

visual_identity.hair: shaved, scarred from forge-sparks
distinctive_features: extensive forge-burn scarring on both forearms and hands
a thick blacksmith's callus on the right palm

desires: To perfect the qilin-iron folding technique and create a legendary blade
To earn enough to open a legitimate forge far from the war
fears_or_limits: Discovering his enhanced blades are killing their owners
The Chu quartermaster tracing the black-market weapons back to his forge

entries.name: Xu Anwen
entries.gm_notes: A paper maker from a family of paper makers who has developed a method to infuse paper with chi, creating 'spirit paper' that can hold written spells and activate them when read. This is the technology behind the Jin warlord's chi-propaganda proclamations—Wei Fengge's chi-infused calligraphy is written on Xu's spirit paper, which is why the emotional manipulation works. Xu does not know her paper is being used for propaganda; she was commissioned by the Jin court to make 'fine ceremonial paper' and was not told its purpose. She has recently seen one of the proclamations and recognized her paper, and the calligraphy's unsettling emotional effect has made her suspect something is wrong.

payload.summary: A skilled paper maker from a long line of paper makers whose fine ceremonial paper is prized by the Jin court for important documents.
payload.role: Paper maker and unknowing supplier of chi-propaganda technology
payload.appearance: Patient and earthy, wearing paper-maker's work clothes stained with pulp. Hands always slightly damp from pulp.

visual_identity.hair: dark, wrapped in a cloth headband
distinctive_features: permanently pruned fingertips from working in water
a pulp-stain birthmark on the right wrist

desires: To discover what the Jin court is doing with her paper
To reclaim her family's paper-making legacy from military use
fears_or_limits: The Jin court silencing her if she asks too many questions
That her paper has been used to manipulate thousands of people

entries.name: Niu Caihong
entries.gm_notes: An elderly beggar woman in Jin-an who is actually a retired chi-cultivation master who faked her death twenty years ago to escape the Jin warlord's father, who wanted to conscript her into his war machine. She lives as a street beggar because it is the last place anyone would look for a master cultivator. She watches over the street children of Jin-an and has quietly taught basic chi-centering to a dozen of them to help them survive. One of her students has shown prodigy-level talent and she is deciding whether to train the child fully or push them away to protect them from her past.

payload.summary: A wrinkled, seemingly frail beggar woman who sits by the market well and watches the world with unsettlingly clear eyes.
payload.role: Disguised chi-cultivation master and protector of street children
payload.appearance: Small and hunched in layered dirty rags, but with eyes that are too clear and a stillness that does not match her apparent frailty.

visual_identity.body_build: small, hunched, deceptively solid beneath the rags
visual_identity.hair: thin white, under a ragged head wrap
distinctive_features: a web of fine scars on the hands (old chi-training marks)
a barely visible, perfectly circular callus on each palm (cultivation seat-mark)

desires: To train the talented street child without bringing the warlord's attention
To die as herself, not as the weapon the old warlord wanted
fears_or_limits: The Jin warlord discovering his father's lost cultivator is alive
That training the child will repeat the cycle she fled

entries.name: Mizuhito Taro
entries.gm_notes: A Mizuhito fisherman who tends eel traps in the canal junction and has witnessed a Wei military construction project through the mist: workers building chi-powered war barges on a hidden tributary. He does not understand what he saw but described the 'glowing boats' to Zhou Geha, who recognized the military significance. He is now Zhou Geha's unwitting eyes on the canal. He is simple-hearted and loyal to Zhou and does not realize he is part of an intelligence chain. The Wei military has posted guards on the tributary, and one guard noticed Taro's boat and reported it.

payload.summary: A cheerful Mizuhito fisherman who works the canal junctions and knows the waterways like the lines on his own hands.
payload.role: Canal fisherman and unwitting intelligence asset
payload.appearance: Weathered and easy-smiling, wearing Mizuhito water-gear and a woven reed hat. Always smells of canal water and eel oil.

visual_identity.hair: gray-black, cropped close
distinctive_features: a Mizuhito river-tattoo of a water-serpent on the right forearm
a hook-scar on the left index finger

desires: To keep fishing and help Zhou when she asks
To see the canals clean and peaceful again
fears_or_limits: Wei soldiers finding his boat near the forbidden tributary
That his reports to Zhou are putting him in danger he does not understand

entries.name: Han Xueling
entries.gm_notes: A dancer in the Chu court who performs at state banquets and is the Chu warlord's favorite entertainer. She is also the daughter of a Jin spy who was executed by the Chu warlord fifteen years ago. She was spared because she was five years old and the warlord did not know her parentage. She has known the truth since she was sixteen and has spent her entire adult life positioning herself as the warlord's trusted performer to get close enough to kill him. She has a poisoned hairpin and has rehearsed the assassination a hundred times in her mind. She has never gone through with it because the warlord's young son is often present, and she cannot bear to orphan a child the way she was orphaned.

payload.summary: A mesmerizing court dancer in Chu whose performances at state banquets leave audiences spellbound and the warlord entranced.
payload.appearance: Luminous and expressive, wearing Chu-state performance silks of crimson and gold. Moves like water and smoke.

visual_identity.hair: long black, worn in performance coils and cascades
distinctive_features: a dancer's callus on the balls of both feet
a tiny, faded scar on the left jaw from a childhood fall

desires: To avenge her father without creating another orphan
To find a way to leave the Chu court alive
fears_or_limits: Killing the warlord in front of his son
That the warlord's trust in her is turning to love, which complicates everything

entries.name: Kang Wenzhao
entries.gm_notes: A scholar at the Great Academy specializing in pre-war political philosophy. He has written a treatise arguing that the three-state division is illegitimate and that the unified kingdom should be restored—not by conquest but by a council of scholars. The treatise has circulated secretly among Academy scholars and is gaining support. The Jin warlord has obtained a copy and considers it treasonous. Kang does not know the warlord has read it. He has been invited to a 'scholarly symposium' at the Jin court, which is actually a trap to arrest him. The Academy has suspicions but no proof.

payload.summary: A passionate, idealistic Academy scholar whose writings on reunification have made him a hero among students and a target among warlords.
payload.appearance: Earnest and slightly rumpled, wearing Academy scholar's robes with ink on the cuffs. Always carrying scrolls.

visual_identity.body_build: medium and slightly soft from scholarly life
visual_identity.hair: black, in a scholar's topknot, often loosening
distinctive_features: a scholar's ink-stain on the left jaw
a slight stoop from years at writing desks

desires: To see the reunification council become reality
To protect the students who follow his philosophy from warlord retaliation
fears_or_limits: The Jin 'symposium' invitation being a trap he cannot refuse without confirming his treason
That his idealism will get his students killed

entries.name: Ai Gulan
entries.gm_notes: A servant in the Wei warlord's household who has been spying for the Jin state for six years. She was recruited after Jin agents rescued her daughter from a Wei prison. Her handler threatens to stop protecting her daughter if she stops spying. She hates the Jin state and everything it has made her do. She has been passing Wei military secrets that have led to Jin victories and Wei deaths, including the death of a Wei guard who was kind to her. She has decided to find a way to feed Jin false information that will get her daughter freed without more blood on her hands, but this requires finding a way to contact Jin's handler without being detected.

payload.summary: A quiet, unobtrusive servant in the Wei warlord's household who cleans rooms, serves tea, and is never noticed or remembered.
payload.role: Palace servant and coerced Jin spy
payload.appearance: Plain and deliberately forgettable, wearing servant's gray. Moves silently and keeps her head down.

visual_identity.hair: dull black, in a tight servant's bun
visual_identity.eyes: dark brown, downcast but missing nothing
distinctive_features: a servant's rope-burn callus on both wrists from years of carrying water
a small, old scar on the left cheekbone

desires: To free her daughter from Jin's control and stop spying
To find a way to atone for the deaths her information caused
fears_or_limits: Her Jin handler harming her daughter if she disobeys
The Wei warlord discovering her espionage and executing her publicly

entries.name: Luo Shufen
entries.gm_notes: A cook in the Great Academy's kitchens who has been feeding the Academy community for thirty years and knows every student, teacher, and visitor by their food preferences. She is the Academy's unofficial counselor—students confide in her over bowls of soup. She has pieced together from hundreds of conversations that the Academy's headmaster is being coerced by the Jin warlord to subtly steer Academy research toward military applications. She has not told anyone because the headmaster is her oldest friend and she believes he is trying to protect the Academy. She has begun leaving anonymous notes in the headmaster's meals suggesting resistance strategies.

payload.summary: A warm, motherly cook in the Great Academy kitchens whose soups are legendary and whose ear is always open.
payload.appearance: Round and flour-dusted, wearing a cook's apron and head wrap. Always smells of star anise and ginger.

visual_identity.hair: white, under a cook's head wrap
distinctive_features: a cook's burn-scar on the right wrist
a small mole on the left jaw

desires: To help the headmaster find a way to resist the warlord's coercion
To protect the students who confide in her from being used as pawns
fears_or_limits: The headmaster discovering she is the anonymous note-writer and feeling humiliated
That her notes will lead the headmaster into a confrontation he cannot survive

entries.name: Tang Ruixiang
entries.gm_notes: An acrobat and street performer who travels the tri-border region with a small troupe. Her acrobatic troupe is actually a spy ring: they perform at festivals and military camps, and during performances, one member distracts while another steals documents. Tang is the leader and the best pickpocket. She was a Chu army brat who deserted after being ordered to burn a village. Her troupe sells intelligence to all three states but favors whichever is currently losing, to prolong the war and weaken all sides. She has recently stolen a document describing a secret meeting between Jin and Wei warlords to coordinate a joint invasion of Chu.

payload.summary: A dazzling acrobat and troupe leader whose performances across the three states draw crowds and applause wherever she goes.
payload.role: Acrobat troupe leader and master spy-thief
payload.appearance: Vibrant and athletic, wearing performer's bright silks. Laughs loudly and moves with impossible grace.

visual_identity.hair: black, in a performer's high ponytail with red ribbons
distinctive_features: a performer's callus on the right shoulder from acrobatic lifts
a small knife-scar on the left forearm from a close-call theft

desires: To find a buyer for the Jin-Wei alliance document who will use it to prevent the Chu invasion
To keep her troupe safe and free
fears_or_limits: A troupe member being captured and revealing the spy ring
That selling to the highest bidder has made her complicit in deaths she cannot justify

entries.name: Miao Qingci
entries.gm_notes: A physician at the Great Academy's medical hall who specializes in chi-pathology—the study of how chi disruption causes disease. She has identified a new illness she calls 'spirit-drift' affecting people who live near old qilin-spirit sites: their chi gradually detaches from their bodies, causing dissociation, memory loss, and eventually coma. She has traced the illness to the three warlords' ancestor-ritual, which scattered qilin spirits and destabilized the chi-meridians of the land itself. She has twelve patients in varying stages of spirit-drift and is running out of time to find a treatment. She has not published her findings because the conclusions would be politically explosive.

payload.summary: A precise, compassionate Academy physician who researches chi-based illnesses and treats patients that other healers cannot diagnose.
payload.appearance: Neat and focused, wearing Academy medical robes of gray-white. Carries a diagnostic case with chi-sensing tools.

visual_identity.hair: black, in a medical-practitioner's clean bun
distinctive_features: a physician's chi-sense callus on both index fingertips
a faint scar on the left thumb from a dissection accident

desires: To find a treatment for spirit-drift before her twelve patients progress to coma
To publish her findings despite the political danger
fears_or_limits: The warlords suppressing her research to protect their ancestor-ritual legitimacy
That the treatment requires a qilin spirit's willing cooperation, which may be impossible to obtain

entries.name: Yang Fuhai
entries.gm_notes: A canal worker and Mizuhito elder who has maintained the canal locks at the tri-border junction for forty years. He knows the original canal blueprints, which include sealed channels that predate the three-state division—channels that could bypass all three states' military checkpoints. He has been approached by Zhou Geha to reveal the sealed channels' locations for refugee smuggling. He refused because the sealed channels are rigged with ancient chi-mechanisms that flood if opened incorrectly, and the knowledge was entrusted to his family by the old unified kingdom's canal authority. He is the last person alive who knows the mechanism codes.

payload.summary: A weathered Mizuhito canal lock-keeper whose understanding of the waterways is encyclopedic and whose loyalty to the old ways is absolute.
payload.role: Canal lock-keeper and keeper of sealed-channel secrets
payload.appearance: Old and river-worn, wearing Mizuhito canal-worker's garb and a faded official's sash from the old kingdom. Works methodically.

visual_identity.body_build: wiry and sinewy, aged but strong
visual_identity.hair: white, thin, under a canal-keeper's cap
distinctive_features: a Mizuhito river-tattoo of a lock-gate on both forearms (master lock-keeper mark)
a permanently crooked left ring finger from a lock-chain accident

desires: To pass the sealed-channel codes to someone worthy before he dies
To see the canals used for trade and life, not war
fears_or_limits: The wrong person learning the codes and flooding the canals deliberately
Dying without passing on the knowledge and the channels being forced open destructively

entries.name: Xie Mengxue
entries.gm_notes: A young woman who was the Wei warlord's personal chi-cultivation student until she discovered that the warlord's training method involved draining chi from prisoners to fuel his students' advancement. She escaped the Wei palace, taking evidence of the chi-draining practice—a bloodstained cultivation manual. She is now hiding in Jin-an under a false name, working as a laundress. The Wei warlord has sent his best chi-cultivator to retrieve her and the manual. She has sought refuge at the Great Academy but has not yet revealed what she knows because she is terrified the Academy will hand her back to Wei to avoid a diplomatic incident.

payload.summary: A quiet, watchful young woman working as a laundress in Jin-an who flinches at loud noises and watches doors.
payload.appearance: Nondescript and deliberately plain, wearing laundress's clothes. Hands red and rough from lye soap. Moves quietly and stays near exits.

visual_identity.hair: dye-darkened brown (naturally lighter), in a tight laundress bun
distinctive_features: chi-cultivation calluses on both palms (inconsistent with a laundress's hands)
a faded Wei-state cultivation corps brand on the inside of the left wrist

desires: To find safety and someone trustworthy to give the cultivation manual to
To expose the Wei warlord's chi-draining without being killed
fears_or_limits: The Wei cultivator finding her before she reaches safety
The Academy returning her to Wei as a diplomatic gesture

entries.name: Qiu Yuanshan
entries.gm_notes: A retired Jin army sergeant who lost his left hand to a Wei sword at the Battle of Red Marsh. He runs a small restaurant in Jin-an that is a gathering place for veterans from all three states—he serves anyone who leaves their weapons at the door. He has unofficially become a mediator between veteran communities, and his restaurant is where deserters from No Flag Village sometimes come for news and supplies. He has been approached by the Jin warlord's representative to report on 'disloyal elements' among his veteran patrons. He agreed, but is actually feeding the warlord false information to protect the deserter network.

payload.summary: A gruff, one-handed veteran who runs a humble restaurant in Jin-an where soldiers from all three states eat in uneasy truce.
payload.appearance: Stocky and scarred, wearing a cook's apron over an old military undershirt. Left arm ends at the wrist in a leather cap.

visual_identity.hair: cropped gray, military style
distinctive_features: left hand missing, wrist capped in leather
a network of battle scars across the chest and back (visible when sleeves roll)

desires: To protect the deserter network and his veteran community
To see the restaurant remain neutral ground where enemies can share a meal
fears_or_limits: The Jin warlord realizing his reports are false
A fight breaking out in the restaurant between rival-state veterans that he cannot stop one-handed

entries.name: Zheng Lianshu
entries.gm_notes: A librarian at the Great Academy who manages the student reading rooms. She has noticed that someone has been systematically removing and replacing pages from historical texts about the qilin-spirit ritual that split the kingdom. The tampering alters the texts to make the warlords' ancestors appear as heroes rather than perpetrators of the failed ritual. She has compared the tampered texts with Bai Shuyi's archivist copies and confirmed the alterations. She does not know who is doing the tampering—a faculty member with after-hours access, or an infiltrator. She has set a trap: she has marked several texts with a chi-reactive ink that will stain the hands of the next person who handles them.

payload.summary: A meticulous, bespectacled Academy librarian who keeps the reading rooms perfectly organized and notices every misplaced page.
payload.appearance: Neat and attentive, wearing Academy brown with a librarian's reading chain. Always has a list and a pen.

visual_identity.hair: black, in a neat librarian's bun with reading-glasses chain
distinctive_features: a paper-cut scar on the right thumb
a faint ink-stain on the left jaw that never quite fades

desires: To catch the tamperer and expose the historical revisionism
To restore the altered texts to their original content
fears_or_limits: The tamperer being a senior faculty member she cannot confront safely
That the chi-reactive ink trap will catch an innocent student and damage her credibility

entries.name: Pan Yaqing
entries.gm_notes: A Chu court official's daughter who was betrothed to the Chu general who defected to Wei—Yan Qiulin's missing husband. Pan and the general had a secret affair before his defection, and she helped him plan his escape, believing he would send for her. He never did. She has learned through Yan Qiulin's spy network (which she has infiltrated) that the general abandoned both women. Pan is now playing a dangerous double game: she maintains her position in Chu court society while secretly feeding information to Yan Qiulin's spy network, not out of loyalty but to position herself to destroy the general who betrayed her.

payload.summary: A poised, socially connected young woman in the Chu court who navigates balls, banquets, and alliances with effortless charm.
payload.appearance: Polished and fashion-forward, wearing Chu-state court silks of deep red. Always perfectly composed.

visual_identity.hair: long black, in elaborate court styles
visual_identity.eyes: dark brown, warm on the surface, calculating beneath
distinctive_features: a small jade Chu-court pendant at the throat
a nervous habit of pressing the right thumbnail into the left palm

desires: To personally confront and destroy the general who betrayed her
To build a life and identity that does not depend on any man
fears_or_limits: Yan Qiulin discovering she was the general's lover and viewing her as an enemy
The Chu court discovering her connection to the defected general

entries.name: Cui Zhenbo
entries.gm_notes: A Jin court physician who serves the warlord's family and is one of the few people who knows the Jin warlord is slowly being poisoned. The poison is chi-based and undetectable by normal examination—it mimics the symptoms of natural aging. Cui identified it because he studied under the same master as Hua Suxin and recognizes chi-pathology. He has not told the warlord because he suspects the poisoner is the warlord's own son, the crown prince, who stands to inherit. Cui is treating the warlord's symptoms with chi-countermeasures that slow the poisoning but cannot stop it. He has perhaps six months before the warlord's condition becomes visibly serious.

payload.summary: A dignified, silver-bearded court physician in the Jin palace who has tended the warlord's family for two decades.
payload.role: Court physician and keeper of a poisoning secret
payload.appearance: Distinguished and grave, wearing fine Jin court physician's robes. Moves with a physician's careful deliberateness.

visual_identity.hair: white, full, in a physician's formal topknot with a silver pin
distinctive_features: a physician's pulse-callus on all three fingers of the right hand
a faint liver-spot map across the brow

desires: To confirm whether the crown prince is the poisoner before the warlord dies
To find an antidote that does not require revealing the poisoning to the court
fears_or_limits: Accusing the crown prince wrongly and being executed for treason
That the warlord will die and the poisoner will inherit before Cui can act

entries.name: Fang Yuwan
entries.gm_notes: A Mizuhito boat builder who constructs canal boats using a technique passed down through her family for generations: planks sealed with a chi-infused resin that makes the boats nearly silent in the water. Her family's boats are the preferred vessels of smugglers and intelligence couriers because they cannot be heard approaching in the dark. She does not ask what her boats are used for—she builds for anyone who pays. She has recently been commissioned to build a fleet of twenty silent boats by a buyer who will not give their name, and the specifications match military assault craft. She suspects a state is preparing a canal-based invasion and is debating whether to build the boats or sabotage the commission.

payload.summary: A skilled Mizuhito boat builder whose canal craft are prized for their speed, durability, and uncanny silence on the water.
payload.role: Boat builder and unwilling military supplier
payload.appearance: Practical and wood-shaving-dusted, wearing Mizuhito boat-builder's leather work clothes. Strong hands, measuring eye.

visual_identity.body_build: strong-armed and broad-backed from years of plank-bending
visual_identity.hair: dark brown, cropped to the jaw and tied back
distinctive_features: a Mizuhito river-tattoo of a boat-hull on the right shoulder
resin-stained hands with a missing left ring finger (table-saw accident)

desires: To keep her family's boat-building tradition alive without enabling violence
To identify the anonymous fleet buyer and warn the intended target
fears_or_limits: Refusing the commission and the buyer taking revenge on her family
Building the boats and her craft being used in a canal invasion that kills hundreds

entries.name: He Jingtian
entries.gm_notes: A Wei scholar-strategist who authored the Wei warlord's most successful battle plans. He has had a crisis of conscience after the Battle of Sorrowful Ford, where his flanking strategy worked perfectly but resulted in the deaths of three thousand Chu conscripts—mostly farmers with spears. He has secretly corresponded with the Great Academy, offering to defect and provide Wei's strategic archives in exchange for asylum. The Academy is interested but fears the diplomatic fallout. He has not yet defected because his daughter is held as a 'guest' (hostage) in the Wei warlord's household, and he knows defection would mean her death.

payload.summary: A tall, grave scholar in Wei blue robes whose military treatises are studied by officers across all three states.
payload.appearance: Dignified and somber, wearing Wei-state scholar's robes of deep blue. Carries a fan inscribed with strategic diagrams.

visual_identity.hair: black heavily streaked with gray, in a formal scholar's topknot
distinctive_features: a scholar's ink-stain on the right forefinger
a thin, old scar on the left brow from a riding accident

desires: To defect and atone for the deaths his strategies caused
To free his daughter from the Wei warlord's hostage-guest arrangement
fears_or_limits: His daughter being killed if he defects
That the Academy will refuse asylum and the Wei warlord will learn of his contact

entries.name: Ye Qingrong
entries.gm_notes: A chi-cultivation nun who runs a small mountain monastery that is a refuge for women fleeing abusive situations in all three states. She is Qin Baotian's sister—the one who performs the chi-war-rituals on his soldiers. She believes the rituals are necessary because the Jin warlord has threatened to destroy her monastery if she does not cooperate. She has been secretly diverting some of the chi she channels to sustain a protective barrier around the monastery, which is why her rituals are slightly less effective than they should be—a discrepancy that a careful observer might notice. She is looking for a way to free herself from the warlord's coercion without abandoning the women she protects.

payload.summary: A serene, white-robed chi-cultivation nun at a mountain monastery who welcomes all women who seek shelter, no questions asked.
payload.role: Chi-cultivation nun, war-ritual performer, and monastery protector
payload.appearance: Calm and luminous, wearing simple white cultivation robes. Moves with a cultivator's centered stillness.

visual_identity.hair: black, cropped short in monastic style
visual_identity.eyes: clear gray, serene with private strain
distinctive_features: cultivation calluses on both palms
a faint chi-glow around the hands visible in dim light

desires: To free herself from the warlord's coercion without endangering the monastery
To tell her brother the truth about what his victories cost
fears_or_limits: The warlord destroying the monastery if she stops the rituals
Her brother discovering the truth and doing something rash that gets him killed

entries.name: Jin Xiao'er
entries.gm_notes: An eight-year-old boy who is the Jin warlord's youngest son and is deliberately kept out of public view because he was born with a lame left leg. The warlord considers him an embarrassment. Jin Xiao'er is quietly brilliant—he has taught himself to read military texts and has an intuitive grasp of chi-flow that none of his siblings possess. He has secretly befriended Niu Caihong, the beggar-chi-master, who has been teaching him basic cultivation through the market well where he sometimes sneaks out to. He does not understand his father's war but has intuited from his readings that the war is built on a lie, though he cannot articulate which lie.

payload.summary: A small, bright-eyed boy of eight with a wooden leg-brace who reads too much for his age and asks questions that unsettle adults.
payload.role: Warlord's youngest son and hidden chi-prodigy
payload.appearance: Small and pale, wearing fine but plain Jin court children's clothes. Left leg braced with a wooden support. Always has a scroll.

visual_identity.body_build: small and slight for his age
visual_identity.hair: black, in a child's simple topknot
distinctive_features: a wooden leg-brace on the left leg
ink stains on the right hand from reading and writing beyond his years

desires: To understand why his father is ashamed of him
To learn chi-cultivation from the old beggar woman at the well
fears_or_limits: His father discovering his secret outings and confining him
That his lameness means he will never matter to anyone

entries.name: Sha Wuyin
entries.gm_notes: A shadowy figure who operates Jin-an's underground gambling den and is the city's premier fixer—able to arrange forged documents, discreet passage, and anonymous contacts for a price. She lost her entire family to a Wei military raid twenty years ago and rebuilt her life in the criminal underworld. She is the only person who knows that the Jin warlord's chief advisor and the Chu warlord's chancellor have been secretly corresponding about a partition plan to divide Jin territory between Wei and Chu after a coordinated coup. She has kept this information because she is waiting to sell it to the highest bidder, but the coup timeline is approaching and she is running out of time to find a buyer she trusts.

payload.summary: A sharp-eyed, sharp-tongued woman who runs Jin-an's most discreet gambling den and knows where every secret in the city is buried.
payload.role: Gambling den operator and underground fixer
payload.appearance: Hard-edged and watchful, wearing dark, practical clothes under a gambler's coat. Rings on every finger, eyes on every door.

visual_identity.hair: black with a white streak at the right temple, in a practical gambler's ponytail
distinctive_features: a knife-scar from the right ear to the jaw
a gambler's callus on the right thumb from dice and cards

desires: To sell the partition plan before the coup happens
To find a buyer who will use the information to prevent the partition, not enable it
fears_or_limits: The Jin advisor or Chu chancellor discovering she knows before she can sell the information
That no buyer will pay what the information is worth and she will have died for nothing

entries.name: Yara Moonflower
entries.gm_notes: The eldest living shaman of the Teluna tribe and keeper of the Moonflower Pact, a spirit agreement made three generations ago between the tribe and a being called the Mother of Jaguars. The Pact guarantees the tribe's safety from rainforest predators in exchange for a life-essence offering every nineteen rains. Yara has made the offering herself four times. The next offering is due in two seasons, and the designated young woman — Yara's own granddaughter Iuri — has begun to suspect what the ritual truly demands. Yara has been considering breaking the Pact and accepting the consequences, because she believes the Mother of Jaguars is no longer the benevolent spirit she once was but has been slowly corrupted by something older that sleeps beneath the temple ruins.

payload.summary: An aged jaguar beast-kin shaman who speaks with spirits in her sleep and carries the scent of night-blooming flowers wherever she goes.
payload.appearance: Weathered and regal, draped in layers of ceremonial feather-cloth and bone jewelry. Moves slowly but with absolute presence. Painted jaguar spots trace her temples and fade down her neck.

visual_identity.body_build: gaunt but unbowed, tall for a beast-kin
visual_identity.hair: white, coarse, worn loose past the shoulders
distinctive_features: faint jaguar-spot patterning across the temples and jaw
a ritual scar in the shape of a crescent moon on the left palm
elongated canines visible when she speaks

desires: To find a way to end the Moonflower Pact without unleashing the Mother of Jaguars on her people
To pass on the true spirit-speaking art to someone worthy before her last breath
fears_or_limits: That her granddaughter Iuri will volunteer for the next offering out of love for her
That the corruption she senses in the Mother of Jaguars has already touched her own spirit

entries.name: Corrente Watersong
entries.gm_notes: A Mizuhito river pilot who knows every submerged channel between Iara and the distant salt mouth — knowledge she inherited from her mother, who drowned under circumstances no one will discuss. Corrente privately believes her mother was killed by a rival pilot family that sabotaged her canoe's spirit-binding. She has spent years quietly mapping their involvement and has confirmed the family's identity, but the saboteurs are now allied with the Iara dock council, meaning any accusation would collapse the fragile trade alliance. She has begun teaching her own daughter a secret technique — a way to sense sabotaged spirit-bindings by touch — that she hopes will one day serve as evidence and protection both.

payload.summary: A blue-skinned Mizuhito river pilot who navigates the flooded forests with an almost supernatural sense for hidden currents and submerged obstacles.
payload.role: Master river pilot and canoe navigator
payload.appearance: Compact and weathered, perpetually damp. Wears minimal clothing of woven river-reed. Her webbed hands are callused from decades of paddle work.

visual_identity.hair: dark green-blue, cropped short and clinging to the skull
distinctive_features: blue-green skin with faint bioluminescent mottling along the forearms
webbed fingers and toes with visible membrane
a pale scar across the throat shaped like a paddle-edge cut

desires: To expose the rival pilot family without destroying the Iara trade alliance
To see her daughter pilot the full river route alone and safely
fears_or_limits: Drowning the same way her mother did
That her daughter will learn the truth and seek vengeance instead of protection

entries.name: Quilla Featherhand
entries.gm_notes: The most skilled feather worker in the western rainforest, famous for ceremonial headdresses that are said to carry fragments of bird-spirits. What no one knows is that Quilla's mastery comes from a bargain she made as a desperate young woman with a feathered serpent-spirit called the Plumed Tongue: in exchange for the ability to weave spirit-essence into feathers, she must weave one headdress per year that contains a fragment of a living person's breath — a tiny theft of vitality that she disguises as part of the blessing ritual. The stolen vitality goes to the Plumed Tongue, who is using it to slowly manifest a physical body. Quilla has realized what she is feeding and has been secretly weakening the headdresses for three years, but the spirit has noticed and is beginning to threaten her through her dreams.

payload.summary: A brilliant bird beast-kin feather artist whose headdresses are sought after by every tribe for ceremonies, each one said to carry a whisper of the bird it came from.
payload.role: Master feather worker and ceremonial artisan
payload.appearance: Vivid and bright-eyed, draped in her own feather-work — mantles of scarlet, gold, and iridescent green. Her fingers are perpetually stained with natural dyes.

visual_identity.hair: a crest of iridescent blue-green feathers that rises when she is emotional
distinctive_features: feathered crest along the crown that molts seasonally
fine scales faintly visible on the cheekbones and ears
hollow-boned lightness to her step

desires: To break free of the Plumed Tongue's bargain before it manifests fully
To create one final headdress that is genuinely blessed — with no stolen breath in it
