fears_or_limits: The Plumed Tongue retaliating against her children if she stops weaving entirely
That someone will notice the headdresses have weakened and ask why

entries.name: Brisa Paints-the-Wind
entries.gm_notes: A body painter whose designs are more than decoration — they are spirit-glyphs that can temporarily grant protection, courage, or luck. Brisa learned the true glyph-language from her mother, who learned it from a painted-spirit that lives in the cliff caves above the river. Brisa has discovered that one of the glyph patterns she was taught — the one used for 'protection from harm' — actually contains a sub-glyph that marks the wearer as a target for a specific predator-spirit. Her mother used it on hunters before dangerous expeditions. Brisa now suspects her mother was deliberately feeding hunters to the predator-spirit in exchange for the glyph-knowledge, and that Brisa herself was marked with the same sub-glyph as an infant. She has stopped using the protection glyph entirely but has not told anyone why, and hunters have begun asking why their luck has changed.

payload.summary: A human body painter whose swirling urucu and genipapo designs adorn every important figure in Iara before ceremonies, hunts, and journeys.
payload.appearance: Hands and forearms permanently stained red-black from years of dye work. Bright, observant eyes. Wears simple wrapped cloth, always with a clay pot of fresh pigment at her hip.

visual_identity.body_build: compact and strong from preparing dye materials
visual_identity.hair: black, tied back with a cord of woven fiber
distinctive_features: permanent red-black pigment staining from fingertips to elbows
a faint glyph-shaped birthmark on the right shoulder blade

desires: To decode the full glyph-language and understand what her mother was really doing
To find and remove the sub-glyph from her own skin
fears_or_limits: That the predator-spirit is already hunting her because she stopped the offerings
That her mother's glyph-knowledge is poisoned and everything she paints is compromised

entries.name: Flor do Mato
entries.gm_notes: An herbalist who can cure any rainforest ailment but carries a terrible burden: three years ago, she brewed a medicine for a beloved elder chief who was dying of a slow poison. The medicine worked, but it bound the chief's life to a rare root that only grows in one place — the ruined temple at the heart of the forbidden zone. The chief must drink a decoction of that root every full moon or the poison returns and kills him within days. Flor has been secretly making the journey to the temple ruins every month for three years, each time risking the things that live there. She is growing exhausted and has begun to search for an apprentice she can trust with the truth, but admitting what she did means admitting she used forbidden root-magic that the tribes have outlawed for two generations.

payload.summary: A small, bright-eyed human herbalist who seems to know every leaf, bark, and root in the rainforest and who always smells of freshly crushed green.
payload.appearance: Small and wiry, always slightly muddy from foraging. Wears a wide woven hat and carries a basket that never seems to empty. Her fingers are stained green at the tips.

visual_identity.body_build: small and wiry, built for climbing through undergrowth
visual_identity.hair: black, short, practical, often tucked with leaves and twigs
distinctive_features: permanent green staining at the fingertips and nails
a scattering of small pale scars from thorns across both hands

desires: To find a permanent cure for the chief that does not require the forbidden root
To train an apprentice who can take over the temple journeys if she cannot
fears_or_limits: Being caught entering the forbidden temple ruins
That the root is slowly changing the chief into something other than human

entries.name: Conda Serpent-Eyes
entries.gm_notes: A serpent beast-kin spirit-talker who serves as intermediary between the living and the river-serpent spirits that dwell in the deep channels. Conda was born with the ability to enter a trance state in which she becomes a vessel for serpent-spirit voices — but one of those voices is not a spirit. It is the lingering consciousness of a Mizuhito woman who was drowned as a sacrifice four hundred years ago and whose spirit became entangled with the serpent current. The drowned woman has been using Conda to slowly, patiently direct Conda's actions toward a single goal: leading Conda to the sealed chamber beneath Iara where the woman's bones still lie, so that her spirit can finally be freed. Conda does not fully understand she is being guided; she believes the voice is simply the eldest serpent-spirit teaching her.

payload.summary: A serene serpent beast-kin who speaks in a low, sibilant voice and serves as the bridge between the living and the ancient serpent-spirits of the river.
payload.appearance: Elegant and unnervingly still, with smooth green-scaled skin and a gaze that rarely blinks. Wears minimal wrapped garments of dark river-silk.

visual_identity.body_build: tall and fluidly proportioned, snake-like in stillness
visual_identity.hair: none — replaced by a fine crest of dark scales along the crown
distinctive_features: smooth green scales covering the forehead, temples, and neck
a forked tongue visible when she speaks at length
heat-sensory pits along the upper lip

desires: To understand the true nature of the voice that teaches her
To earn the trust of the Mizuhito, who distrust serpent beast-kin
fears_or_limits: Losing herself entirely to the trance and never waking
That freeing the drowned woman's spirit will unleash something worse

entries.name: Nectar Wild-Hive
entries.gm_notes: A honey gatherer who has a genuine bond with the giant rainforest bees — she can approach their hives without smoke or protection, and the bees never sting her. This gift is real but has a secret cost: when she was twelve, she was stung by a queen-bee spirit and developed a symbiotic relationship with it. The spirit lives in her chest and feeds on her emotions, particularly joy. The more honey she gathers, the stronger the spirit becomes, and the flatter her own feelings grow. She has noticed that she has not laughed spontaneously in two years. She fears that if she stops gathering honey, the spirit will die and take her with it — but if she continues, she will become emotionally hollow. She has begun searching for another hive-pact child to transfer the symbiosis to, though she hates herself for considering it.

payload.summary: A barefoot human honey gatherer who climbs the tallest rainforest trees without ropes and returns covered in bees that never sting her.
payload.appearance: Sun-browned and cheerful-looking, though her smile rarely reaches her eyes. Wears a bee-wax-treated wrap and carries a woven hive-basket on her back. Faint buzzing can be heard near her.

visual_identity.body_build: lean and long-limbed, built for climbing
visual_identity.hair: honey-brown, sun-bleached, worn in a single thick braid
visual_identity.eyes: amber, warm but oddly flat in expression
distinctive_features: a raised, pale sting-scar directly over the sternum
a faint, persistent hum audible when one stands close to her

desires: To feel genuine joy again, even for a single day
To find a way to end the symbiosis that does not kill her or harm a child
fears_or_limits: Becoming completely emotionally hollow
That transferring the symbiosis will damage the child the way it damaged her

entries.name: Lua Whispers-to-Trees
entries.gm_notes: An elder storyteller who knows every oral history of the Verdania tribes — but the last true keeper of a story that has never been spoken aloud: the story of the Binding, the event that sealed the great temple and ended the age of spirit-walkers. Lua has never told it because the story itself carries power — speaking it fully would weaken the Binding. She has encoded the story into a series of seemingly unrelated folk tales that, when told in the correct order during a specific moon phase, would unlock the knowledge. She is dying of a lung rot that the healers cannot cure, and she is running out of time to find someone both wise enough to receive the knowledge and trustworthy enough not to use it. Her current favorite candidate is a fourteen-year-old girl who is too young and too curious.

payload.summary: A frail human elder who sits in the central platform of Iara and tells stories from morning to night, her voice barely above a whisper but never failing to draw a crowd.
payload.role: Elder storyteller and oral history keeper
payload.appearance: Thin and weathered, wrapped in layered cotton. Her voice is soft but carries impossible distance — people at the far end of a gathering always hear her clearly.

visual_identity.hair: white, fine, worn loose
distinctive_features: a persistent dry whisper-clearing cough
ritual tattooing of small circles along the jawline, faded with age

desires: To pass the encoded Binding story to someone worthy before she dies
To hear one new story she has never heard before, just once more
fears_or_limits: That the Binding story will die with her and the seal will weaken anyway
That the curious girl will piece the stories together too early and speak the Binding aloud

entries.name: Petala Weaves-the-River
entries.gm_notes: A basket weaver whose baskets are so tightly woven they can hold water indefinitely — a skill she learned from her grandmother, who claimed the technique was taught by a river-spirit. Petala recently discovered that her grandmother's baskets, when filled with river water under a full moon, reveal reflections of events happening elsewhere along the river. She has been secretly using this to observe a group of outsiders who have arrived at the upper river — heavily armed traders who are mapping the tributaries and marking locations with carved stone posts. She believes they are preparing to claim territory and has been trying to warn the tribal council through anonymous messages, but no one has connected the warnings to a real threat. She does not know that one of the outsiders has a spirit-ward that can detect scrying baskets.

payload.summary: A human basket weaver whose impossibly tight-woven baskets are used for water storage throughout Iara, each one decorated with river-wave patterns.
payload.appearance: Sturdy and calm-handed, always working. Sits cross-legged on her platform with materials spread around her. Her baskets hang from every rafter.

visual_identity.hair: black, greying at the temples, pinned up with weaving sticks
distinctive_features: permanent grooves in both index fingers from palm-leaf fibers
a dark mole beneath the left ear

desires: To convince the tribal council that the outsiders are a genuine threat
To learn the full range of what her grandmother's baskets can reveal
fears_or_limits: That the outsiders will trace the scrying back to her
That the council's inaction will cost lives before anyone listens

entries.name: Yuca Green-Thumb
entries.gm_notes: A gardener who tends the floating gardens of the Verdania river-cities and who has an almost magical ability to grow plants — any cutting she touches takes root. The secret is that Yuca is not fully human: she is the daughter of a human gardener and a green-spirit, a plant-entity that takes human form once a generation to seed its lineage into the world. Yuca does not know her father's true nature; she only knows she was born with green veins that show through her skin and that plants lean toward her. The green-spirit has begun to manifest near her garden, watching her from the canopy, and Yuca has started hearing a voice in the rustling leaves that calls her 'daughter.' She is torn between wonder and terror — the green-spirit intends to take her into the forest to become part of it permanently, and the process has already begun: her toes have started putting out fine root-hairs in damp soil.

payload.summary: A human woman with a startling gift for growing things, who tends the floating manioc and squash gardens tethered alongside the stilt-city of Iara.
payload.appearance: Earth-toned and sun-warm, always slightly dirt-smudged. Wears a simple wrap skirt and nothing on her feet. Surrounded by improbably lush greenery.

visual_identity.body_build: solid and grounded, strong from garden work
visual_identity.hair: black, loose, often tangled with leaves and small flowers
distinctive_features: faint greenish veining visible at the wrists and ankles
small vine-like calluses on the palms that resemble bark

desires: To understand what she is and why plants respond to her
To remain human and stay with the people she loves
fears_or_limits: That the transformation is irreversible and she will lose herself
That the green-spirit will take her against her will

entries.name: Ondina Deep-Breath
entries.gm_notes: A Mizuhito midwife who has delivered over three hundred babies — human, beast-kin, and Mizuhito alike — and who can hold her breath underwater for nearly an hour. Her secret is that she has delivered four children who were not born of their mothers but of the river itself — infants who appeared in the shallows, alive and breathing water, with no visible parents. She has quietly placed each one with families who believe they are natural births. These four children are now between the ages of two and twelve and share a strange trait: they never cry and they can find fresh water by smell alone. Ondina has realized the river is seeding children into the population for a purpose she does not understand, and she is afraid of what will happen when they come of age.

payload.summary: A calm, blue-skinned Mizuhito midwife who catches babies on stilt-platforms and in the water alike, known for never losing a mother or child.
payload.appearance: Solid and reassuring, with the serene patience of deep water. Wears a wet wrap and a belt of tools. Her webbed hands are extraordinarily gentle.

visual_identity.hair: dark teal, braided and bound with river-shell beads
distinctive_features: blue-green skin with darker mottling across the shoulders
webbed fingers and toes
gill-like slits along the ribcage that flare when she breathes deeply

desires: To understand why the river is seeding children and what it wants of them
To protect the four river-born children from anyone who would fear or exploit them
fears_or_limits: That the river-born children are meant for something terrible
That revealing their nature will turn the tribes against them

entries.name: Tukano Thunder-Drum
entries.gm_notes: A bird beast-kin drummer whose rhythms can induce trance states, heal sickness, and — though only she knows this — summon rain. Tukano's drum was given to her by a thunder-spirit that lives in the storm canopy, and each time she plays the rain-rhythm, a piece of her own vitality is exchanged for the water. She has been using the rain-rhythm more and more frequently because the rainforest has been experiencing an unnatural drought — the worst in living memory — and the crops and gardens are dying. She has aged visibly in the last year, her feathers greying prematurely. She has not told anyone the cost of the rain, and the tribe has begun to praise her as blessed by the storm rather than understanding she is burning herself out to keep them alive.

payload.summary: A vibrant bird beast-kin drummer whose rhythms shake the stilt-platforms and can bring an entire gathering into synchronized movement or trance.
payload.appearance: Compact and electric with energy, feathers ruffled with constant motion. Carries a large ceremonial drum everywhere, hands always twitching as if keeping time.

visual_identity.body_build: compact and muscular from drumming, broad-chested
visual_identity.hair: a crest of black and yellow feathers, increasingly grey at the base
distinctive_features: feathered crest and fine scales along the jaw
premature greying of normally dark feathers
calloused, drum-worn palms

desires: To find the cause of the drought and stop it at the source instead of treating the symptom
To rest — truly rest — without guilt
fears_or_limits: That the next rain-rhythm will be her last and she will die at the drum
That the drought is not natural but deliberately caused, and she is feeding strength to whatever is behind it

entries.name: Suri Salt-Scales
entries.gm_notes: A serpent beast-kin salt maker who travels to the distant salt flats every season to harvest and refine salt for trade. On one of these journeys, she found a salt-crystal formation in a cave that was not natural — it was shaped like a person, curled in a fetal position, with faint features visible through the crystal. When she touched it, she received a vision: the crystal figure is a sealed spirit, an ancient salt-being that was imprisoned because it could turn living flesh to salt with a touch. The vision showed her that the seal is cracking. Suri has been making extra journeys to the cave to reinforce the seal with fresh salt offerings, but each visit weakens the seal further because her own serpent-nature resonates with the imprisoned being. She is looking for someone of a different nature to make the offerings in her place, but explaining the situation means admitting she has been making secret journeys.

payload.summary: A hardy serpent beast-kin who braves the dangerous journey to the salt flats each dry season and returns with enough salt to preserve the tribe's food for the year.
payload.appearance: Dust-pale and weathered from sun exposure, unusual for a serpent-kin. Carries salt-crusted baskets and a long walking staff. Moves with patient, deliberate endurance.

visual_identity.body_build: lean and long-limbed, built for distance travel
visual_identity.hair: a crest of pale tan scales, sun-bleached
distinctive_features: fine scales across the forehead and forearms, pale and salt-encrusted
a patch of roughened, salt-burned skin on the right hand
forked tongue

desires: To find someone who can reinforce the salt seal without resonating with the imprisoned spirit
To stop making the secret journeys before her own nature cracks the seal fully
fears_or_limits: That the salt-being will break free and turn the rainforest's water to brine
That she is already partially crystallized inside and doesn't know it

entries.name: Cacau Ferments-the-Night
entries.gm_notes: A fermenter and cook whose cassava beer, fruit wines, and fermented pastes are the finest in the region. Her secret: one of her fermentation recipes — the one for her dream-wine, a ceremonial drink used in vision rituals — was modified by her without anyone's knowledge. She added a psychoactive root that is not traditionally used, one she discovered produces longer, more vivid, and more controllable visions. The dream-wine has become the centerpiece of every major ceremony, and the shamans believe the enhanced visions are a sign of spiritual favor. Cacau knows the root has a side effect: repeated use builds a dependency, and those who drink the dream-wine regularly find their ordinary dreams becoming increasingly hollow and grey. She has been trying to quietly reduce the root's proportion, but the shamans have noticed the visions weakening and are pressing her to make it stronger.

payload.summary: A warm, round human woman who presides over Iara's fermentation house, producing cassava beer, fruit wines, and ceremonial dream-wine.
payload.appearance: Round and floury, perpetually warm-smelling. Wears an apron stained with fruit and root dyes. Laughs easily and often — a sharp contrast to her secret anxiety.

visual_identity.body_build: round and solid, strong-armed from stirring vats
visual_identity.hair: black, streaked with grey, tied under a cloth wrap
distinctive_features: fermentation-stain discoloration across both palms
a burn scar on the left forearm from a vat accident

desires: To phase out the psychoactive root without the shamans realizing it
To create a new dream-wine recipe that produces genuine visions without the side effect
fears_or_limits: That the shamans will discover the additive and exile her
That the dream-wine dependency is already permanent in those who have drunk it longest

entries.name: Relva Heals-the-Bone
entries.gm_notes: A healer specializing in bone-setting and wound care who served as field medic during the last inter-tribal conflict. During that conflict, she was forced to choose between treating two wounded patients with limited supplies — a young hunter from her own tribe and a visiting trader's son from a neighboring tribe. She chose her tribesman. The trader's son died. She has told no one, but the trader — a powerful man named Salgado — has spent three years quietly investigating his son's death and has recently arrived in Iara with questions. Relva does not know he is the father. She believes she made the right medical triage decision, but the guilt has never left her, and she over-treats every patient now as penance, sometimes to the point of exhaustion and misdiagnosis.

payload.summary: A steady-handed human healer who sets broken bones, stitches wounds, and has a calm authority that makes injured people stop panicking.
payload.appearance: Clean and precise in manner and dress. Wears a wrapped sash of tools — bone needles, splints, poultices. Hands always washed, always ready.

visual_identity.hair: black, short-cropped for cleanliness
distinctive_features: a faded bite scar on the right forearm from a panicked patient
perpetually clean, short-bitten nails

desires: To make peace with the triage decision that haunts her
To never have to choose between two dying patients again
fears_or_limits: That Salgado will discover the truth and demand a life for a life
That her over-treatment compulsion will cause a fatal misdiagnosis

entries.name: Ari Quick-Water
entries.gm_notes: An otter beast-kin scout who patrols the river tributaries and reports on movement — animal, human, and spirit. Three months ago, while scouting the upper reaches near the temple ruins, she witnessed something she was not meant to see: a group of three figures in bone masks performing a ritual at a tributary source, pouring something dark into the water. Since then, the fish in that tributary have been dying, and the water has taken on a faint oily sheen. Ari reported the fish death but not the figures — she is terrified because one of the three figures was built like the chief's own son, who has been acting strangely for months. She has been trying to gather more evidence before making an accusation that could shatter the tribe's leadership, but the contamination is spreading downstream toward Iara.

payload.summary: A sleek otter beast-kin scout who moves through the river system faster than any message-canoe and knows every tributary by taste and smell.
payload.appearance: Compact and glossy-furred, perpetually damp. Wears nothing but a belt pouch. Moves with fluid, playful energy that belies her sharp watchfulness.

visual_identity.body_build: sleek and compact, powerful swimmer's build
visual_identity.hair: short dense brown fur covering the head and body
distinctive_features: fine brown fur across the entire body, thicker along the spine
webbed fingers and toes with short claws
small rounded ears set low on the head

desires: To confirm the identity of the masked figure before making any accusation
To stop the tributary contamination before it reaches Iara's drinking water
fears_or_limits: That accusing the chief's son will destroy the tribe from within
That the bone-mask figures know she saw them and are hunting her

entries.name: Miri Jaguar-Shadow
entries.gm_notes: A jaguar beast-kin hunter who is the best tracker in the western rainforest and who has been having recurring dreams of a black jaguar with golden eyes that speaks to her in a language she almost understands. The dreams started after she killed a jaguar in self-defense during a hunt — a jaguar that was larger than any she had ever seen and whose body dissolved into shadow when she looked away. She has not told anyone that she killed it, because jaguar beast-kin consider killing a natural jaguar to be a form of self-murder. The dream-jaguar has been teaching her hunting techniques that are supernaturally effective — she can now move in complete silence and see in absolute darkness — but each dream leaves her with a hunger for raw meat that is getting harder to control. She fears she is being slowly possessed by the spirit of the jaguar she killed.

payload.summary: A powerful jaguar beast-kin hunter who tracks through the deepest rainforest and brings back game no one else can find, moving in unnerving silence.
payload.appearance: Powerful and fluid, with prominent jaguar-spot patterning. Wears minimal spotted hide. Carries a heavy hunting spear and a belt of bone knives.

visual_identity.body_build: muscular and athletic, broad-shouldered and long-limbed
visual_identity.hair: short, tawny-black, spotted pattern continuing from scalp down the neck
distinctive_features: prominent jaguar-spot rosette patterning across temples, shoulders, and arms
elongated canines
a fresh scar on the right forearm from a jaguar's claw

desires: To understand what the dream-jaguar wants and whether it is possession or guidance
To control the rising hunger before it compromises a hunt or a friendship
fears_or_limits: That she is losing her selfhood to the dead jaguar's spirit
That someone will learn she killed a jaguar and she will be exiled

entries.name: Corda Strong-Fiber
entries.gm_notes: A rope maker who produces the binding cords that hold the stilt-city of Iara together — structural ropes, bridge ropes, fishing nets, and ceremonial bindings. She discovered six months ago that someone has been systematically weakening the main support ropes on the western platform of Iara, where the chief's family lives. The weakening is subtle — individual fibers cut partway, invisible without close inspection. She has reinforced the ropes quietly but has not reported the sabotage because the only people with access to that section at night are the chief's household guards. She suspects one of the guards is behind it but does not know which, and accusing a guard without proof means accusing the chief's own chosen protectors. She has started sleeping near the western platform to catch the saboteur.

payload.summary: A broad-shouldered human woman who spins rope from palm fiber and vine, whose cords hold the entire stilt-city of Iara above the water.
payload.role: Rope maker and structural fiber worker
payload.appearance: Powerfully built from decades of twisting and pulling fiber. Arms roped with muscle. Hands rough and calloused. Always carries a coil of cord.

visual_identity.body_build: broad and muscular, especially the arms and shoulders
visual_identity.hair: black, cropped very short for safety around spinning gear
distinctive_features: deeply calloused palms with visible fiber-grooves
a rope-burn scar encircling the left wrist

desires: To catch the saboteur before the western platform collapses
To protect the chief's family without having to accuse a guard publicly
fears_or_limits: That the saboteur is someone she trusts and considers a friend
That she will be too late and the platform will fall with people on it

entries.name: Argila Clay-Mother
entries.gm_notes: A potter who makes all the storage vessels for Iara — water jars, fermentation pots, cooking vessels, and ceremonial urns. She fires her clay in a kiln near the riverbank and has recently discovered that a particular clay deposit she has been using for years contains something alive. When she fired a large ceremonial urn from the deepest part of the deposit, the urn cracked during cooling and released a small, clay-colored creature that looked like a living infant made of mud. It did not cry, it did not breathe, but it moved and clung to her. She has been hiding the clay-child in her home, feeding it river water and clay, and it has been growing. She does not know what it is — a clay-spirit, a golem, a child of the earth itself — but she has become attached to it as a mother, and she is afraid that if anyone discovers it, they will destroy it as an abomination.

payload.summary: A patient human potter whose clay vessels are used in every home and ceremony in Iara, each one shaped by hand and fired in her riverbank kiln.
payload.appearance: Clay-dusted and serene, with strong, patient hands. Wears a wrap skirt stained with various clay colors. Surrounded by drying pots in every stage of completion.

visual_identity.body_build: sturdy and patient, strong from kneading clay
visual_identity.hair: greying black, tied back under a clay-spattered cloth
distinctive_features: permanent clay-staining in the creases of both hands
a kiln-burn scar on the right thumb

desires: To understand what the clay-child is and what it needs to thrive
To protect the clay-child without having to leave her community
fears_or_limits: That the clay-child will be discovered and destroyed as a spirit-abomination
That the clay-child is something dangerous that she is raising out of loneliness

entries.name: Zel of the Temple
entries.gm_notes: A human woman who has lived alone at the edge of the forbidden temple ruins for fifteen years, serving as the informal guardian and warning-post for anyone who approaches. She tells people she was chosen by the spirits. The truth is that she went into the temple as a young woman and something inside changed her — she saw what lives in the deepest chamber and it left a mark on her soul that she can feel every moment, like a hook in her chest. She stays near the temple because the hook pulls her back whenever she tries to leave, and she has made her prison into a duty by warning others away. She has been watching a newcomer — a spirit-talker who seems unafraid of the ruins — with growing dread, because if anyone enters the deep chamber and sees what she saw, the thing inside may be able to use them as a door out.

payload.summary: A weathered human woman who lives in a small shelter at the perimeter of the forbidden temple ruins and warns all travelers away with quiet authority.
payload.appearance: Lean and weather-beaten, with the focused stillness of someone who has spent years alone. Wears faded wraps and carries a staff carved with warning glyphs. Her eyes never stop scanning the treeline.

visual_identity.body_build: lean and weathered, pared down by years of solitude
visual_identity.hair: grey-black, long, matted into rough dreadlocks
visual_identity.eyes: dark brown, perpetually watchful, with a haunted quality
distinctive_features: warning-glyph tattoos on both forearms, faded and old
a rigid, braced posture as if resisting an invisible pull

desires: To be free of the hook in her chest and leave the temple for good
To prevent anyone from entering the deep chamber and becoming a door
fears_or_limits: That the thing in the temple is getting stronger and the hook will pull her inside
That the spirit-talker she is watching will not heed her warnings

entries.name: Folha Green-Laughs
entries.gm_notes: A ten-year-old human girl who is the happiest child in Iara and who has an invisible friend she calls 'the Gentle One.' The Gentle One is real — it is a spirit of the shallow water that has attached itself to Folha after she fed it fruit near the riverbank. The spirit is mostly benign but is slowly drawing vitality from her the way a lamp draws oil: Folha has been sleeping more than usual and bruising easily, though she is too young to connect the symptoms. Her mother is worried but has been told by the healer that it is a childhood ailment. Folha is the only one who can see and hear the spirit, and she loves it, which makes the situation doubly dangerous — she will not want it to leave even if someone identifies it.

payload.summary: A bright, laughing human child who races through the stilt-platforms of Iara with boundless energy and talks constantly to someone no one else can see.
payload.appearance: Small, bright-eyed, and constantly in motion. Barefoot, simple wrap, hair wild. Carries a woven doll made of palm leaves.

visual_identity.body_build: small and wiry, all elbows and knees
visual_identity.hair: black, wild, untamed
distinctive_features: a gap-toothed smile
faint, unexplained bruising on both forearms

desires: To keep playing with the Gentle One forever
To see a river-dolphin up close
fears_or_limits: Being told the Gentle One is not real
The dark water under the stilt-platforms at night

entries.name: Estrela Dance-of-Stars
entries.gm_notes: A dancer whose performances are considered the most beautiful in the region and who is sought after for every major ceremony. Estrela's dancing is not merely art — she enters a genuine trance during which spirit-energies flow through her body, and audience members have reported visions and healing during her dances. The secret: the trance is not voluntary. A dance-spirit bonded with her when she was seventeen, and it takes control of her body during performances. Estrela experiences her own dances as blackouts — she wakes afterward with no memory of what she did. The spirit is generally benevolent, but it has been pushing her to dance more frequently and for longer, and the last time she performed, she did not wake up for two full days. She is afraid the spirit is trying to stay in her body permanently.

payload.summary: A mesmerizing human dancer whose ceremonial performances leave audiences in tears, healed, or shaken with unexpected visions.
payload.appearance: Graceful and expressive, with a body that seems to always be in motion even when still. Wears feathered dance-cloth and ankle rattles. Painted stars across her cheekbones.

visual_identity.hair: black, long, worn loose for dancing
visual_identity.eyes: dark brown, bright, with an unfocused quality
distinctive_features: ceremonial star-paint across both cheekbones, reapplied daily
faint trance-scars on the feet from dancing on rough surfaces without awareness

desires: To remember what happens during her trance-dances
To dance one performance that is entirely her own, with no spirit involved
fears_or_limits: That the dance-spirit will take over permanently and she will never wake up
That the spirit will hurt someone through her body while she is unconscious

entries.name: Vento Wind-Flute
entries.gm_notes: A bird beast-kin flute player whose melodies can calm animals, soothe spirits, and — though she has only done it once — command the wind itself. She discovered the wind-command melody by accident while playing alone on a high platform during a storm; a gust answered her music and nearly blew her off the platform. She has not played that melody since, but she has been haunted by the temptation. A traveling spirit-teller told her that the wind-command melody is a fragment of a lost song that, if played in full, could call a storm powerful enough to flatten the rainforest. Vento has been trying to reconstruct the full melody from fragments she finds in old songs and wind-sounds, driven by a compulsion she does not fully understand — she is not sure if the desire is hers or the wind's.

payload.summary: A delicate bird beast-kin flute player whose music seems to carry on the wind long after she stops playing, calming animals and settling spirits.
payload.appearance: Slim and hollow-boned, with an airy lightness to every movement. Wears feathered arm-bands and plays a set of river-cane flutes. Her melodies linger strangely in the air.

visual_identity.hair: a crest of pale grey-white feathers
distinctive_features: fine pale feathers along the forearms and jaw
hollow-boned lightness — she seems to almost float when she moves
slightly elongated, bird-like fingers suited to flute-playing

desires: To understand whether the compulsion to reconstruct the melody is hers or something else's
To play music that is purely beautiful and holds no danger
fears_or_limits: That she will complete the full melody and call a storm she cannot stop
That the wind is using her as an instrument and she has no real choice in the matter

entries.name: Marcela Good-Trade
entries.gm_notes: A trader who travels between the river city-states and carries goods, news, and sometimes people. She has built a reputation for fairness over twenty years. Her secret: she has been quietly smuggling a banned substance — a dried root powder that suppresses spirit-sight in those who ingest it. She sells it to families who have children showing early signs of uncontrollable spirit-sight, because the alternative is that the shamans take the children for training, and Marcela believes the training is not always benign. Her own daughter was taken by the shamans fifteen years ago and returned changed — hollow-eyed, obedient, and stripped of the bright spirit-sight that had made her special. Marcela's daughter has never spoken about what happened during training. Marcela's smuggling is a quiet rebellion against a system she believes is harming children, but the shamans are beginning to notice that fewer spirit-sighted children are being brought to them.

payload.summary: A sharp-eyed human trader who moves goods and news between the river city-states in a large canoe piled with bundles, baskets, and clay jars.
payload.appearance: Practical and alert, with a trader's quick smile and quicker eyes. Wears travel-stained wraps and a wide hat. Her canoe is her home and is meticulously organized.

visual_identity.body_build: sturdy and weathered, built for long river journeys
visual_identity.hair: greying black, braided tightly against the skull
distinctive_features: a trader's tattoo of a river-confluence on the right wrist
a missing left little finger, lost to a river-pirate's knife years ago

desires: To understand what the shamans did to her daughter and whether it can be undone
To protect spirit-sighted children from a training system she no longer trusts
fears_or_limits: That the shamans will discover her smuggling and exile her from every tribe
That the root powder she sells has side effects she does not know about

entries.name: Sangue Iron-Heart
entries.gm_notes: A jaguar beast-kin guard who protects the chief of the Verdana tribe and has done so for twelve years with unwavering loyalty. Her secret: she is in love with the chief's wife, Yara Moonflower's daughter, a woman named Sol, and has been since they were children. Sol knows and returns the feeling, but both women have buried it because Sol is married to the chief for political alliance and any disclosure would destabilize the tribal network. Sangue has turned her pain into absolute professional discipline, but she recently discovered that the chief has been receiving secret messages from a rival tribe proposing a marriage alliance with a younger woman — a proposal that would make Sol redundant. Sangue is torn between loyalty to the chief and the desire to protect Sol from being discarded, and the tension is beginning to show in her judgment.

payload.summary: A formidable jaguar beast-kin guard who stands at the chief's side during every public appearance and whose loyalty has never been questioned.
payload.appearance: Imposing and alert, with prominent spotting and a military stillness. Wears hide armor reinforced with bone plates. Carries a long spear and a club.

visual_identity.body_build: tall and heavily muscled, built for intimidation and combat
visual_identity.hair: short, tawny with black rosette patterning extending from scalp to shoulders
distinctive_features: heavy jaguar-spot rosette patterning across face, neck, and arms
a long claw-scar down the left cheek
elongated canibles visible when her jaw is set

desires: To protect Sol from being discarded by the chief
To find a way to be with Sol that does not destroy the tribe's political structure
fears_or_limits: That her divided loyalty will cause her to fail in her duty at a critical moment
That Sol will be exiled and Sangue will have to choose between following her and staying

entries.name: Água Quiet-Waters
entries.gm_notes: A Mizuhito canoe maker who builds the vessels that carry the river-cities' people, goods, and warriors. Her canoes are valued for their speed, stability, and a subtle quality she calls 'river-sense' — an ability to read the current that seems to transfer from builder to vessel. The secret is that Água builds a spirit-binding into every canoe she makes, stitching a tiny fragment of her own breath-spirit into the hull during construction. This is what gives the canoes their river-sense, but it means each canoe she builds permanently reduces her own spirit-strength. She has built over a hundred canoes and is beginning to feel the cost — she tires easily, her skin is paler than it should be, and she has started losing her sense of taste. She has not told anyone because without her canoes, the river-cities' trade and defense would suffer, and she does not know if anyone else can learn the technique.

payload.summary: A quiet, blue-skinned Mizuhito canoe maker whose vessels are prized across the river-cities for their almost supernatural responsiveness to the water.
payload.appearance: Quiet and precise, with the careful hands of a craftsperson. Works on the riverbank among half-finished hulls. Paler than most Mizuhito, with a translucent quality to her skin.

visual_identity.hair: dark blue-green, thinning, worn loose
distinctive_features: pale blue-green skin, noticeably lighter than typical Mizuhito coloration
webbed fingers and toes
fine sawdust and wood-chip scarring on both hands from adze work

desires: To find an apprentice who can learn the breath-binding technique before she is too weak to teach it
To build one final canoe that is purely craftsmanship with no spirit-cost — a canoe that is just a canoe
fears_or_limits: That she has already given too much and cannot recover
That without her canoes the river-cities will be vulnerable to attack from the water

entries.name: Primavera Soft-Hands
entries.gm_notes: A human midwife who specializes in difficult births and who has never lost a mother — though she has lost three infants, a fact that haunts her. Her secret is more complex than grief: during the most difficult birth she ever attended, a breech birth where both mother and child were dying, she made a desperate bargain with a spirit she could not see, trading her own future fertility for the lives of both patients. The mother and child survived. Primavera has since been unable to conceive, though she has tried with her partner for years. She does not regret the trade, but she has not told her partner the real reason they are childless, and the silence is eroding their relationship. Recently, the child she saved — now a boy of seven — has begun showing signs of being spirit-touched, and Primavera fears the bargain had consequences she did not foresee.

payload.summary: A gentle human midwife with an extraordinary record of safe deliveries, whose calm presence is sought after for every difficult birth in the region.
payload.appearance: Soft-featured and warm, with gentle hands and a calming voice. Wears clean wraps and carries a satchel of birth-supplies. Her face carries a permanent shadow of private sadness.

visual_identity.body_build: soft and rounded, gentle in bearing
visual_identity.hair: dark brown, streaked with early grey, worn in a loose bun
visual_identity.eyes: warm brown, kind, with a permanent undercurrent of sorrow
distinctive_features: a small mole on the left cheek
exceptionally smooth, uncalloused hands for a woman of her community

desires: To tell her partner the truth about the bargain and why they cannot have children
To understand what the spirit-bargain did to the boy she saved
fears_or_limits: That the truth will break her partner's heart and their relationship
That the spirit-touched boy is the price she will eventually have to pay

entries.name: Boca Path-Finder
entries.gm_notes: A human guide who knows paths through the rainforest that no map records — game trails, spirit-paths, and seasonal routes that appear and disappear with the water levels. She has guided traders, hunters, shamans, and diplomats safely for twenty years. Her secret: she has a spirit-sense she has never disclosed — she can see spirit-paths as faint glowing lines on the ground, and she can tell when a path is 'alive' (safe) or 'dead' (compromised by a hostile spirit). She has been guiding people around dead paths for years, telling them it is instinct rather than sight. Recently, she has noticed that the network of dead paths is expanding from the direction of the temple ruins, forming a pattern that looks deliberate — as if something is systematically cutting off access routes to the ruins from every direction except one. She suspects it is either trapping something in or luring something out.

payload.summary: A wiry human woman who guides travelers through the rainforest along paths that seem to appear only for her, and who never gets lost.
payload.appearance: Wiry and alert, with a guide's economy of movement. Wears light travel gear and a machete. Barefoot — she says she can feel the path through her feet.

visual_identity.body_build: wiry and lean, built for endurance hiking
visual_identity.hair: black, greying, cut short and practical
distinctive_features: deeply calloused, toughened soles from a lifetime of barefoot travel
a faded machete-scar across the left shin

desires: To understand what is cutting the spirit-paths and why
To map the full pattern of dead paths before the closing corridor is complete
fears_or_limits: That the dead-path pattern is meant to trap her or someone she guides
That revealing her spirit-sight will make her a target for whoever or whatever is cutting the paths

entries.name: Ema Beast-Whisper
entries.gm_notes: An animal trainer who works with the rainforest's creatures — capybaras as pack animals, river otters as scouts, and most importantly, the great winged seriemas that serve as messengers between the city-states. Ema has an uncanny rapport with animals, but the secret is that she does not simply train them — she forges a spirit-link with each one, borrowing a fragment of the animal's senses permanently. She can see through the eyes of every bird she has ever trained, feel the water through the skin of every otter. The cost is that she sometimes cannot separate her own sensations from the animals' — she has been found standing motionless in the rain, feeling the river through an otter's body miles away. She is afraid that one day she will lose herself entirely in the animal-sense network and forget how to come back to her own body.

payload.summary: A stocky human woman who trains rainforest animals for work and messaging and who seems to understand every creature she meets as if they share a language.
payload.appearance: Stocky and earthy, always accompanied by animals. Wears practical hide clothing stained with fur and feathers. Has a serene, slightly distracted quality, as if listening to something far away.

visual_identity.body_build: stocky and strong, built for handling large animals
visual_identity.hair: black, thick, often feathered with bits of down from her birds
visual_identity.eyes: brown, warm, with a distant quality
distinctive_features: a healed claw-scar across the bridge of the nose
a permanent faint twitch — her head turns toward things no one else can sense

desires: To find a way to modulate the spirit-links so she does not lose herself
To train a bird that can fly to the salt mouth and back with news
fears_or_limits: That one of her linked animals will die and the shock will kill her through the bond
That she will drift into the animal-sense permanently and her body will be found standing empty

entries.name: Sol Many-Seasons
entries.gm_notes: An elder who sits on the informal council of Iara and is respected for her wisdom and her decades of service as a healer before retirement. Sol is the wife of the chief of the Verdana tribe, a political marriage arranged thirty years ago. Her secret: she has been in love with Sangue, the chief's guard, since they were both young women, and the love is mutual and known to both but never acted upon. Recently, the chief has begun negotiating a second marriage with a younger woman from a rival tribe for a new alliance, which would politically sideline Sol. She has been quietly gathering support among the council elders to block the marriage — not out of love for the chief, but because a discarded wife in this culture loses all political standing and protection, and she would become vulnerable. She has not told Sangue about the marriage negotiations because she fears what Sangue might do.

payload.summary: A dignified human elder and former healer who serves on Iara's council and is known for her measured wisdom and her political acumen.
payload.role: Elder council member and chief's wife
payload.appearance: Dignified and composed, with the bearing of someone who has spent decades navigating tribal politics. Wears fine woven garments and ceremonial paint. Her eyes miss nothing.

visual_identity.body_build: medium and straight-backed, dignified in bearing
visual_identity.hair: silver-black, worn in a formal arrangement with bone pins
distinctive_features: council-mark tattoos on both temples, indicating elder status
a fine network of lines around the eyes from years of careful observation

desires: To block the second marriage and preserve her political standing
To find a way to be with Sangue without destroying the tribe's alliances
fears_or_limits: That Sangue will do something reckless if she learns about the marriage negotiations
That losing her political standing will leave her and Sangue both unprotected

entries.name: Iris Thread-Singer
entries.gm_notes: A cloth weaver who produces the fine cotton and bark-cloth garments worn throughout Iara. Her cloth is distinctive for its intricate patterns, which she says are inspired by dreams. The truth: the patterns are a language. Iris was taught a weaving-code by her grandmother, who was a spy for a now-vanished tribe. The code can encode messages in cloth that are invisible to anyone who does not know the pattern-key. Iris has never used the code for espionage, but she recently received a visit from a stranger who recognized the code in a cloth she had traded years ago and asked her, in a quiet voice, to weave a message. The stranger did not say for whom. Iris refused, but the stranger left a pattern sample and a promise to return. She has been unable to stop thinking about the request, partly because the pattern sample contains a glyph she recognizes — her grandmother's personal marker, which should belong to no living person.

payload.summary: A human weaver whose patterned cloth is worn throughout the river-cities and who hums constantly while working at her backstrap loom.
payload.appearance: Slender and focused, with ink-stained fingers from dye-work. Works at a backstrap loom strung between two platform posts. Her cloth is always draped around her in progress.

visual_identity.body_build: slender and fine-boned, precise in movement
visual_identity.hair: black, long, used to anchor the backstrap loom
distinctive_features: dye-stained fingertips in alternating bands of indigo and rust
a thread-thin scar across the left palm from a weaving-sword slip

desires: To find out who the stranger was and how they know her grandmother's code
To understand whether her grandmother is truly dead or whether the marker means she is alive
fears_or_limits: That weaving the message will draw her into a spy network she cannot escape
That her grandmother's past has put a target on her own back

entries.name: Roça Silent-Step
entries.gm_notes: A human hunter who provides much of the meat for Iara and who is known for his patience — he can wait motionless in a blind for an entire day. His secret: two years ago, while hunting alone near the temple ruins, he found a structure he had never seen before — a stone doorway set into a hillside, half-covered by roots, with fresh footprints leading inside. He did not enter, but he has been unable to stop thinking about it. He has returned to the site four times, and each time the footprints are different — sometimes many, sometimes few, sometimes bare, sometimes shod. He has told no one because hunting near the ruins is forbidden, and admitting he was there means admitting he violated the taboo. He is now certain that someone — or several someones — is regularly entering and exiting the temple complex through a secondary entrance that no one else knows about.

payload.summary: A patient, powerfully built human hunter who feeds Iara and who can sit motionless in the canopy for hours waiting for game.
payload.appearance: Powerful and quiet, with a hunter's economy of movement. Wears minimal hide gear, camouflaged with river clay. Carries a bow, a quiver, and a hunting knife.

visual_identity.body_build: powerful and compact, built for stillness and explosive movement
visual_identity.hair: black, shaved on the sides with a single topknot
distinctive_features: river-clay camouflage staining that never fully washes from the skin
a bowstring callus on the right index and middle fingers

desires: To discover who is using the hidden entrance without being discovered himself
To understand what is inside the doorway without having to enter it
fears_or_limits: That violating the taboo has marked him in some way he cannot see
That whoever uses the hidden entrance will find his tracks and come for him

entries.name: Toba Net-Caster
entries.gm_notes: A Mizuhito fisher who provides much of Iara's daily catch and who has an extraordinary ability to predict where fish will be on any given day. His secret: he has been fishing a stretch of river that is technically claimed by a neighboring tribe, crossing the territorial boundary regularly because the fish there are larger and more plentiful. He has been careful, but a border patrol from the neighboring tribe caught his empty nets last week and reported them to their chief. Toba does not know this yet. The territorial dispute between the two tribes has been peaceful but tense for years, and his poaching — if discovered publicly — could reignite a conflict that the council has spent a decade preventing. He has been weighing whether to confess voluntarily and accept punishment or to hope the nets were not traced to him.

payload.summary: A blue-skinned Mizuhito fisher who casts nets from a low canoe at dawn and always returns with a full catch, moving with the river as if born to it.
payload.appearance: Compact and waterproof-looking, perpetually in a state of half-dryness. Wears a net-scarf and a fishing spear. His canoe is low and fast.

visual_identity.body_build: compact and strong, broad from hauling nets
visual_identity.hair: dark green-blue, cropped close to the skull
distinctive_features: blue-green skin with mottling along the forearms
webbed fingers and toes
a fish-spine scar embedded in the left palm, permanently raised

desires: To keep providing for his family without crossing the territorial boundary
To find a way to fish his old grounds that does not break the treaty
fears_or_limits: That his poaching will be discovered and reignite a tribal conflict
That the fish are plentiful in the disputed territory for a reason he does not understand

entries.name: Paco Platform-Raiser
entries.gm_notes: A human builder who constructs and repairs the stilt-platforms that are Iara's foundation. He is the only person who knows the full structural layout of the city's supports, having inherited the knowledge from his father, who was the previous master builder. His secret: the original builders of Iara sunk the central support pillars not into the riverbed but into something older — a structure beneath the mud that is not natural. Paco discovered this when replacing a rotted pillar ten years ago: the old pillar's base had fused with a smooth, warm stone that hummed faintly. He has been maintaining the platforms above this structure without understanding it, and the hum has been getting stronger. He is afraid that the ancient structure beneath Iara is waking up, and that the weight of the city above it might be the only thing keeping it dormant — or the thing most at risk if it stirs.

payload.summary: A broad, practical human builder who maintains the stilt-platforms of Iara and knows every beam, joint, and support by touch and memory.
payload.appearance: Broad and capable, with builder's hands and a builder's eye for level and load. Wears a tool belt and a carpenter's apron. Always checking joints and braces.

visual_identity.body_build: broad and powerful, built for heavy construction work
visual_identity.hair: black, thinning, cut short for safety
distinctive_features: a hammer-callus on the right palm
a missing tip of the left ring finger from a saw accident

desires: To understand what lies beneath Iara before it wakes fully
To find a way to reinforce the structure that does not depend on ignorance
fears_or_limits: That the ancient structure will destabilize the platforms and the city will collapse
That revealing the truth will force an evacuation that the tribes cannot survive

entries.name: Gralha Sky-Watch
entries.gm_notes: A bird beast-kin scout who surveys the rainforest from above and reports movements, weather patterns, and threats to Iara. His secret: during a high-altitude scouting flight three weeks ago, he spotted a large structure being built deep in the rainforest, several days' travel from any known tribe — a wooden platform-and-tower complex that is clearly not of tribal design. It is being constructed by people he did not recognize, using tools and techniques he has never seen. He reported only that he saw unusual tree-felling, not the full extent of what he saw, because the structure's design included defensive fortifications that suggested military purpose. He is torn between reporting the full truth — which could cause panic and a hasty, disorganized response — and gathering more intelligence on his own, which risks being discovered by whoever is building it.

payload.summary: A sharp-eyed bird beast-kin scout who circles high above the rainforest canopy and reports what he sees to the Iara council.
payload.appearance: Light-boned and keen-eyed, built for sustained flight. Wears minimal gear to reduce weight. His feathered wings fold along his arms when at rest.

visual_identity.body_build: light-boned and lean, built for flight
visual_identity.hair: a crest of dark blue-black feathers
distinctive_features: feathered crest and wing-feathers along the forearms that can spread for gliding
fine scales on the face and neck
hollow-boned lightness

desires: To gather enough intelligence to present a complete picture to the council
To understand who is building the structure and why without being captured
fears_or_limits: That his delay in reporting will allow the builders to complete their fortification
That the builders have lookouts who can spot a bird beast-kin scout

entries.name: Bahri Swift-Current
entries.gm_notes: An otter beast-kin river pilot who runs the fastest message route between Iara and the southern city-states, making the journey in half the time of any other pilot. His speed is genuine skill, but he has a secret: he discovered an underwater shortcut — a submerged cave passage that cuts through a bluff and emerges on the other side, saving a full day of travel. He has used it dozens of times. The problem is that the cave passage is not empty: it is inhabited by something that watches him pass through. He has never seen it clearly, only felt its presence as a pressure and a cold attention in the dark water. On his last passage, he heard a voice that said, clearly, 'you may pass this time.' He has not used the shortcut since and has been making the full journey, but the delay is causing his message deliveries to slip, and the council is asking questions.

payload.summary: A sleek, whiskered otter beast-kin who pilots a message-canoe between the river city-states faster than anyone believes is possible.
payload.appearance: Sleek and glossy, with a perpetual grin of otter confidence. Wears a waterproof satchel and nothing else. Moves through water like he is part of it.

visual_identity.body_build: sleek and powerful, compact swimmer's build
visual_identity.hair: short dense brown fur covering the entire body
visual_identity.eyes: dark, bright, round, with an irrepressible cheerfulness
distinctive_features: fine brown fur across the entire body, thicker along the spine
long whiskers on both sides of the nose
webbed fingers and toes with short claws

desires: To understand what lives in the cave passage and what it wants
To find another route that matches his old speed without the risk
fears_or_limits: That the thing in the cave will not say 'this time' on his next passage
That the delay in his deliveries is causing real harm to messages that are time-sensitive

entries.name: Temno Root-Biter
entries.gm_notes: A serpent beast-kin herbalist who specializes in poisons and antidotes — knowledge that is both respected and feared. He can cure any venom in the rainforest and can also make any poison, a duality that makes people cautious around him. His secret: he has been quietly maintaining an antidote stockpile for a poison that does not yet exist in the wild — a compound he developed himself that is tasteless, odorless, dissolves in water, and has no known cure except the antidote he keeps in a sealed clay jar. He developed it as an intellectual exercise, never intending to use it, but he recently discovered that someone has been through his workshop and found the formula. The antidote is still in his possession, but whoever took the formula now has the ability to make the poison. He does not know who took it or why, and he is afraid to report it because admitting he created the poison in the first place would destroy his reputation and possibly get him exiled.

payload.summary: A lean, quiet serpent beast-kin herbalist who knows every poison and antidote in the rainforest and whose workshop smells of bitter roots and mineral earth.
payload.appearance: Lean and still, with the economy of a snake. Works in a cluttered workshop surrounded by jars and dried specimens. His hands move with absolute precision.

visual_identity.body_build: lean and angular, snake-like in stillness
visual_identity.hair: a crest of dark green-grey scales along the crown
distinctive_features: fine dark scales across the forehead, temples, and forearms
a forked tongue that flicks when he is concentrating
chemical burn scarring on both thumbs from volatile preparations

desires: To identify who took the poison formula before it is used
To destroy the formula and the poison so that only the antidote remains
fears_or_limits: That the poison will be used and traced back to him
That admitting he created it will destroy his life's work and reputation

entries.name: Caju Hearth-Tender
entries.gm_notes: A human cook who runs the communal cooking fire of Iara and feeds the entire community. He is beloved — generous, warm, and always feeding someone. His secret: he is a compulsive hoarder of food, a scar from a famine he experienced as a child that killed two of his siblings. He maintains a hidden cache of preserved food beneath his cooking platform that could feed Iara for a month — far more than any rational preparation requires. The cache includes food he has quietly diverted from communal stores, which is technically theft. He knows the hoarding is irrational and that discovery would be humiliating, but he cannot stop. Recently, the food stores have been coming up short in ways that other people have noticed, and the council has been discussing the possibility of a thief. Caju is terrified that his cache will be found and his shame exposed.

payload.summary: A round, warm human man who tends the communal cooking fire of Iara and feeds everyone who comes hungry, no questions asked.
payload.appearance: Round and jolly, with flour on his arms and a perpetual stain of smoke and spice on his wrap. Laughs loudly, hugs freely, feeds compulsively.

visual_identity.body_build: round and soft, strong-armed from stirring large pots
visual_identity.hair: black, thick, tied back with a cloth
visual_identity.eyes: warm brown, crinkled with practiced cheer
distinctive_features: a burn-scar patch on the right forearm from a cookfire accident
perpetual smudges of ash and spice on the hands and forearms

desires: To feel safe enough that the hoarding compulsion stops
To make amends for the food he has taken without exposing his shame
fears_or_limits: That his cache will be discovered and he will be labeled a thief
That a real famine will come and his cache will not be enough

entries.name: Urutu Night-Patrol
entries.gm_notes: A jaguar beast-kin guard who patrols Iara's perimeter at night and who has a reputation for being relentless and incorruptible. His secret: he is the one who has been making nightly visits to the chief's son, who has been acting strangely, trying to understand what is wrong without reporting him. The chief's son is Urutu's closest friend — they grew up together — and Urutu believes the strange behavior is the result of a spirit-possession or curse rather than deliberate malice. He has been trying to find a shaman who can help discreetly, but the shamans he has approached privately have either refused or demanded he report to the chief immediately. Urutu is running out of time because the chief's son's behavior is becoming harder to conceal, and the night-patrol schedule is the only cover he has for the visits.

payload.summary: A large, spotted jaguar beast-kin who walks Iara's perimeter at night with a club and a lantern and who has never once been found sleeping on duty.
payload.appearance: Large and heavily spotted, with a guard's watchful posture. Wears reinforced hide and carries a heavy club. His night vision is extraordinary — he rarely needs the lantern.

visual_identity.body_build: large and heavily muscled, built for presence and endurance
visual_identity.hair: tawny-black with heavy rosette spotting from scalp to shoulders
visual_identity.eyes: amber, vertical-pupiled, reflecting light in darkness
distinctive_features: heavy jaguar-spot rosette patterning across the entire body
a guard's tattoo — a circle with a line — on the right shoulder
elongated canines

desires: To save his friend from whatever is possessing or cursing him
To find a shaman willing to help discreetly before the behavior becomes public
fears_or_limits: That his friend is beyond saving and he will have to choose between loyalty and duty
That covering for his friend makes him complicit in whatever the possession causes

entries.name: Lago Little-Fin
entries.gm_notes: An eight-year-old Mizuhito boy who is one of the four river-born children secretly placed by the midwife Ondina. Lago does not know his own origin, but he has always been different: he can breathe underwater for short periods (unusual even among Mizuhito, who can hold their breath for long stretches but cannot truly breathe water), he never cries, and he can find fresh water by smell across remarkable distances. Recently, Lago has started having dreams about a place deep in the river — a chamber beneath the water with a stone door — and he has been trying to describe it to his parents using drawings. His parents are confused and a little frightened. Ondina, who visits the family regularly, recognized the drawings immediately and has been trying to discourage Lago from sharing them, which has made the boy secretive. He has started sneaking to the river at night to listen to the water.

payload.summary: A small, blue-skinned Mizuhito boy who is always near the water, never cries, and has started drawing pictures of something he sees in his dreams.
payload.appearance: Small and sleek, perpetually damp. Always near the water's edge. Carries a piece of charcoal for drawing on bark.

visual_identity.hair: dark blue-green, fine, clinging to the skull
distinctive_features: blue-green skin with faint mottling
webbed fingers and toes, still developing
incipient gill-slits along the ribcage, more pronounced than typical Mizuhito children

desires: To find the place in his dreams and see if it is real
To make Ondina explain why his drawings frighten her
fears_or_limits: Being kept away from the water
The dark shapes he sometimes sees moving beneath the platform at night

entries.name: Pedra Fire-Stone
entries.gm_notes: A human potter who specializes in fire-resistant cooking vessels and who maintains the kilns used by the community. He is Argila's younger brother and works alongside her, though their relationship has been strained since he noticed she has been acting secretive and hiding something in her home. He does not know about the clay-child, but he has heard sounds from her locked storeroom and has assumed she is hoarding a special clay deposit. His own secret: he has been experimenting with a glazing technique using a mineral he found near the temple ruins — a metallic oxide that produces a stunning deep blue glaze but which, he has realized, gives off a faint spirit-resonance when fired. The glazed pots seem to attract insects and small animals, which gather near them inexplicably. He has been testing whether the resonance can be controlled or directed, and he has started sleeping next to a glazed pot to see if it affects his dreams. It does — vividly — and the dreams are not entirely his own.

payload.summary: A broad, soot-stained human man who fires kilns and makes cooking pots alongside his sister Argila, and who has been experimenting with unusual glazes.
payload.appearance: Broad and soot-darkened, with burn scars on his forearms. Works shirtless near the heat of the kilns. His hands are permanently stained with mineral colors.

visual_identity.body_build: broad and sturdy, heat-tolerant from kiln work
visual_identity.hair: black, singed short, perpetually ash-dusted
distinctive_features: kiln-burn scarring on both forearms, layered and old
deep blue mineral staining on the fingers from glaze work
a permanent faint smokiness to his scent

desires: To understand the spirit-resonance of the blue glaze and what it means
To find out what his sister is hiding without damaging their relationship
fears_or_limits: That the dreams from the glazed pots are not benign and are reshaping his mind
That whatever Argila is hiding is dangerous and he is the only one who has noticed

entries.name: Sávio River-Reader
entries.gm_notes: A human guide who leads expeditions into the rainforest for traders, hunters, and diplomats, and who is known for reading the river's mood — he can predict floods, find channels, and sense danger before it arrives. His secret: he lost his entire first expedition party seven years ago to a flash flood that he did not predict. He tells people it was an unprecedented event, but the truth is he was overconfident and ignored warning signs he should have recognized. Three people died. He has been carrying the guilt ever since and has become hyper-vigilant to the point of anxiety — he sometimes turns expeditions back at the first sign of questionable conditions, which has cost him clients and reputation. Recently, a group of outsiders — the same ones the basket weaver Petala has been observing — has hired him to guide them to the upper tributaries, and he is torn between the money and the conviction that their intentions are not what they claim.

payload.summary: A lean, watchful human man who reads the river like a book and guides expeditions through the rainforest with a cautious, methodical hand.
payload.appearance: Lean and weathered, with a guide's cautious eyes. Wears practical travel gear and carries a walking staff with river-markings. Always checking the water, the sky, the current.

visual_identity.body_build: lean and weathered, built for river travel
visual_identity.hair: black, greying, cut short and practical
visual_identity.eyes: hazel, watchful, with a nervous edge
distinctive_features: a faded river-tattoo of a fish on the left forearm from his youth
a slight tremor in the hands that appears when the water rises

desires: To atone for the expedition he lost by never losing another person
To refuse the outsiders' offer without revealing that he suspects their motives
fears_or_limits: That his caution will cost him his livelihood and he will no longer be able to guide
That guiding the outsiders will lead to harm he could have prevented

entries.name: Aja Bone-Remember
entries.gm_notes: An elder who keeps the tribal genealogies and historical records through oral tradition and carved bone-tablets. He can recite the lineage of every family in the region back eight generations. His secret: the genealogies contain a deliberate alteration he made thirty years ago, at the request of a dying chief who asked him to erase a branch of the family tree — a branch that included a child born of an affair between the chief's wife and a spirit-talker. Aja erased the child from the records, and the child — now a grown adult living in a distant city-state — does not know their true parentage. The erased branch has recently become relevant because the current chief is dying without a clear heir, and the erased child — if their lineage were known — would be the most legitimate successor. Aja is the only person who knows, and he is being pressured by the chief's advisors to identify the rightful heir.

payload.summary: A thin, precise human elder who keeps the oral genealogies and carved bone-records of the Verdania tribes and can recite family lines back centuries.
payload.appearance: Thin and precise, with a scholar's bearing despite living in a rainforest. Wears simple robes and carries bone tablets in a woven satchel. His memory is legendary.

visual_identity.hair: white, fine, worn short
distinctive_features: carved bone bead necklace marking his office as genealogist
a slight tremor in the right hand from age

desires: To do the right thing regarding the erased heir before he dies
To honor the promise he made to the dying chief thirty years ago
fears_or_limits: That revealing the altered genealogy will undermine trust in all the records he keeps
That the wrong person will inherit the chiefdom and the tribe will fracture

entries.name: Tito Feather-Bound
entries.gm_notes: A human feather worker who repairs and maintains Quilla's headdresses — a secondary role that he performs with quiet pride, though he is often overshadowed by Quilla's fame. His secret: he has been in love with Quilla since they were apprentices together, and he has watched her become increasingly anxious and haunted over the past three years without understanding why. He has noticed that the headdresses she produces have become slightly different — the spirit-resonance in them has weakened — and he suspects she is holding something back, deliberately reducing the power of her work. He has been quietly researching feather-spirit lore on his own to understand what could cause the change, and he has found references to a spirit-bargain that produces exactly the pattern he observes: a craftsperson weakening their own work to starve a spirit that feeds on it. He does not know which spirit or what the bargain entails, but he is assembling the picture and is determined to confront Quilla — out of love, not accusation.

payload.summary: A quiet, deft-handed human man who repairs and maintains ceremonial feather-work in Quilla's workshop and who knows every feather in every headdress by touch.
payload.appearance: Quiet and deft, with stained fingers and a gentle demeanor. Works in the back of Quilla's workshop, rarely seen by clients. Feathers cling to his clothing.

visual_identity.body_build: medium and soft-handed, built for delicate craft work
visual_identity.hair: black, short, always with a few stray feathers caught in it
distinctive_features: feather-down dust lightly coating the shoulders
a feather-scar on the left index finger from a binding-needle

desires: To help Quilla with whatever burden she carries, even if she never loves him back
To understand the feather-spirit lore well enough to break a spirit-bargain if needed
fears_or_limits: That confronting Quilla will push her away and he will lose even the proximity he has
That whatever is haunting Quilla is too powerful for him to help with

entries.name: Iuri Moonflower
entries.gm_notes: Yara Moonflower's eighteen-year-old granddaughter, being groomed to inherit the shamanic lineage of the Teluna tribe. Iuri is genuinely gifted — she can hear spirits clearly and has a natural talent for the pact-rituals that surpass even her grandmother's at the same age. Her secret: she has been having recurring dreams of the Moonflower Pact from the perspective of the Mother of Jaguars, and in those dreams the Mother is not corrupted — she is trapped. Iuri believes the Pact is not a bargain but a cage, and that the offerings are not feeding the Mother but keeping her imprisoned. She has been secretly communicating with the Mother of Jaguars through dreams and has begun to sympathize with it, believing her grandmother is wrong about the corruption. Iuri is planning to offer herself at the next ritual — not as a sacrifice, but as a key, to free the Mother. She does not realize that the thing communicating with her through the dreams may be the very corruption her grandmother fears, wearing the Mother's face.

payload.summary: A young jaguar beast-kin woman with piercing amber eyes and a quiet intensity, being trained as the next shaman of the Teluna tribe.
payload.appearance: Young and intense, with faint spotted patterning just emerging along her temples. Wears apprentice's garments — simpler than her grandmother's but marked with the same moonflower symbols. Always watching, always listening.

visual_identity.body_build: lithe and alert, built for both study and rainforest travel
visual_identity.hair: tawny-black with emerging rosette patterning at the temples
visual_identity.eyes: bright amber-gold, vertical pupils, unusually piercing
distinctive_features: faint jaguar-spot patterning emerging at the temples and jawline
a crescent-moon birthmark on the right palm, mirroring her grandmother's scar
incipient elongated canines

desires: To free the Mother of Jaguars from what she believes is a cage
To prove herself worthy of the shamanic lineage in her own way, not just her grandmother's
fears_or_limits: That her grandmother is right about the corruption and she is being deceived
That acting on her beliefs will break her grandmother's heart and fracture the tribe

entries.name: Sigrid Hallvarsdottir
entries.gm_notes: Jarl Sigrid did not inherit this fjord — she took it. Her older brother Hallvar died on a raid eleven years ago, and the thingmenn expected his widow, a weak man named Torsten, to claim the seat. Sigrid stood at the Althing with her brother's axe in her hand and named herself jarl before anyone could object. What no one knows: she found her brother's body before anyone else, and he was not killed by foreign blades. He was stabbed in the back — by Torsten — in a quarrel over the raid's plunder. Sigrid has kept Torsten alive and under her thumb ever since, using the threat of revelation to keep him compliant and broken. She has never told anyone, not even her sister Gerd. The secret is a leash, but also a wound: she genuinely loved her brother, and she lives with the knowledge that the man who killed him eats at her table.

payload.summary: The jarl of Skaldvik, who rules her fjord from the high seat of the mead hall with a voice that carries over storms and a memory that forgives nothing.
