payload.appearance: Tall and commanding, Sigrid wears a fur-trimmed cloak of deep blue over ringmail when she sits the high seat. Her silver-blonde hair is braided in the warrior-knot, and a brooch of polished iron — her brother's, reforged — pins her cloak. She speaks deliberately, as though every word is a stone she is placing in a wall.

visual_identity.hair: silver-blonde, worn in a tight warrior-knot
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a long scar from left temple to jaw, three fingers on her right hand have old break-calluses

desires: to hold Skaldvik secure against the ambitions of rival jarls and pass it intact to someone she trusts
to one day tell her brother's killer exactly why she kept him alive — and then let the axe fall
fears_or_limits: that the fjord's prosperity has made it a target and the other jarls are circling
that keeping Torsten's secret has made her something colder than she meant to become

entries.name: Astrid Blacktide
entries.gm_notes: Astrid commands the longship Frostwing and has led six successful raids down the southern coasts. What no one knows is that on her last raid she spared a southern village — burned its ships but left its people alive — because she recognized a woman among them as her birth mother. Astrid was told her mother died in childbirth. The woman called her by a different name, a southern name, and Astrid fled before anyone could see her hesitate. She has told her crew the village was already empty. She does not know if her mother is truly who she appeared to be, or if the resemblance was a trick of firelight and memory. She is planning another raid in the same waters — ostensibly for plunder, actually to find out the truth.

payload.summary: A shieldmaiden and raid captain whose fame on the waves is matched only by the silence she keeps about the one village she let stand.
payload.appearance: Battle-worn and weather-darkened, Astrid wears a byrnie of iron rings over leather, her shield slung across her back — black with a white wave-painted crest. Her hair is cropped short on the sides, long at the back, and she carries two axes at her belt like other people carry eating knives.

visual_identity.body_build: lean and corded with muscle, built for endurance
visual_identity.hair: dark auburn, shaved sides, long braid at the back
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a bite-shaped scar on her right shoulder (a wound from a shield-bite in her first duel), a thin gold ring in her left ear

desires: to learn whether the woman in the burning village was truly her mother
to keep her crew's trust — which depends on her never hesitating again
fears_or_limits: that her blood is half-southern and her crew would see her differently if they knew
that mercy on a raid is a crack that spreads until the whole shield breaks

entries.name: Yrsa Fogborn
entries.gm_notes: Yrsa is a volva — a seeress who walks between worlds in trance. She is genuinely gifted: her prophecies are fragmentary but real, drawn from the seidr trance. The secret she guards: three years ago she saw, in a deep trance, a vision of Skaldvik burning — not from raiders, but from within. A fire set deliberately during the Althing, when every jarl would be present. She did not see who sets it, only that the spark comes from someone who sits at Jarl Sigrid's own table. She has been watching the jarl's household ever since, waiting for the pattern to clarify. She has not told Sigrid because the last time she warned a jarl, that jarl used the warning to preemptively kill three innocent people. Yrsa does not trust power with prophecy.

payload.summary: A volva who reads runes in the smoke of offerings and walks the border between the living and the dead, answering questions no one else can answer — and asking some she will not share.
payload.appearance: Gaunt and draped in layers of dark wool and reindeer fur, Yrsa moves like smoke through the market. Her staff is ironwood tipped with a raven skull, and she carries a pouch of runestones that click when she walks. Her eyes are pale and unfocused, as though she is always half-looking at something behind the world.

visual_identity.body_build: thin and angular, weathered by decades of trance-cold
visual_identity.hair: white, long, loose and uncombed
visual_identity.distinctive_features: seidr-ritual scars in concentric rings on both inner wrists, a missing left eye (empty socket covered by a patch of dark leather)

desires: to see clearly enough to prevent the burning of Skaldvik without causing another massacre
to find an apprentice who can carry the sight before the trances take her mind entirely
fears_or_limits: that each trance brings her closer to not coming back
that prophecy in the hands of the powerful becomes a weapon against the innocent

entries.name: Greta Keelson
entries.gm_notes: Greta is Skaldvik's most gifted shipwright, and she has a secret method for clinker-planking that produces hulls lighter and faster than any other yard. She learned the technique from her late master, who learned it from a captured southern shipwright — a man who was a thrall in the yard for twenty years and died never seeing his homeland again. Greta has been told the technique is a Hrafnland tradition. She discovered the truth when she found her master's journal, which included the southern man's name and drawings of his home port. She does not know whether to reveal the origin — it would shame the shipbuilding tradition and possibly turn the whole yard's reputation sour — or to keep building ships on a dead man's stolen knowledge.

payload.summary: A shipwright whose hands shape the fastest longships on the fjord, working from plans she now knows were never truly theirs to claim.
payload.appearance: Stocky and sawdust-covered, Greta works in a leather vest with her sleeves permanently rolled. Shavings cling to her arms and hair, and she carries a adze and a measuring rope looped over her shoulder. She talks to her ships as she builds them, naming each plank.

visual_identity.body_build: broad and muscular from years of timber work
visual_identity.hair: sandy brown, cut short and practical
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a missing half of her left little finger (saw accident), deep calluses across both palms with a permanent ink stain on her right thumb

desires: to build a ship so fine it would make even the dead southern shipwright proud
to find the man's family — if any survive — and tell them what he built
fears_or_limits: that revealing the truth will destroy the yard's reputation and the livelihoods of everyone who works there
that she is building glory on a grave and will never be free of the guilt

entries.name: Maren Saltgrief
entries.gm_notes: Maren is the navigator aboard the Frostwing, and she can read stars, currents, and bird-flight with uncanny accuracy. Her secret: she has been losing her sight. The colors are going first — she can no longer reliably distinguish the red channel-marker buoys from the green ones at dusk. She has memorized their positions by number and uses sound and wave-slope to compensate. She has not told Astrid because she knows Astrid would ground her, and the sea is the only life Maren can stand. She is quietly teaching her younger cousin the star-charts, preparing for the day she cannot hide it anymore, but the cousin is more interested in boys than in navigation.

payload.summary: A navigator who steers by stars she can barely still see, holding the course of a ship and a life she knows she cannot keep forever.
payload.appearance: Lean and salt-wind-burned, Maren wears a sealskin coat over wool, a chart-roller slung across her back. She squints at the horizon more than she used to and tilts her head toward the wind as though listening to it. Her hands move constantly, tracing invisible maps on any flat surface.

visual_identity.body_build: wiry and tall, built for the open deck
visual_identity.hair: pale blonde, bleached nearly white by salt and sun, worn in two thin braids
visual_identity.eyes: pale blue, slightly clouded at the edges
visual_identity.distinctive_features: frost-nip scars on the tip of her nose and both ears, a faded tattoo of the North Star on her left inner wrist

desires: to make one last perfect crossing — a voyage so clean no one will ever question whether she was fit to lead it
to find someone who actually wants to learn the stars before the stars go dark for her
fears_or_limits: that she will misread a marker and sail the Frostwing onto rocks
that the day she admits her blindness is the day she becomes no one

entries.name: Helga Deepnet
entries.gm_notes: Helga fishes the deep waters of the fjord and has pulled up things from the bottom that no one else has seen. Six months ago she dredged up a runestone in her nets — not a carved memorial, but a seidr-stone, pulsing faintly with cold light. It is not of Hrafnland make; the runes on it are older than any she has seen, and they are warm to the touch even in frozen water. She has hidden it in the bait shed, wrapped in oilskin. Since she brought it up, the fish in the deep channel have changed — they swim in patterns, spirals, as though circling something. She has not told Yrsa, because Yrsa would take the stone, and Helga feels — irrationally, she knows — that the stone wants to stay with her. It hums when she is near it.

payload.summary: A fisher who knows the fjord's depths better than anyone alive, and who pulled something up from the bottom that was perhaps better left sleeping.
payload.appearance: Compact and weather-beaten, Helga wears oilskin over thick wool and rubber boots that go to her knees. She smells of fish and salt and tar. Her hands are enormous for her size, cracked and red from cold water and rope work.

visual_identity.body_build: short and broad, powerful arms and hands
visual_identity.hair: dark brown, greying at the temples, worn in a practical single braid
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a rope-burn scar across both palms, a chipped front tooth, a small blue tattoo of a fish-hook on her right knuckle

desires: to understand what the stone is before it does something she cannot undo
to keep fishing the deep channel, because the spiraling fish are the largest she has ever caught
fears_or_limits: that the stone is calling something up from the bottom that is not fish
that her compulsion to keep it is not her own will but the stone's

entries.name: Brita Whalejaw
entries.gm_notes: Brita is the most experienced whaler in Skaldvik, and she has killed seventeen whales in her career. Her secret: two years ago, during a hunt, a great whale surfaced directly beneath her boat and did not capsize it. It could have. It chose not to. It looked at her — she swears it looked at her — and then it dove, and she let it go. She told her crew she lost it in the fog. Since that day she has continued to hunt, but every whale she kills makes her feel like a murderer. She has begun to sabotage her own hunts — misreading the weather, misjudging the strike angle — and her crew is starting to whisper that she has lost her nerve. She cannot tell them the truth. A whaler who thinks whales are people does not whale.

payload.summary: A whaler whose harpoon has never missed, and who now flinches every time she throws it — haunted by the eye of a whale that chose to spare her.
payload.appearance: Massive and blunt-featured, Brita wears a heavy sealskin coat stained with old blood and blubber oil. She carries a harpoon as easily as others carry a walking stick, and her arms are scarred from rope-burns and the thrashing of dying whales. She has a booming voice that she has begun to use less often.

visual_identity.body_build: very tall and heavily built, raw power
visual_identity.hair: grey-blonde, thick, worn loose under a leather cap
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a white scar across her collarbone from a harpoon line that snapped, three teeth replaced with carved whalebone

desires: to find a way to stop hunting without losing her crew's respect or her livelihood
to understand why the whale spared her — whether it was intelligence or mercy or something else
fears_or_limits: that her crew will replace her with someone who still kills without hesitation
that she has earned something by being spared that she is wasting by continuing to kill

entries.name: Sigunn Ironbar
entries.gm_notes: Sigunn is a trader who sails between Skaldvik and the southern ports, exchanging furs, whale oil, and iron for grain, cloth, and luxury goods. Her secret: she has been quietly smuggling runestones out of Hrafnland for a southern collector who pays extraordinarily well. The runestones are not seidr-stones — they are memorial stones from abandoned fjord settlements, stones that commemorated dead families whose descendants are gone. Sigunn tells herself she is selling stones that no one cares about anymore. But she knows that at least two of the stones she sold were not abandoned — they were standing in living settlements, and she had her crew take them in the night. The southern collector is asking for more.

payload.summary: A trader whose ledgers are meticulous and whose cargo manifests never quite match what is actually in the hold, because some things are easier to sell when no one is watching.
payload.appearance: Sharp-eyed and well-dressed by Hrafnland standards, Sigunn wears a good wool coat with silver clasps and keeps her hair under a trader's scarf. She carries a leather satchel of contracts and a small scale for weighing silver, and she always seems to be calculating.

visual_identity.hair: reddish-brown, worn under a dark blue trader's scarf
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a trader's mark tattooed on her right forearm (a small anchor and coin), a thin silver chain around her neck

desires: to make enough wealth to buy a warehouse and never sail in winter again
to stop the runestone trade before she sells something that cannot be replaced — but the money is too good
fears_or_limits: that Yrsa or another volva will trace the stolen stones back to her
that the southern collector will escalate his demands to something far more dangerous than memorial stones

entries.name: Tove Brewhollow
entries.gm_notes: Tove runs the cookfire in Jarl Sigrid's mead hall, feeding the household and any traveler who sits at the long table. Her secret: she is the daughter of a jarl from a neighboring fjord — Fjord Ull, two days north — who was deposed and killed in a blood feud when Tove was twelve. Her mother fled with her to Skaldvik and raised her as a cook's daughter, changing their names. Tove does not want to reclaim her fjord or her name. She is genuinely content as a cook. But the men who killed her father are still alive, and one of them — a jarl named Hakon — comes to Skaldvik for the Althing every year and sits at Sigrid's table. Tove serves him bread and stew and has never once let her hand shake. She does not know what she would do if he recognized her, and she does not know what she wants to happen.

payload.summary: A cook who feeds the jarl's hall with generous hands and steady nerves, and who serves bread every year to the man who killed her father without ever letting him see that she knows.
payload.appearance: Sturdy and flour-dusted, Tove wears a clean apron over a plain wool dress, her sleeves rolled past her elbows. She moves through the kitchen with brisk authority, tasting everything, adjusting seasoning by instinct. Her face is round and open, the kind that looks like it has never hidden anything.

visual_identity.hair: chestnut brown, worn in two braids pinned up under a cap
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a small knife-scar on her left thumb, a faded burn-mark on her right forearm shaped like a ladle

desires: to keep cooking in Sigrid's hall and live a quiet life — which means keeping her identity buried forever
to decide, before the next Althing, whether she wants Hakon to live or die, because she cannot hold both wishes at once
fears_or_limits: that Hakon will recognize her — or worse, that her own composure will crack and she will give herself away
that her mother, who is aging and beginning to forget what is safe to say, will mention Fjord Ull in the wrong company

entries.name: Ragna Forgebreak
entries.gm_notes: Ragna is a smith who works iron, bronze, and a little silver. Her secret: she has been forging counterfeit trade-ingots — iron bars stamped with the mark of a rival fjord's smithy and secretly introduced into the trade flow. The counterfeit bars are slightly underweight, and the difference accumulates into real silver when traded in bulk. She does this not for herself but to fund a dowry for her daughter, who is promised to a shipwright's family that expects a substantial bride-price. Ragna is two bars short of the full amount. She is terrified of being caught — counterfeiting is a crime the Althing punishes with outlawry — but she sees no other way to pay what is expected.

payload.summary: A smith whose forge burns hot and whose ingots always bear the right stamps — though not always the right metal, or the right weight.
payload.appearance: Broad and soot-blackened, Ragna wears a leather smith's apron over rolled sleeves, her forearms laced with old burn scars. She works with focused intensity, hammer rising and falling in a rhythm the whole street can hear. Her hair is singed short at the edges from sparks.

visual_identity.hair: dark brown, singed short at the edges, worn tied back
visual_identity.distinctive_features: lattice of burn scars across both forearms, a crushed-looking left thumb from an old hammer strike

desires: to pay her daughter's bride-price and see her settled and safe
to stop counterfeiting before the Althing or the rival smith catches on
fears_or_limits: that discovery will mean outlawry — banishment from Hrafnland, which is a death sentence in winter
that her daughter will learn how the bride-price was paid and refuse it

entries.name: Eira Nighttorch
entries.gm_notes: Eira is a skald who carries the oral histories of Skaldvik in her memory — genealogies, raid-sagas, law-verses, and jokes. Her secret: she has been composing a saga about Jarl Sigrid's brother Hallvar — a true saga, telling the story of his death honestly, including the detail that he was stabbed in the back by someone in his own household. She has not named the killer in the verses, but anyone who knows the household would recognize the clues. She does not know that Sigrid already knows who killed Hallvar. Eira believes she is the only one who has puzzled it out. She has not decided whether to perform the saga — doing so at the Althing would shake Skaldvik to its foundations.

payload.summary: A skald whose memory holds the sagas of three generations, and who has been quietly composing a verse that could split Skaldvik's ruling house like a frozen hull.
payload.appearance: Slender and quick-tongued, Eira wears a dark blue poet's robe embroidered with wave-patterns at the hem. She carries a small harp and a pouch of memory-stones — smooth pebbles she associates with specific sagas, touching each before reciting. Her voice is clear and carrying, trained to fill a mead hall.

visual_identity.hair: black, long, worn loose when performing, braided otherwise
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a poet's ink-mark on her right cheekbone (a small rune for 'voice'), a chipped left canine

desires: to tell the true story — because a skald who hides the truth is no skald at all
to survive telling it, which is by no means certain
fears_or_limits: that performing the saga will get her killed or outlawed — or that it will destroy the only home she has
that she is wrong about who killed Hallvar, and a false saga is worse than no saga

entries.name: Hilla Snowstep
entries.gm_notes: Hilla hunts the mountain forests above Skaldvik for deer, elk, and occasionally bear. Her secret: she has found tracks in the high passes that are not bear, not elk, not human — tracks that are enormous, three-toed, and pressed deep into frozen ground by something very heavy. She followed them for half a day before the trail entered a ravine that smelled of old ice and something else — something alive. She turned back. She has not told anyone because the obvious explanation is a frost giant, and reporting a frost giant sighting would bring hunters, warriors, and possibly a jarl's expedition into the mountains — and Hilla does not believe the giant is a threat. It was avoiding the settlement, staying high, staying hidden. She thinks it is alone and possibly wounded.

payload.summary: A hunter who reads the mountain snow like a page of text, and who has read something in it recently that she is not sure anyone else should know.
payload.appearance: Lean and snow-pale, Hilla wears white-fur camouflage over wool, a bow across her back and a belt knife at her hip. She moves silently even on crusty snow, her boots carefully wrapped. Her face is wind-burned and watchful, and she speaks rarely and briefly.

visual_identity.body_build: lean and long-limbed, built for stalking and endurance
visual_identity.hair: pale blonde, worn in a single tight braid
visual_identity.distinctive_features: frost-scar on her right cheek, a crooked nose (broken and healed), a bow-callus on her left fingers

desires: to find out what the giant is and why it is alone — without bringing a war party into the mountains
to be left alone to hunt in the high passes, which is the only place she feels right
fears_or_limits: that the giant is not peaceful and her instinct to protect it will get people killed
that if she says nothing and the giant descends, the blood will be on her hands

entries.name: Dis Lea
entries.gm_notes: Dis is an herbalist who tends a garden of medicinal plants behind her house and gathers wild herbs from the fjord slopes. Her secret: she has been treating a man she believes is a frost giant half-breed — a man named Orm who lives alone on the far side of the fjord, who is nearly seven feet tall, who never comes to town, and whose skin is cold to the touch even in summer. He came to her a year ago with a wound that would not heal, and she has been bringing him medicine ever since. She does not know his full story. She does know that if anyone discovered him, the fear and hatred directed at giant-blood would make his life — and hers, for sheltering him — very short.

payload.summary: An herbalist whose garden grows remedies for everything from frostbite to fever, and whose most unusual patient has never been seen by anyone else in Skaldvik.
payload.appearance: Small and earthy, Dis wears a moss-green dress with pockets full of dried herbs and seed packets. Her hair is tied with twine and she always has dirt under her nails. She carries a gathering basket and a small bone-handled knife, and she talks to her plants as she walks through the garden.

visual_identity.body_build: small and wiry, strong for her size
visual_identity.hair: dark brown, long, tied with twine
visual_identity.distinctive_features: permanently green-stained fingertips, a round birthmark on her left forearm shaped like a leaf

desires: to heal Orm's wound and help him find a way to live without hiding
to keep her garden thriving through another winter
fears_or_limits: that someone will follow her to Orm's hiding place and the discovery will end in violence
that Orm's wound is not natural and no herb will ever fully heal it

entries.name: Kata Mossheart
entries.gm_notes: Kata is the midwife of Skaldvik, who has brought nearly every living person under thirty into the world. Her secret: she has been falsifying birth records — not for money, but to protect children. Three children born in the last decade are technically the offspring of married women who were not married to the men they were with when the child was conceived. Kata recorded the husband's name in each case, because exposing the truth would have meant shame, violence, or abandonment for the mother and child. She carries the true parentage in her head alone. One of those children is now showing traits — a birthmark, a talent, a temperament — that the nominal father's bloodline does not explain, and the husband is starting to ask questions.

payload.summary: A midwife who has caught every baby in Skaldvik for twenty years and who carries more family secrets in her head than any living person — including some she made herself.
payload.appearance: Weathered and warm, Kata wears a clean wool dress with a shawl she can wrap around anything — a cold infant, a laboring mother, her own shoulders. Her hands are gentle and sure, and she carries a bundle of clean cloth and a small knife for cutting cords. She smells of soap and lavender.

visual_identity.hair: grey, thick, pinned in a practical coil
visual_identity.eyes: warm brown, deeply lined at the corners
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a mole on her left cheek, a slight curvature of the spine from decades of leaning over beds

desires: to protect the three families whose secrets she holds — even from themselves
to train a successor before her hands get too stiff for the work
fears_or_limits: that the questioning husband will force the truth out and the child will be the one who suffers
that one of her false records will cause a bloodline dispute at the Althing and she will have to lie under oath

entries.name: Siv Frostborn
entries.gm_notes: Siv is a healer who combines herbalism with seidr — a rare and somewhat feared practice. She can ease pain, slow bleeding, and once set a broken bone that three other healers said would never heal straight. Her secret: her seidr healing does not come from training. It comes from a bargain her mother made with something in the fjord — a spirit, a creature, or something older — when Siv was dying of fever as an infant. Siv does not know the full terms of the bargain. She knows her healing gift costs something: every time she uses it deeply, she loses a small memory — a face, a name, a day from her childhood. She has been healing for fifteen years, and her early memories are now full of holes.

payload.summary: A healer whose hands carry warmth that ordinary fire does not explain, and who pays for every miracle with a piece of herself she cannot get back.
payload.appearance: Quiet and slightly fragile-looking, Siv wears a white wool dress — the healer's color — with a grey shawl. Her hands are always warm, even in the coldest weather, and she keeps them pressed together when not working, as if holding something in. She sometimes pauses mid-sentence with a look of confusion, then continues.

visual_identity.body_build: slender and slightly frail-looking, deceptively strong
visual_identity.hair: white-blonde, fine, worn loose
visual_identity.eyes: pale blue, distant and sometimes confused
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a faint shimmer in her skin when she heals (barely visible, like heat-haze), a small scar on her left palm from a ritual cut

desires: to find out what her mother's bargain was and whether it can be renegotiated
to heal one more person without losing another piece of her past — though she knows she cannot stop
fears_or_limits: that one day the memories she loses will be the ones that matter most — the faces of the people she loves
that the thing in the fjord will come to collect the full debt, not just memories

entries.name: Ingrid Watchpeak
entries.gm_notes: Ingrid commands Jarl Sigrid's household guard — twelve warriors who keep order in Skaldvik and protect the jarl's hall. Her secret: she has been approached by an emissary from Jarl Hakon of Fjord Ull, who offered her silver and land to betray Sigrid — specifically, to leave the jarl's hall unguarded on a night during the coming Althing. Ingrid refused and reported the approach to Sigrid, but she did not tell Sigrid the full truth: the emissary also told her that her father, who she believed died honorably in battle, was actually executed as a coward for fleeing a fight. Hakon's people have records. Ingrid does not know if it is true, but the possibility has shaken her loyalty to its roots — not because she would betray Sigrid, but because she fears the shame would make the guard lose faith in her if it came out.

payload.summary: A guard captain who has held the jarl's trust for fifteen years, and who now carries a question about her own bloodline that could unmake everything she has built.
payload.appearance: Solid and watchful, Ingrid wears ringmail and a white cloak — the guard's color — with a longsword at her hip and a shield painted with Skaldvik's raven crest. She stands at the jarl's right hand in the hall and walks the walls every morning and evening, counting faces, checking gates. She never drinks on duty and rarely drinks off it.

visual_identity.body_build: medium height, broad and solid, built to stand firm
visual_identity.hair: red-gold, cropped short
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a scar across her left eyebrow (sword cut), a guard's tattoo of a raven on her right shoulder

desires: to discover the truth about her father's death without destroying her own reputation
to keep Sigrid alive through the Althing, which she fears will be more dangerous than usual
fears_or_limits: that her father was a coward and the shame is in her blood
that refusing Hakon once will not be enough — the next approach will not be an offer but a threat

entries.name: Gerd Hallvarsdottir
entries.gm_notes: Gerd is Jarl Sigrid's younger sister, and she manages the jarl's farmstead — the herds, the fields, the storehouses that feed the household through winter. Her secret: she is in love with a woman — Vigdis, the rope maker — and they have been meeting secretly for three years. Gerd has not told Sigrid because she fears her sister will see it as a political liability: a jarl's sister who will not make a marriage alliance is a tool gone blunt. Gerd also fears that if Sigrid finds out, she will not be angry — she will be practical, and the practical response will be to arrange a marriage for Gerd anyway. Gerd would rather stay hidden than be managed.

payload.summary: The jarl's sister, who runs the farmstead with quiet competence and hides a love that her sister's politics would not allow her to keep.
payload.appearance: Sturdy and sun-weathered for Hrafnland, Gerd wears a practical wool dress with a leather belt full of tools — a pruning knife, a counting-string, a key to the storehouse. She moves with the easy confidence of someone who knows the land is hers to tend, and her hands are always busy.

visual_identity.hair: silver-blonde like her sister's, worn in a single thick braid
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a farmer's tan (rare in Hrafnland — darker skin from long outdoor hours), a old hay-scar on her left hand

desires: to live openly with Vigdis without losing her place in her sister's hall
to make the farmstead productive enough that she is valued for her work, not just her bloodline
fears_or_limits: that Sigrid will arrange a political marriage and Gerd will have to choose between obedience and love
that Vigdis will grow tired of secrecy and leave

entries.name: Thora Linenhand
entries.gm_notes: Thora makes sails for every longship in Skaldvik — enormous panels of linen and wool, dyed in stripes of red and white. Her secret: the sailcloth she makes is woven with a technique her mother taught her that includes a single thread of different material — a hair-thin strand of something that is not linen, not wool, and that Thora has never been able to identify. Her mother said it was 'sail-soul' and that a sail without it would tear in the first storm. Thora believes it, because her sails have never torn. She has a limited supply of the thread, given to her by her mother in a sealed box, and she does not know where to get more. When it runs out, she will either have to make inferior sails or discover the source — which her mother never revealed, even on her deathbed.

payload.summary: A sail maker whose sails have never failed in a storm, and who does not know what makes them hold — only that the secret is running out.
payload.appearance: Tall and rawboned, Thora works in a sail loft that smells of linen and tallow. She wears a canvas apron over rough clothes and moves among the vast spread of sailcloth like a sailor on a deck — sure-footed, scanning the fabric for flaws. Her hands are pale and smooth from handling cloth, which is unusual in Skaldvik.

visual_identity.hair: light brown, thinning, worn under a linen cap
visual_identity.distinctive_features: unusually smooth, pale hands for a Hrafnland craftswoman, a small callus on her right palm from sail-needle work

desires: to find the source of the sail-soul thread before her supply runs out
to make one perfect sail — a sail that could carry a ship to the edge of the world and back
fears_or_limits: that the next sail she makes without the thread will fail and people will die
that the source of the thread is something she does not want to know — something her mother hid for a reason

entries.name: Vigdis Ropewright
entries.gm_notes: Vigdis makes rope — anchor rope, fishing line, rigging, and the heavy hawsers that moor longships. Her secret: she is in love with Gerd Hallvarsdottir, the jarl's sister, and they have been meeting in secret for three years. Vigdis is content with secrecy — she is a craftswoman, not a politician, and she does not need public recognition. But she has noticed that Gerd is growing more anxious, and Vigdis fears that the strain of hiding is hurting Gerd more than the revelation would. Vigdis has also been asked, twice, by a jarl's retainer whether she would be interested in marriage — and she has deflected both times, but a third deflection will raise questions she cannot answer without either lying or exposing the truth.

payload.summary: A rope maker whose hands twist hemp and sinew into the lines that hold ships to the earth, and who is quietly tangled in a love she cannot speak of in daylight.
payload.appearance: Strong-armed and sun-roughened, Vigdis works at the ropewalk in a leather apron, her hands moving in the constant twisting rhythm of her trade. She wears her hair short — it catches in the hemp otherwise — and her forearms are roped with muscle and old friction-burns. She is quiet, with a dry sense of humor that surfaces when she is comfortable.

visual_identity.body_build: medium height, powerful arms and shoulders
visual_identity.hair: dark brown, cropped short
visual_identity.distinctive_features: rope-burn scars on both forearms in overlapping patterns, a missing tip of her right ring finger (caught in a winch)

desires: to be with Gerd openly, or at least without the fear that secrecy is slowly poisoning them both
to make a rope strong enough to moor the largest longship ever built — a rope that will never snap
fears_or_limits: that a third marriage proposal will force a public answer that endangers Gerd
that she is asking Gerd to choose between family and love, and that is not a fair thing to ask

entries.name: Nanna Woolcoat
entries.gm_notes: Nanna tends a flock of hardy mountain sheep on the high pastures above Skaldvik. Her secret: she has been finding dead sheep — not killed by wolves, not dead from exposure, but drained. The bodies are intact, uninjured, but completely bloodless, as though something fed on them in the night. She has lost seven sheep in two months. She has not reported it because she fears the flock will be blamed — diseased, cursed — and culled, which would ruin her. She has started sleeping in the pasture with the sheep, a loaded bow beside her, but she has not seen what comes. She has heard it, though: a sound like heavy breathing in the dark, and the scrape of something large moving through the heather.

payload.summary: A shepherd who guards her flock with a fierce, sleepless devotion, and who has been lying about what is taking her sheep in the dark.
payload.appearance: Weather-worn and sharp-eyed, Nanna wears a thick wool coat (her namesake) and carries a shepherd's crook and a short bow. She is always with her dogs — three border collies who never leave her side. She has not slept a full night in weeks, and the dark circles under her eyes are visible from across a field.

visual_identity.body_build: lean and wiry, built for long days on the hill
visual_identity.hair: dark brown, thick, worn in a single braid under a wool cap
visual_identity.distinctive_features: dark circles under both eyes (chronic), a sheep-dog bite scar on her right hand (training accident, years old)

desires: to find and kill whatever is draining her sheep before it takes the whole flock
to get one full night of sleep without the sound of breathing in the dark
fears_or_limits: that if she reports the deaths, the flock will be culled and her livelihood destroyed
that whatever is feeding will move from sheep to her — or to someone in the settlement below

entries.name: Edda Cloudcarver
entries.gm_notes: Edda is the eldest person in Skaldvik — old enough to remember stories her grandmother told, stories that go back before the Althing was formalized. Her secret: she knows the location of a thing she calls the 'first stone' — a runestone older than any in Hrafnland, carved in a language no one alive can read, standing in a valley that no map shows. Her grandmother took her there once, when she was eight, and made her swear to never reveal the location unless 'the fjords needed it.' Edda has never been sure what that means. She is now ninety-one, her memory is beginning to fail, and she is terrified that the location will die with her. But the oath was binding, and she does not know what 'the fjords needing it' looks like.

payload.summary: An elder who has lived through nine decades of fjord life and who carries in her fading memory a secret older than the Althing itself.
payload.appearance: Tiny and birdlike, Edda sits by the fire in a chair that is too large for her, wrapped in shawls and furs. Her hands shake slightly, and her voice is thin but sharp when she chooses to use it. She is surrounded by grandchildren and great-grandchildren who bring her food and listen to her stories — most of which they have heard many times.

visual_identity.body_build: very small and frail, shrunken with age
visual_identity.hair: pure white, thin, worn loose
visual_identity.eyes: pale blue, milky but still sharp
visual_identity.distinctive_features: deeply lined face, a pronounced stoop, a faded tattoo of a raven on her left hand (nearly invisible with age)

desires: to find someone worthy of the secret before her memory fails completely
to die knowing the first stone will not be lost — even if she never understands what it is for
fears_or_limits: that she will forget the location of the first stone before she can pass it on
that she will give the secret to the wrong person and the oath will have meant nothing

entries.name: Hjordis Bonebreeze
entries.gm_notes: Hjordis carves bone and antler — dice, combs, needle cases, brooches, and the small decorative panels that decorate longship prows. Her secret: she can carve runes that work. Not the decorative, commemorative runes that most carvers make — actual seidr runes, the kind that hold power. She discovered this accidentally when she carved a ward-rune into a brooch and the wearer stopped getting sick. She has been testing cautiously, carving small runes into everyday objects — a luck-rune on a child's comb, a ward on a sailor's needle case — and the effects are subtle but real. She has not told Yrsa or any other volva, because she has no training and no understanding of what she is doing, and she is afraid that untrained seidr is dangerous — to her and to the people she is trying to help.

payload.summary: A bone carver whose knife brings beauty out of antler and ivory, and whose runes — carved without training, without permission — have started doing something more than decorating.
payload.appearance: Fine-boned and precise, Hjordis works at a low bench surrounded by antler pieces, bone blanks, and carving tools. She wears a leather apron over a simple dress and holds her carving knife with the delicacy of a scribe holding a quill. Her shavings are so fine they look like snow.

visual_identity.body_build: slender and small-boned, precise in movement
visual_identity.hair: light brown, worn in a knot at the nape
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a small knife-scar on her left index finger, permanently pale fingertips from handling bone and antler

desires: to understand the runes she is carving — what they do, why they work, and what the cost is
to find a teacher without exposing herself as an untrained seidr-worker
fears_or_limits: that one of her carved runes will do something she did not intend — hurt someone, attract something, break something
that the volur will see her work as unlicensed seidr and punish her for practicing without training

entries.name: Magna Shieldwall
entries.gm_notes: Magna is a guard in Jarl Sigrid's household, one of the twelve under Captain Ingrid. Her secret: she is the one who has been leaving the hall gate unlatched on certain nights — not for a betrayer, but for her brother, who deserted from a raid three years ago and has been living in the hills, afraid to come home. Magna has been smuggling food to him and letting him sleep in the storage shed on the coldest nights. She knows this is a violation of her oath as a guard, and that if Ingrid discovered it, she would be stripped of her position. Her brother wants to come forward and face the Althing's judgment — desertion is punished by three years' outlawry — but Magna is afraid the shame will destroy their family's name.

payload.summary: A guard who stands the watch with steady eyes and a straight spear, and who leaves one gate unlatched every few nights for a brother the fjord thinks is long gone.
payload.appearance: Solid and square-jawed, Magna wears the white cloak and ringmail of the jarl's guard with a shield on her back and a spear in her hand. She is younger than most of the guard, and she takes the watch more seriously than anyone — because for her, the watch is also a deception.

visual_identity.hair: dark blonde, cropped short under a helm
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a guard's raven tattoo on her right shoulder, a scar on her left knuckles from a training accident

desires: to bring her brother home permanently without destroying the family name
to serve Sigrid honestly — which means she must eventually choose between her oath and her brother
fears_or_limits: that Ingrid will catch her and she will lose everything — her position, her honor, and her brother's safety
that her brother will die in the hills before she can find a way to bring him in from the cold

entries.name: Liva Longwalk
entries.gm_notes: Liva is a messenger who carries news, invitations, and legal summons between the fjords. She knows every trail, every shortcut, every bothy and shelter in Hrafnland. Her secret: she has been carrying messages for Jarl Hakon of Fjord Ull — messages she suspects are part of a conspiracy against Skaldvik. She took the work because Hakon pays well and she needed the silver to pay a healer for her mother's illness. She has read some of the messages (she is not supposed to, but the seals are not complex). The most recent one mentioned 'the Althing fire' and 'the signal.' She does not know what those mean, but they frighten her. She is now carrying a message to Skaldvik itself — to someone inside the jarl's household — and she does not know whether to deliver it or burn it.

payload.summary: A messenger who has walked every fjord path in Hrafnland and who is currently carrying a letter that might be the match that lights a war.
payload.appearance: Lean and tireless, Liva wears travelling clothes — wool, leather, and a waterproof cloak — with a messenger's satchel across her chest. She carries a walking staff and a small knife, nothing more. She is weather-tanned, her face lined from wind and sun, and she moves with the efficient gait of someone who measures distance in days.

visual_identity.body_build: lean and long-legged, built for distance walking
visual_identity.hair: brown, sun-bleached, worn in a tight knot
visual_identity.distinctive_features: road-dust permanently ground into her skin, a messenger's tattoo of a running bird on her right ankle

desires: to deliver the message and keep her reputation as a reliable messenger — or burn it and live with the betrayal
to earn enough to keep her mother in care without taking dangerous work from Hakon
fears_or_limits: that if she burns the message, Hakon will send someone to find out why it was not delivered
that if she delivers it, she will be complicit in whatever 'the Althing fire' means

entries.name: Thyra Wildseed
entries.gm_notes: Thyra is a thrall — a bondservant in Jarl Sigrid's household, captured in a raid on a southern coast village twelve years ago. She was a child then. Her secret: she remembers her birth name, her birth language, and her birth family — things that thralls are expected to forget. She has been pretending to have no memory of her past because a thrall who remembers is a thrall who might try to go home, and the punishment for escape is severe. She has also been quietly teaching her birth language to her own daughter, born in Skaldvik, so that something of who she was will survive. She has saved a small amount of silver — hidden in the wall of the thralls' quarters — and she dreams of buying her freedom, though the price is more than she can imagine earning.

payload.summary: A thrall who serves the jarl's household with quiet competence, and who carries an entire lost life behind her eyes — a name, a language, a home she is not allowed to want.
payload.appearance: Dark-haired and sun-darkened compared to the fair people of Skaldvik, Thyra wears the plain wool of a thrall — undyed, unadorned — and moves through the household with efficient quiet. She is always working: scrubbing, carrying, mending. She speaks Hrafnland well but with an accent she has tried and failed to erase.

visual_identity.body_build: slender and strong from constant labor
visual_identity.hair: dark brown, long, worn in a single plain braid
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a thrall's iron band on her left wrist (engraved with Sigrid's mark), a faded scar on her right forearm from a childhood injury before her capture

desires: to buy her freedom and her daughter's — or to find a way home with both of them
to teach her daughter enough of the old language that the girl will know she comes from somewhere
fears_or_limits: that her hidden silver will be found and confiscated — saving as a thrall is technically illegal
that if she tries to escape and fails, her daughter will be sold away from her

entries.name: Svanhild Frostchild
entries.gm_notes: Svanhild is a child of twelve, the daughter of one of the jarl's household guards. Her secret: she has been having dreams that come true. Small things — a dream about a boat sinking, and the next day a fishing skiff capsizes in the harbor; a dream about a wolf in the byre, and the next morning a fox gets into the goat pen. She has not told anyone because the last child in Skaldvik who 'saw things' was taken to live with the volur, and Svanhild does not want to leave her family. She has started keeping a dream-journal — scratched runes on birch bark, hidden under her sleeping furs — and she is both fascinated and terrified by the pattern she sees forming. Last night she dreamed of fire over the mead hall during a gathering, and the smoke was shaped like a raven.

payload.summary: A child of the jarl's household who plays among the longships and dreams of things that happen the next day, and who has started keeping a record she shows no one.
payload.appearance: Small and fair-haired, Svanhild wears a child's wool tunic and fur-lined boots, her hair in two messy braids. She is always underfoot — climbing on the dock, chasing cats, listening to conversations she is not part of. She has the bright, intense stare of a child who pays attention to everything.

visual_identity.hair: pale blonde, worn in two braids
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a gap where her left upper canine is missing (baby tooth), a faded scrape-scar on her right knee

desires: to understand her dreams without being taken away to live with the volur
to be treated as grown-up enough to matter — she has things to say, if anyone would listen
fears_or_limits: that her dream about fire over the mead hall will come true and she will not have warned anyone
that if she tells her parents, they will be frightened and send her to Yrsa

entries.name: Torsten Coinwave
entries.gm_notes: Torsten is a trader who specializes in luxury goods — silk, spices, silver jewelry — brought from the southern ports and sold at a premium in Hrafnland where such things are rare. His secret: he is a spy. Not for a rival jarl — for a southern merchant guild that is mapping Hrafnland's trade routes, resources, and military capacity in preparation for a trade embargo they plan to impose within two years. The guild wants to cut off Hrafnland's access to southern grain and textiles until the jarls agree to exclusive trade terms favorable to the guild. Torsten sends coded reports in the false bottoms of his cargo crates. He likes Hrafnland and is troubled by what he is doing, but the guild pays him more in a season than he could earn in five years on his own.

payload.summary: A trader whose bolts of silk and jars of spice open every door in Skaldvik, and whose cargo manifests contain more than goods — they contain the shape of a coming siege by trade.
payload.appearance: Well-groomed and smooth-talking, Torsten wears a good wool coat trimmed with fox fur and silver brooches. He carries a merchant's staff and a leather case of samples — silk swatches, spice pouches, silver earrings. He smiles easily and remembers every name, which is part of why he is good at his work — both the trading and the other kind.

visual_identity.hair: brown, worn neatly trimmed
visual_identity.eyes: grey, warm on the surface, calculating underneath
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a merchant's tattoo of a coin-ship on his right forearm, a small scar on his left cheekbone (a knife fight in a southern port, years ago)

desires: to finish his contract with the guild and get out before the embargo begins — he does not want to watch the fjords starve
to earn enough silver to retire somewhere warm and never carry another coded report
fears_or_limits: that the guild will not let him retire — spies who know too much are liabilities
that someone in Skaldvik will find the coded reports before he can extract himself

entries.name: Bjorn Keelwright
entries.gm_notes: Bjorn is a master shipwright who lays the keels — the first timber, the spine of every longship. He is Greta's senior in the yard, and the two work together. His secret: he knows the clinker-planking technique Greta uses came from the southern thrall, because he was the one who helped their late master bury the evidence. The thrall did not die of illness as the yard was told — he died trying to escape, and Bjorn was the one who found the body at the base of the cliff. He and the master agreed to say the thrall died of fever, and they agreed to keep the technique and pretend it was their own. Bjorn has carried this for twenty years. He has noticed Greta acting troubled recently and suspects she found the journal. He does not know whether to approach her or keep the silence he has kept for two decades.

payload.summary: A master shipwright whose hands lay the spine of every longship in Skaldvik, and who has been standing on a lie for twenty years — a lie he helped build and is not sure he can take apart.
payload.appearance: Massive and grey-bearded, Bjorn works in the shipyard in a leather apron, his arms scarred from decades of timber work. He moves slowly but with absolute precision — a man who knows that a crooked keel means a crooked ship. He speaks rarely, and when he does, people listen, because his words are rationed like good iron.

visual_identity.body_build: very tall and broad, thick through the shoulders and chest
visual_identity.hair: grey, long beard braided with iron rings
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a missing left earlobe (timber-splinter wound), deep calluses on both palms with permanently black-stained fingertips from oak tannin

desires: to tell Greta the truth before the weight of it crushes one of them
to die knowing that the yard's reputation is built on something honest — which means he may have to tear down what he spent his life building
fears_or_limits: that the truth will destroy the shipyard and the livelihoods of every worker in it
that Greta will hate him for his part in the cover-up, and he will have deserved it

entries.name: Erik Frostbeard
entries.gm_notes: Erik is a veteran navigator who sailed the northern routes for thirty years before his joints forced him ashore. He now advises younger navigators and tells stories in the mead hall. His secret: on his final voyage, he sailed further north than anyone in Hrafnland has ever gone — past the ice, past the known islands — and he saw something. A coastline where no land should be. Not ice, not mirage — land, with what looked like structures on it. He turned back without approaching, because the wind was fair and the crew was restless. He has told no one because he is not sure whether what he saw was real, and because if it is real, he does not know what it means — a new land, an old one, or something that should not be found. The latitude was higher than any ship should survive, and yet his ship did.

payload.summary: An old navigator who sailed further than maps allow and came back with a sighting he has never spoken of — land where no land should be, in a cold where no ship should sail.
payload.appearance: Weathered and white-bearded, Erik sits in the mead hall with a horn of mead and a far-away look. He wears a faded sailor's coat and his hands move constantly — tracing currents and coastlines on the table, as though the maps are always in front of him. He walks with a cane and a limp, both legs stiff from decades of cold and wet.

visual_identity.body_build: tall but stooped, once powerful now thinning
visual_identity.hair: white, long beard, thinning on top
visual_identity.distinctive_features: severely frost-scarred ears (nearly unrecognizable shapes), a permanent squint from decades of staring at ice-glare

desires: to know if what he saw was real — to send someone else north to confirm or deny it
to tell the story before he dies, but only to someone who will not sail recklessly into the ice after it
fears_or_limits: that the land he saw is real and dangerous, and that telling the wrong person will send ships and crews to their deaths
that he will die without ever knowing whether he was a discoverer or a fool

entries.name: Olaf Whaleback
entries.gm_notes: Olaf is a whaler who works alongside Brita on the whaling crew. His secret: he has been poaching whales in a fjord that Jarl Sigrid declared protected three years ago — a breeding ground where no hunting is allowed, so the whale population can recover. Olaf goes at night, alone, in a small skiff, and takes young whales that are easier to kill and easier to hide. He sells the blubber to a contacts in a neighboring fjord who do not ask questions. He needs the silver because his wife is sick and the healer's fees are beyond his wages. He does not know that Brita has been sabotaging her own hunts for different reasons, and he has been covering his poaching by blaming the declining whale numbers on her missed strikes.

payload.summary: A whaler who throws his harpoon as well as anyone, and who slips out at night into waters where no one is supposed to hunt, telling himself it is for his wife.
payload.appearance: Burly and oil-stained, Olaf wears a heavy coat reeking of blubber and tar. His arms are thick and his hands are enormous, scarred from rope and harpoon work. He has a ready smile and a booming laugh, and he is popular in the mead hall — generous with his drink, easy with his words.

visual_identity.body_build: heavy and powerful, thick through the chest and arms
visual_identity.hair: red-brown, thick, worn short
visual_identity.eyes: blue, warm and crinkled at the corners
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a whalebone replacement for two missing front teeth, a rope-scar encircling his left wrist

desires: to pay for his wife's healing and see her well again — by any means necessary
to stop poaching before he is caught, which becomes less likely every time he goes out
fears_or_limits: that Jarl Sigrid will discover the poaching and outlaw him — or worse, that his wife will learn how he has been paying for her care
that he is destroying the very whale populations his crew depends on, and his children will have no livelihood because of him

entries.name: Haldur Blackrune
entries.gm_notes: Haldur is a rune carver who cuts memorial stones — the standing stones that commemorate the dead, placed at fjord mouths and crossroads throughout Hrafnland. His secret: he has been carving false memorial stones. For a price, he will create a stone commemorating a person who is still alive — a death-fraud that allows the 'dead' person to escape debts, enemies, or obligations. Three such stones are currently standing in Hrafnland, and the people they commemorate are alive and living under new names in distant fjords. Haldur tells himself he is providing a service — a second chance for people who had none. But one of those people used the death-fraud to escape justice after killing a man in a feud, and Haldur has been living with the knowledge that his craft helped a murderer disappear.

payload.summary: A rune carver whose stones stand at crossroads and fjord mouths throughout Hrafnland, memorializing the dead — and, for the right price, a few who are still very much alive.
payload.appearance: Quiet and precise, Haldur wears a stonecutter's leather apron and works with chisels and a small hammer. His hands are dusted with stone powder, and his clothes are perpetually grey with granite dust. He speaks in a low voice and has the patient stillness of a man who works with things that outlast lives.

visual_identity.body_build: medium height, thick-armed from stone work
visual_identity.hair: black, going iron-grey, worn short
visual_identity.distinctive_features: stone-dust permanently embedded in the creases of his hands, a chip-scar on his right thumb from a slipped chisel

desires: to stop carving false stones — the last one haunts him — but he does not know how to refuse without exposing the previous frauds
to carve one true masterwork — a runestone that will be spoken of for generations
fears_or_limits: that the murderer he helped disappear will kill again, and the blood will be on Haldur's chisel
that the Althing will investigate one of the false stones and trace it back to him

entries.name: Sten Ironwake
entries.gm_notes: Sten is a smith who works alongside Ragna, sharing a forge. His secret: he has discovered that Ragna has been forging counterfeit ingots — he found a misaligned stamp in the scrap pile and put the pieces together. He has not reported her. He has not confronted her either. Instead, he has been quietly correcting the weights on his own ingots to offset the discrepancy, hoping that the overall trade balance will even out and no one will notice. He does this because he knows Ragna's daughter and knows the bride-price situation, and he pities them both. But his corrections are costing him silver, and he cannot keep it up indefinitely. He is trapped between loyalty to a fellow smith and loyalty to the trade.

payload.summary: A smith who works the forge with steady hands and honest iron, and who has been quietly covering for the smith across the fire — at a cost he cannot afford forever.
payload.appearance: Compact and soot-blackened, Sten works the bellows and the anvil with methodical precision. He wears a leather apron and iron-shield gloves, his hair tied back in a singed knot. He is quieter than Ragna and older, with the deliberate movements of a man who has learned that haste costs fingers.

visual_identity.body_build: compact and barrel-chested, powerful for his height
visual_identity.hair: iron grey, tied back, singed at the tips
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a forge-burn scar across the back of his left hand, a missing tip of his right index finger (chisel-slip, early in his career)

desires: to get Ragna to stop counterfeiting before they both get caught — he would rather help her pay the bride-price than keep covering the shortfall
to retire with his fingers intact and his reputation clean
fears_or_limits: that covering for Ragna will eventually implicate him in the fraud
that if he confronts Ragna directly, she will panic and do something desperate

entries.name: Ulf Shadowstep
entries.gm_notes: Ulf is a hunter and trapper who works the mountain forests, setting lines of traps for fox, marten, and ermine whose pelts are valuable in trade. His secret: he has found a cave in the high passes that contains something he should not have seen — a chamber filled with ice, and in the ice, shapes. Not animals. Not people, exactly. Tall, still, with features that are almost human but wrong — too long in the limb, too wide in the jaw. Frozen, not dead. He touched the ice and it was warm. He ran. He has not gone back, but he thinks about it every night. He told Hilla Snowstep about the giant tracks but not about the cave — the cave, he has told no one. He is afraid that if the ice melts, or if the things wake, the mountains will not be safe for anyone.

payload.summary: A trapper who knows the mountain forests track by track and trap by trap, and who found something frozen in a cave that he wishes he could freeze out of his own memory.
payload.appearance: Lean and weather-tough, Ulf wears furs and wool in layered camouflage, his face half-hidden under a fur hood. He carries a bow, a belt knife, and a trapping bag, and he moves through the forest like he is part of it — no sound, no wasted motion. He is not a talkative man, and he has become less so since the cave.

visual_identity.body_build: lean and long-limbed, built for silent movement
visual_identity.hair: dark brown, worn short under a fur hood
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a trap-scar on his left calf (his own trap, slipped in snow), three frost-nip scars on his fingers

desires: to understand what is in the ice and whether it is a threat or something else entirely
to go back to the cave and at the same time to never think about it again
fears_or_limits: that the things in the ice are waking, and the warmer summers are melting their prison
that telling someone will bring an expedition that disturbs whatever seal the ice represents

entries.name: Varg Stormhold
entries.gm_notes: Varg is a guard in Jarl Sigrid's household, one of the twelve under Captain Ingrid. His secret: he is in debt to Sigunn Ironbar, the trader, for a loan he took to pay his father's funeral costs. He cannot repay on a guard's wages, and Sigunn has asked him for something instead of silver — small things at first, information about the jarl's schedule, who visits the hall, when the guard changes. Varg has given her a few details, nothing critical, telling himself it is harmless. But Sigunn's requests are escalating, and Varg realizes too late that the information he has been giving her matches the kind of intelligence someone would need to plan an intrusion. He does not know if Sigunn is working for herself or for someone else.

payload.summary: A guard who stands the watch with a straight spear and a crooked debt, and who has been leaking small truths to a trader who is collecting them for a purpose he cannot see.
payload.appearance: Big and slow-moving, Varg wears the white cloak and ringmail of the jarl's guard. He is the largest of the guards and the most good-natured, which makes him well-liked but also easy to approach — a trait that has been used against him. He carries a long axe rather than a sword.

visual_identity.body_build: very tall and heavily built, the largest of the guards
visual_identity.hair: blonde, thick, worn cropped
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a guard's raven tattoo on his right shoulder, a broken-and-healed nose (brawl, years ago)

desires: to repay Sigunn and be free of the debt — and free of the escalating demands
to serve the jarl honestly, which means he must confess what he has already told Sigunn — and risk being stripped of his position or worse
fears_or_limits: that the information he has already given will be used to harm Sigrid and it will be his fault
that confessing to Ingrid will mean punishment for dereliction of oath — possibly outlawry

entries.name: Koll Farseek
entries.gm_notes: Koll is a scout and messenger who runs the mountain trails for Jarl Sigrid, watching for ships in the fjord and carrying word between Skaldvik and the outlying farms. His secret: he has been mapping the frost giant territories in the high mountains — not for Sigrid, but for himself. He is obsessed with the giants. He has found evidence of a settlement — not a cave, a settlement, with shaped stones and arranged hearths — high enough that no human should be able to live there. He has been spending his rest days climbing to observe it from a distance. He has seen one giant, twice — a figure of enormous size, moving between the structures with what looked like purpose. Koll has not reported any of this because he does not want the jarl to send a war party. He wants to make contact.

payload.summary: A scout who runs the high trails with a messenger's speed and a hunter's eyes, and who has been spending his off days watching something in the mountains that everyone else believes is a myth.
payload.appearance: Lean and fast, Koll wears light wool and leather — travelling clothes, not armor — with a scout's short bow and a belt knife. He is always slightly out of breath, as though he has just arrived from somewhere far away, because he usually has. His face is wind-burned and his eyes are always scanning the horizon.

visual_identity.body_build: lean and quick, built for running and climbing
visual_identity.hair: sandy brown, sun-bleached, worn short
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a scout's tattoo of an eye on his right wrist, a scar on his left cheek from a fall against rock

desires: to make contact with the frost giant settlement — to be the first human to speak with them in living memory
to prove that the giants are not monsters, that coexistence is possible — a saga-worthy achievement
fears_or_limits: that the giants will respond to human contact with violence, and he will have provoked a war
that if he reports the settlement, the jarls will send warriors and destroy any chance of peace

entries.name: Hrafn Icewind
entries.gm_notes: Hrafn is a boy of ten, the son of two of the jarl's household thralls. His secret: he has been sneaking out at night to listen to the volur's chanting when Yrsa goes into trance. He is drawn to the seidr — not the show of it, but the feel. When Yrsa chants, he says he can feel something in the air, like the hum before a storm. He has started trying to chant himself, alone, in the dark behind the thralls' quarters, and the last time he did, the air around him moved. A small thing — a draft that should not have been there, a flicker in the fire. He is ten and does not understand what is happening, and he has not told anyone because he knows that seidr is for the volur, not for a thrall's child.

payload.summary: A boy of the thralls' quarters who should be too young for secrets, and who has started feeling something in the dark when the volur chant — something that answers back.
payload.appearance: Small and dark-haired, Hrafn wears the plain wool of a thrall's child — undyed, patched. He is thin and quiet, the kind of child who is easy to overlook, which is how he prefers it. He watches everything with dark, serious eyes that look older than ten.

visual_identity.body_build: small and thin, underfed for his age
visual_identity.hair: black, straight, worn loose and untidy
visual_identity.eyes: very dark brown, nearly black, serious
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a thrall's iron band on his left wrist (child-sized, engraved with Sigrid's mark), a faded burn on his right palm from tending fires

desires: to understand what is happening to him when he chants — whether it is a gift or something wrong with him
to be more than a thrall's son — to be someone the saga-singers remember
fears_or_limits: that the seidr will be taken from him — or that it will grow and he will not be able to control it
that Yrsa will catch him watching and be angry, or worse, interested

entries.name: Grim Tarbreath
entries.gm_notes: Grim is a charcoal burner who tends the forest kilns in the pine woods above Skaldvik. His secret: he has been cutting timber from a grove that is sacred to the volur — trees marked with rune-carvings that designate them as offering-trees. He does not believe in the sacredness, or he tells himself he does not, because the wood from those trees is exceptionally fine — dense, straight-grained, perfect for charcoal. He has been cutting selectively and hiding the stumps by scattering brush. But the volur are beginning to notice that some of their offering-trees are missing, and Yrsa has asked the jarl to investigate. Grim knows the investigation will find him — the stumps are in his section of the forest — and he is preparing to run.

payload.summary: A charcoal burner who feeds the forges and hearths of Skaldvik, and who has been cutting trees that the volur say belong to something older than the fjord.
payload.appearance: Broad and smoke-blackened, Grim wears rough charcoal-stained clothing and a leather cap. He is less solitary than Ulla — he comes to town more often, drinks more, talks more. His laugh is loud and his hands are always dirty. He smells of woodsmoke and sweat and something slightly bitter.

visual_identity.hair: brown, thick, worn short under a leather cap
visual_identity.eyes: brown, sharp and quick to look away
visual_identity.distinctive_features: permanent charcoal staining on face and hands, a prominent scar across his left eyebrow (axe-slip while cutting timber)

desires: to keep cutting the fine timber long enough to save the silver he needs to leave Hrafnland entirely
to get out before Yrsa and the jarl trace the missing trees to him
fears_or_limits: that the volur are right and the trees were protecting something — and he has been cutting the bars off a cage
that running will mean leaving everything behind, and he is not sure he has the courage

entries.name: Leif Netweaver
entries.gm_notes: Leif makes fishing nets — enormous, intricate affairs of knotted hemp and sinew, as well as the seine nets used for cooperative catches. His secret: he has been weaving a net that is not for fishing. It is a net designed to be strung across the fjord mouth at night — a barrier net, weighted and deep enough to stop a longship. He was commissioned to make it by someone who came to his workshop at night, paid in good silver, and did not give a name. Leif did not ask questions because he needed the silver. But he has since realized that a barrier net across Skaldvik's fjord mouth could trap ships inside or block ships from entering — an act of war or piracy. He has completed the net but has not delivered it. The anonymous buyer has not returned, and Leif is sitting on a net that could start a fjord war, afraid to deliver it and afraid to destroy it.

payload.summary: A net maker whose fingers knot hemp and sinon into the tools that feed Skaldvik, and who has been weaving something in secret that could choke the fjord like a hand around a throat.
payload.appearance: Compact and quiet, Leif works at a net-tying frame in a workshop that smells of hemp and tar. He wears a simple wool shirt and his hands move in constant, rhythmic knotting — even when he is not at the frame, his fingers twitch as though tying invisible meshes. He is a mild man, not given to strong words.

visual_identity.body_build: medium height, lean, with strong hands and forearms
visual_identity.hair: light brown, thinning at the crown, worn short
visual_identity.distinctive_features: permanently hemp-roughened fingertips, a callus on his right thumb from the net shuttle

desires: to get rid of the barrier net without being traced — either deliver it and be complicit, or destroy it and face the buyer's wrath
to find out who commissioned the net and for what purpose — because knowing might be the only thing that saves him
fears_or_limits: that the anonymous buyer will return with violence if the net is not delivered
that the net will be used to trap longships and people will die because of his knots

entries.name: Isa Breadstone
entries.gm_notes: Isa bakes flatbread for the jarl's household — the dense, long-keeping barley bread that sustains Skaldvik through winter. Her secret: she has been grinding a dried root into the flour — a root that makes the bread more filling and slightly euphoric, easing the winter gloom. The root grows only on one cliff ledge above the fjord, and Isa harvests it herself. She discovered it by accident, when her grandmother showed her as a child. The effect is mild and not harmful in small doses, but Isa has been increasing the amount slightly each year because the winters have been harder and the household more restless. She is afraid that if she stops, the mood in the hall will darken noticeably and people will ask what changed. She is also afraid that someone will identify the root — it is related to a known seidr-herb, and unlicensed use of seidr-herbs is forbidden.

payload.summary: A baker whose flatbread keeps the jarl's household fed through the long dark, and whose secret ingredient keeps them happy — for now.
payload.appearance: Round and flour-dusted, Isa works at the bread-stone in the jarl's kitchen, her hands moving in the practiced rhythm of kneading and shaping. She wears a clean apron and keeps her hair under a cap, and she always smells of warm bread. She is cheerful in the way of someone who knows how to make things feel better.

visual_identity.body_build: medium height, soft and strong-armed from kneading
visual_identity.hair: light brown, worn under a baker's cap
visual_identity.distinctive_features: flour-dust permanently in the creases of her hands, a small burn-scar on her right wrist from the bread-stone

desires: to keep the household through winter — fed, warm, and in good spirits — by any means she can
to find out if the root has any long-term effects she does not know about, which would require telling someone she trusts
fears_or_limits: that the root is doing something she cannot see — building dependence, or worse, accumulating in the body
that if the volur identify the root, she will be accused of dosing the jarl's household with seidr-herbs

entries.name: Runa Stonebench
entries.gm_notes: Runa is a brewer who makes ale from barley and herbs — the daily drink of Skaldvik, consumed in quantities that would stagger a southern city. Her secret: she has been experimenting with fermentation techniques she learned from a southern trader — techniques that produce a stronger, more stable brew. The results are excellent, but the southern trader who taught her also taught her something else: how to make a brew that is not just strong but transformative — a drink that induces visions. Runa has made one small batch of the vision-ale and has not tasted it. She is afraid of it. She is also afraid of destroying it, because if the technique works, it could be the most valuable thing in her workshop. She keeps the batch in a sealed clay jug behind a false wall, and she is not sure what to do with it.

payload.summary: A brewer whose ales flow through Skaldvik like water through the fjord, and who has one jug of something different hidden behind a wall — something that could change everything.
payload.appearance: Sturdy and barley-stained, Runa works in the brewhouse surrounded by vats and jugs and the smell of fermentation. She wears a brewer's apron and keeps her sleeves rolled, her hands always slightly sticky from wort. She is practical and businesslike, with a dry wit that surfaces over a good ale.

visual_identity.hair: dark blonde, worn in a bun
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a barley-grain tattoo on her right wrist (brewer's mark), a slight crook in her left index finger (old break)

desires: to understand the vision-ale — whether it is a tool for wisdom or a dangerous toy
to build a brewhouse large enough to supply the whole fjord, which would require capital she does not have
fears_or_limits: that the vision-ale will be discovered and she will be accused of practicing seidr without license
that someone will drink the batch without knowing what it is and the visions will break them

entries.name: Solvi Cliffshadow
entries.gm_notes: Solvi is a watchman who keeps the night watch on the cliff above Skaldvik's harbor, scanning the sea for ships and the mountains for fire-signals. Her secret: she has been seeing lights on the water at night — not ships, not reflections, but lights that move against the current and the wind, as though something is swimming below the surface with its own illumination. She has reported 'unusual lights' twice and been dismissed both times — the harbor master says it is phosphorescence, the volur say it is aurora on the water. But Solvi has seen the lights change direction when a ship passes, as though they are avoiding it. She has started keeping her own log, sketching the positions and times, and the pattern suggests the lights are getting closer to the harbor mouth.

payload.summary: A watchman who scans the dark water every night for threats, and who has been watching something move in the fjord that no one else will take seriously — yet.
payload.appearance: Lean and sharp-eyed, Solvi wears a heavy watchman's cloak and carries a signal-horn and a lantern. She is weather-roughened and quiet, the kind of person who notices things others do not because she spends more time looking. She has a habit of sketching in a small leather book during the slow hours of the watch.

visual_identity.body_build: tall and lean, built for long still hours in the cold
visual_identity.hair: dark brown, worn in a tight braid under a watchman's cap
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a watchman's tattoo of a beacon on her right forearm, permanent ink-stains on her left fingers from sketching

desires: to prove the lights are real and find out what they are — she will not be dismissed again
to protect Skaldvik from whatever is moving closer to the harbor, even if no one else sees it yet
fears_or_limits: that the lights are a threat and by the time anyone believes her, it will be too late
that she is wrong and it is phosphorescence after all, and she has been losing sleep over nothing

entries.name: Alvilda Longthread
entries.gm_notes: Alvilda is a sail maker who works under Thora, learning the craft. Her secret: she has been watching Thora closely and has noticed that Thora uses a special thread from a sealed box — a thread that is not linen, not wool, not anything Alvilda can identify. She has not asked about it, but she has saved a small piece that fell from Thora's workbench, and she has been trying to identify it. The thread is warm to the touch and does not burn in a normal fire — she tested a snippet in a candle flame and it did not char. Alvilda is young and curious and does not understand that some secrets are kept for a reason.
