visual_identity.distinctive_features: a pearl pouch at the belt — always within hand's reach, a habit of holding pearls to her ear to listen, a trader's quick appraising glance that she turns on people as well as objects

desires: To find the remaining black pearls and complete the set — to hear what they say when they resonate together
To find the person who is hearing the same note she hears in the pearls — because she knows someone must be
fears_or_limits: That the complete set of pearls will not be a key but a weapon — or a door
That the pearls are not fragments of something broken but eggs of something that is about to hatch

entries.name: Ariki Lost-Chief
entries.gm_notes: Ariki was the chief of a small island that submerged two years ago. She arrived at Lani Atoll with her people — twelve families — and has been living as a refugee ever since. She is technically still a chief, but without an island, her authority is symbolic at best. She has been quiet, helpful, and unobtrusive, and most people see her as a dignified elder. Her secret is that she is not quiet at all. She has been meeting with chiefs from three other islands that are projected to submerge within the next year, and she is building a coalition to do something unprecedented: merge their populations onto a single island that can support them all, and form a new joint governance. She has identified the island — a large, elevated islet that is currently uninhabited — and she has been quietly negotiating with its nearest neighbor for water rights. She has not told the refugee council or the wayfinder guilds because she is afraid they will see it as a power grab rather than a survival plan, and she needs everything in place before she announces it.

payload.summary: A chief who lost her island and has been living quietly as a refugee while secretly building a coalition to merge four sinking islands' populations onto one that can survive.
payload.appearance: A dignified, composed woman who carries herself with a chief's bearing even in refugee cloth. She is always in conversation, always building relationships, always listening more than she speaks.

visual_identity.hair: black, greying, worn in a chief's style despite her refugee status
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a chief's whale-bone pendant — the only remnant of her island, worn openly, a quality of authority that persists even in donated cloth, a habit of counting people — always knowing exactly how many are in a room and who they are

desires: To complete the merger plan and give her people and three other islands' populations a permanent home before their islands sink
To prove that a chief without an island is still a chief — that leadership is not about land but about people
fears_or_limits: That the coalition will be seen as a power grab and she will be exiled from the refugee community she is trying to save
That the uninhabited island she has chosen will not support the combined population — that she is leading people to a second disaster

entries.name: Tane Hull-Shaper
entries.gm_notes: Tane is the master canoe builder of Lani Atoll, and his voyaging canoes are sailed across the entire Archipelago. He is known for hulls that are light, strong, and fast. His secret is that he has been building a canoe in secret for six months that is different from anything he has ever made. It is not a voyaging canoe and not a fishing canoe. It is a deep-water canoe, designed to dive, not sail. He does not know how to explain the design — it came to him in dreams, fully formed, with hull shapes that should not work and a ballast system he has never seen. He has been building it in a hidden cove and is three-quarters done. He does not know what it is for, but the dreams that bring the designs also bring a feeling: urgency. He is afraid that if he does not finish it in time, whatever it is needed for will happen without it. He is also afraid that if he does finish it, he will have to use it — and the dreams show him diving it into water so deep that no light reaches the bottom.

payload.summary: A master canoe builder who is secretly constructing a diving canoe from dream-designs he does not understand. He does not know what it is for, only that it is urgently needed.
payload.appearance: A broad, strong-handed man with wood shavings in his hair and sawdust on his arms. He works with an intensity that borders on obsession, and his hands move with the confidence of decades of practice.

visual_identity.hair: black, short, full of shavings
visual_identity.distinctive_features: wood shavings always in the hair and on the shoulders, calloused hands with a woodworker's grip, a hidden cove he visits every day without explanation, dark intensity that has grown over the past six months

desires: To finish the diving canoe before whatever it is needed for happens — and to understand what it is for
To find someone who recognizes the design and can tell him if it has been built before and what happened when it was used
fears_or_limits: That the dreams are not guidance but compulsion — that the canoe is being built through him, not by him
That finishing the canoe means he will have to dive it into water from which nothing returns

entries.name: Pili Bone-Cutter
entries.gm_notes: Pili is a bone carver who creates tools, fishhooks, and ornaments from the bones of fish and sea mammals. She is skilled and respected and has been trading her work for years. Her secret is that she has been carving a set of bone fishhooks that are not for fishing. Each hook is carved to catch something specific — not a fish, but a promise, a memory, a secret. She learned the technique from her grandmother, who told her that bone hooks can catch intangible things if they are carved with the right intention. She has tested it. She carved a hook for 'lost things' and cast it into the lagoon, and it returned with a wedding ring that a refugee woman had lost during her crossing. She carved a hook for 'forgotten names' and cast it, and it returned with a bone fragment inscribed with a name no one recognized — a name that Vehina the chant keeper later identified as belonging to an island that submerged fifty years ago. She is now carving a hook for 'what the sea has swallowed,' and she is afraid of what it will bring back.

payload.summary: A bone carver who makes hooks that catch intangible things — memories, promises, lost objects. She is now carving a hook for 'what the sea has swallowed,' and she is afraid of the catch.
payload.appearance: A lean, quiet man with bone dust on her hands and a carver's careful focus. She works in a small shelter and speaks rarely, letting her craft communicate for her.

visual_identity.hair: black, short, neat
visual_identity.distinctive_features: bone dust permanently staining both hands, a set of carved bone hooks kept in a woven pouch — each one different, a quiet intensity that makes people lower their voices around her, a bone fishhook worn on a cord around the neck — her first successful catch-hook

desires: To cast the hook for 'what the sea has swallowed' and learn what the rising waters have taken that no one has noticed
To understand the full range of what bone hooks can catch — and whether some things should not be caught
fears_or_limits: That the hook for 'what the sea has swallowed' will catch something that was swallowed deliberately — something that should stay down
That each catch comes with a cost she has not yet identified — that the sea is trading, not giving

entries.name: Hoku Star-Path
entries.gm_notes: Hoku is a veteran wayfinder, one of the most experienced in the guilds, and she has sailed every known route in the Archipelago. She is quiet, reliable, and the person the guild sends when a route is too dangerous for younger navigators. Her secret is that she has been sailing to a place that is not on any chart — a fixed point in the open ocean where the water is always calm and the stars reflect differently. She found it by accident seven years ago, and she has returned every year since. The point is not an island — there is nothing there but water and stillness. But when she sits in her canoe at the point, she can hear everything happening in the Archipelago at once — every conversation, every song, every wave. She calls it the Listening Point. She has not told the guild because she is afraid of what it means — that the ocean has a place where it hears everything, and if she can hear through it, something else might be listening through it too. She has noticed that each year, the Listening Point is farther south, as if it is moving, and she is afraid it is moving toward something.

payload.summary: A veteran wayfinder who has been secretly visiting a point in the open ocean where all sound in the Archipelago can be heard at once. The point is moving south, and she does not know what it is moving toward.
payload.appearance: A weathered, quiet man with extensive wayfinder tattoos covering both arms and her chest. She moves with the economy of someone who has spent more of her life on water than on land.

visual_identity.hair: black, greying, short and salt-stiffened
visual_identity.distinctive_features: wayfinder tattoos covering both arms, chest, and part of the neck — more routes than any active wayfinder, a weathered quality that speaks of decades at sea, a wayfinder's staff worn smooth by years of handling

desires: To follow the Listening Point south and find out what it is moving toward — and whether it is gathering sound for a purpose
To tell someone about the Listening Point and share the burden of knowing — but to find someone who will not be destroyed by the knowledge
fears_or_limits: That the Listening Point is an ear, and something vast is using it to hear the Archipelago — and that Hoku's annual visits have been noted
That the point is moving toward the source of the rising seas, and what she will hear when it arrives is something that cannot be unheard

entries.name: Rangi Deep-Cast
entries.gm_notes: Rangi is a deep-water fisher who works alone, sailing his canoe to the edge of the Archipelago's waters to catch fish that no one else will pursue. He is known for his strength and his fearlessness. His secret is that he has been catching fish that should not exist — deep-water fish surfacing in shallow water, fish with bioluminescent patterns that match no known species, and most recently, a fish with an object in its belly: a small carved stone tablet inscribed with a script that resembles the patterns in wayfinder tattoos. He has been keeping the tablet hidden and has been trying to catch more fish from the same area, hoping to find more tablets. He has caught two more since, each with a fragment of the same script. He cannot read it, but the fragments fit together like pieces of a broken thing, and he is afraid they are instructions — for something that was supposed to stay at the bottom of the sea.

payload.summary: A deep-water fisher who has been catching impossible fish and recovering carved stone tablets from their bellies. The tablets form a message he cannot read, and he is afraid of what they say.
payload.appearance: A big, sun-darkened man with a fisher's scars and a quiet, solitary manner. He works alone and speaks little. His canoe is always loaded for deep water.

visual_identity.hair: black, short, salt-bleached
visual_identity.distinctive_features: fishing scars on both hands and forearms, a solitary quality that keeps people at a distance, three carved stone fragments kept hidden in a waterproof pouch, a deep-water canoe always loaded and ready

desires: To recover all the stone fragments and find someone who can read the script — or determine if it matches the wayfinder tattoo patterns
To understand why deep-water fish are surfacing with these tablets in their bellies — what is releasing them from the sea floor
fears_or_limits: That the tablets are instructions for something that was deliberately sunk, and assembling them will activate it
That the fish carrying the tablets are not random catches but messengers — and that something sent them to him specifically

entries.name: Tau Drum-Maker
entries.gm_notes: Tau makes the drums that every island uses for ceremony, communication, and rhythm-keeping. He is a master woodworker who selects every tree personally and cures every drumhead with care. His secret is that he has been making a drum he has not been asked to make — a very large drum, large enough that it cannot be carried by one person, from a log he found floating in the lagoon six months ago. The log was not from any tree on the Archipelago's islands. It is dark, dense, and when he taps it, the sound is deeper than any wood he has worked. He has been hollowing it slowly, and every time he works on it, he hears the same rhythm Kiri is hearing — the twenty-first pattern, the heartbeat. He does not know Kiri, and Kiri does not know him. He has not told anyone about the drum because he is afraid of it. The wood is warm to the touch — warmer than it should be — and the interior of the log, as he hollows it, is not uniform. There are structures inside the wood that look organic, like the chambers of a heart.

payload.summary: A drum maker who is building an enormous drum from a mysterious log that is warm to the touch and has organic structures inside. The drum produces a rhythm he cannot explain.
payload.appearance: A stocky, precise man with woodworker's calluses and a careful, measuring gaze. He treats every piece of wood with reverence, but he handles the dark log with something closer to caution.

visual_identity.hair: black, greying, cropped short
visual_identity.distinctive_features: woodworker's calluses on both hands, a large unfinished drum in a hidden workshop, a quality of caution — he handles most wood with confidence but the dark log with wariness, sawdust always on his clothing

desires: To finish the drum and hear what it sounds like when it is complete — and to understand why it beats on its own
To find out where the dark log came from and whether there are more like it drifting in the Archipelago's waters
fears_or_limits: That the drum is not an instrument but a body part — that he is building the heart of something that will come alive when the drum is complete
That the rhythm the drum produces is the same rhythm someone else is hearing — and that completing the drum will connect them in a way neither of them chose

entries.name: Makea Shield-Arm
entries.gm_notes: Makea is a guard on Lani Atoll who patrols the meeting house and the chief's compound. He is large, gentle, and loyal, and most people see him as a friendly presence rather than a warrior. His secret is that he was not always a guard. He was a wayfinder — one of the best of his generation — until he lost his nerve. Twelve years ago, he was navigating a route through a storm when he heard something singing in the wind. The song was so beautiful and so alien that he lost his orientation and nearly sailed his canoe into a reef. He landed safely, but when he tried to sail again, he heard the song every time — always in the wind, always at sea. He could not navigate with that sound in his ears, so he quit the guild and took a land-based role. He has told everyone he lost his nerve due to a near-death experience. He has never told anyone about the song. And now he is hearing it on land — faintly, in the wind that comes off the water, growing louder. He is afraid the song is not in the wind but in his blood, and that it has been waiting for him to come back to the sea.

payload.summary: A guard who was once a gifted wayfinder until he heard an alien song in the wind at sea. He quit sailing and has hidden the reason for twelve years. Now he is hearing the song on land.
payload.appearance: A large, gentle man with a guard's staff and a former wayfinder's faded tattoos on his arms. He moves with care for his size and has a warm, reassuring presence that belies his private fear.

visual_identity.hair: black, short, practical
visual_identity.distinctive_features: faded wayfinder tattoos on both arms — visible but clearly no longer maintained, a guard's staff carried with a wayfinder's grip, a flinch when the wind comes off the sea that most people read as squinting

desires: To understand what the song in the wind is — and whether it is a threat or a call he should have answered
To find a way to hear the song without losing himself — or to silence it permanently
fears_or_limits: That the song is the same thing calling Hina, Mele, and others — and that his resistance has not protected him but marked him as the one who ran
That the song is getting louder on land because the sea is getting closer — and when it reaches the meeting house, he will not be able to resist it anymore

entries.name: Solomona Drowned-Home
entries.gm_notes: Solomona is a refugee who arrived at Lani Atoll with his two children after his island submerged. He is a skilled canoe builder who has been repairing boats at the atoll to earn his family's keep. He is quiet, hardworking, and grateful. His secret is that he did not flee his island when it submerged. He stayed until the water was waist-deep, because he was trying to retrieve something from beneath the meeting house: a stone chest that his grandfather buried there three generations ago. He could not find it — the water was too fast, the sand too churned. He got his children out with minutes to spare. He has been rebuilding canoes at Lani Atoll not just for income but to build a canoe capable of diving to his submerged island, which is now thirty feet underwater. He believes the chest contains something his grandfather said 'must not be in the water and must not be in the air' — something that was safest buried on land, and is now neither buried nor on land. He is afraid that whatever is in the chest has been released by the submergence, and he is afraid that it is the reason his island sank so fast.

payload.summary: A refugee canoe builder who stayed too long on his sinking island trying to retrieve a buried chest. He is now building a diving canoe to recover it from thirty feet of water.
payload.appearance: A strong, quiet man with a builder's hands and a refugee's donated clothing. He works constantly, building and repairing canoes with a skill that betrays his former status as a master craftsman.

visual_identity.hair: black, short, prematurely grey at the temples
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a builder's calloused hands with a master craftsman's precision, donated clothing that does not quite fit, two children always within sight, a quality of urgency — he works as if every canoe he builds is a step toward something

desires: To build a canoe that can reach his submerged island and recover the stone chest before whatever is inside it is fully released
To find out if the chest is the reason his island sank — and whether the same thing is buried beneath other islands
fears_or_limits: That whatever is in the chest has already been released and is causing the rising seas
That he will build the diving canoe and find that the chest is gone — taken by something that got there first

entries.name: Tamatoa Chief-Son
entries.gm_notes: Tamatoa is the son of Chief Lani, though this is not widely known — his mother has kept their relationship out of public governance, and he has respected that by never invoking it. He is a fisherman on Lani Atoll, ordinary and unremarkable, and most people see him as just another face on the docks. His secret is that he knows why his mother is so worried about the rising seas, beyond the obvious. He found her private records — charts of water levels over twenty years, annotated with notes in his grandmother's handwriting. The notes go back three generations, and they show that the sea level has risen and fallen before — in a cycle. According to his grandmother's notes, the sea rises for about a generation, then falls, and the cycle has happened at least three times. But this time is different. The rate of rise is faster than any previous cycle, and his grandmother's last note, written in a shaking hand, says 'this is not the cycle. Something is pushing it.' Tamatoa has been trying to determine whether his grandmother was right or whether she was a frightened old woman, and he has been afraid to tell his mother what he found because it would confirm her worst fears.

payload.summary: Chief Lani's son, a quiet fisherman who found his grandmother's secret records showing the rising seas follow a cycle — but this time, the cycle has been broken by something pushing it faster.
payload.appearance: An unremarkable, weathered man who blends into the docks. He has his mother's build and his father's quiet manner, and he works hard at not being noticed.

visual_identity.hair: black, short, salt-stiffened
visual_identity.eyes: dark brown — the same sharp watchfulness as his mother, though he hides it better
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a fisherman's weathered appearance that is deliberately unremarkable, old charts hidden in a waterproof roll in his canoe, a resemblance to Chief Lani that he does not acknowledge and most people do not notice

desires: To determine whether his grandmother's cycle theory is correct — and whether this rise is natural or pushed
To find the courage to tell his mother what he found, or to investigate on his own until he has proof
fears_or_limits: That confirming his grandmother's notes will break his mother's spirit — she has been governing on the assumption that the seas can be adapted to, not that they are being deliberately pushed
That the cycle his grandmother recorded means the seas have risen and fallen before — and that each time, something was left behind beneath the water

entries.name: Fale Wood-Hand
entries.gm_notes: Fale is a wood carver who makes the practical wooden tools of the Archipelago — bowls, utensils, paddles, house posts. She is not an artist; she is a craftswoman, and her work is valued for its durability rather than its beauty. Her secret is that the wood she uses has been talking to her. Not in words — in grain. When she carves a piece of wood, she can feel its history: where it grew, what weather it endured, what touched it. She has always had a feel for wood, but over the past year, the sensation has become specific and detailed — she can feel events that happened near the tree, including ones that happened after the wood was cut. She carved a paddle from driftwood last month and felt, through the grain, the image of a canoe sinking in a storm that had not happened yet. She dismissed it as imagination. The canoe sank three days later. She has been afraid to carve anything since, because the wood is showing her things that have not happened, and she does not know if she is seeing the future or causing it.

payload.summary: A practical wood carver whose wood has begun showing her future events through its grain. She carved a paddle and saw a canoe sink three days before it happened.
payload.appearance: A solid, plain man with a craftswoman's hands and an unremarkable face. She works steadily and without flair, and her workshop is full of functional, beautiful-in-their-simplicity wooden objects.

visual_identity.hair: black, short, practical
visual_identity.distinctive_features: wood-stained hands, a plainness of appearance and manner that is genuine — not disguise, a workshop full of unfinished pieces she has been afraid to complete, a quality of distraction that has grown over the past month

desires: To understand whether the wood is showing her the future or whether her carving creates it — and if it shows the future, whether she can use it to warn people
To find the courage to carve again without fear of what she will see
fears_or_limits: That completing a carving causes the event it shows — that her craft has become a weapon she does not know how to stop using
That the wood is not showing her the future but asking her to choose — to carve or not to carve, to make the event happen or prevent it

entries.name: Poto Old-Cord
entries.gm_notes: Poto is an elder rope maker, the oldest in the Archipelago, and he has been making cord for sixty years. He is Finau's father and taught her the knot that holds the world together — but he did not teach her everything. His secret is that the knot has a counterpart — an untying knot, which he has never used and hopes he will never need. The untying knot, when tied and then cut, releases whatever the holding knot has been holding. His grandfather taught it to him and made him swear never to teach it unless the Archipelago faced destruction from what the knot holds. Poto has been watching the rising seas with growing alarm, not because of the water but because of what the water might be approaching. He believes the holding knot — tied somewhere in the Archipelago by his ancestors — is holding something beneath the sea floor, and that the rising water is not the real threat. The real threat is what happens when the water reaches whatever is held. He does not know where the knot is tied. He does not know if it is still holding. He knows the untying knot, and he prays he never needs it.

payload.summary: An elder rope maker who knows a knot his family has guarded for generations — an untying knot that releases whatever the holding knot contains. He does not know where the holding knot is, and he prays it is still intact.
payload.appearance: A thin, weathered old man with rope-worker's hands that are still steady despite his age. He sits outside his home making cord, his fingers moving in patterns he has known for sixty years.

visual_identity.hair: white, thin
visual_identity.distinctive_features: rope-worker's calluses that have hardened into permanent ridges on both hands, a coil of cord always in his lap, fingers that tie and untie complex knots absently, a quality of watchfulness toward the sea that goes beyond normal islander caution

desires: To find where his ancestors tied the holding knot and verify that it is still intact before the rising seas reach what it contains
To decide whether to teach Finau the untying knot — and whether she would use it wisely if the worst came
fears_or_limits: That the holding knot has already failed — that the rising seas are not the approach of water but the release of what was held
That the untying knot, if needed, will not just release what is held but will unravel everything the holding knot has kept in place — including the routes, the songs, and the islands themselves

entries.name: Niu Root-Digger
entries.gm_notes: Niu is a farmer who cultivates taro, breadfruit, and coconut on one of the larger agricultural islands. He is a quiet, practical man who feeds his community and asks for little. His secret is that he has been growing something in addition to his crops — a plant that came from a seed he found inside a drift log. The plant is not from the Archipelago. It grows fast, needs no fresh water, and thrives in salt-saturated soil. It produces a tuber that is nutritious and filling. In short, it is a miracle crop for an archipelago losing its farmland to salt contamination. But Niu has not shared it because the plant is also aggressive — it sends runners through the soil that strangle other plants, and it cannot be easily controlled. He has been growing it in a sealed stone pit to contain it, but it is pushing through the stone. He is afraid that if he shares it, it will save the food crisis and destroy every other crop in the Archipelago. He is afraid that if he destroys it, he will have thrown away the only answer to the salt-killed gardens.

payload.summary: A farmer who found a miracle crop that thrives in salt-saturated soil — but it is aggressively invasive and threatens to strangle every other plant in the Archipelago. He must decide whether to share it or destroy it.
payload.appearance: A sun-browned, earth-handed man with a farmer's steady patience and a worried expression that he hides behind a calm face. He is always near his fields, always checking, always testing the soil.

visual_identity.hair: black, short, practical
visual_identity.distinctive_features: soil-stained hands with a farmer's calluses, a sealed stone pit near his fields that he checks daily, a worried quality behind his calm expression, a habit of testing soil with his fingers and frowning at the results

desires: To find a way to control the invasive crop — to make it productive without letting it destroy other plants
To decide whether to share the crop with Kaimana and other farmers fighting salt contamination, knowing the risk
fears_or_limits: That the plant cannot be controlled and sharing it will trade one famine for a different, worse one
That the plant is not a natural species but something designed — and that the drift log that brought it was sent deliberately

entries.name: Koa Far-Eye
entries.gm_notes: Koa is a scout who watches the southern approaches to the Archipelago from a watchtower on the southernmost inhabited island. He is young, sharp-eyed, and reliable, and his reports of weather and approaching ships are trusted by the guild. His secret is that he has seen something in the south that he has not reported. Three months ago, he saw a light on the horizon at night — not a star, not a ship's lamp, but a steady green glow beneath the water's surface, moving slowly north. He has seen it every night since, and it is closer. It moves against the current and the wind, as if it has its own direction. It is now close enough that he can see it is not a single light but a formation — a line of lights, evenly spaced, moving in formation like a convoy. He has not reported it because he does not know what it is, and he is afraid that if he reports it, the response will be a war fleet — and if the lights are refugees from somewhere farther south, a war fleet would be a catastrophe. He is also afraid that if the lights are not refugees, a war fleet would be too late.

payload.summary: A southern watchtower scout who has been tracking a formation of underwater lights moving north toward the Archipelago. They are getting closer every night, and he has not told anyone.
payload.appearance: A young, lean man with a scout's trained eyes and a watcher's patience. He spends most of his time in the watchtower and has the sun-weathered look of someone who is always outdoors.

visual_identity.hair: black, short, wind-tossed
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a scout's watchtower — he is almost always in it, a spyglass worn on a cord around the neck, a logbook of observations he keeps private, dark circles under the eyes from sleepless nights of watching the southern horizon

desires: To identify the underwater lights before they reach the Archipelago — and to determine if they are a threat or people in need
To find the courage to report what he has seen — to trust that the response will be wise rather than violent
fears_or_limits: That the lights are an approaching threat and his hesitation to report has cost the Archipelago its chance to prepare
That the lights are a convoy of refugees fleeing something worse than the rising seas — and that they will be met with fear instead of welcome

entries.name: Vili Deep-Lung
entries.gm_notes: Vili is a pearl diver, one of the few men in the profession, and he is known for his deep dives — deeper than anyone else in the Archipelago. He can reach depths that would kill most divers, and he has never suffered the sickness that affects divers who surface too fast. His secret is that he should not be able to do this. He has gills. Not visible ones — slits along his ribcage that open when he is submerged and close when he is in air. They are hidden beneath his arms and are invisible unless he raises his arms above his head in water. He has had them since birth and has never shown anyone, not even his wife. He has been diving deeper and deeper, not for pearls but to explore the sea floor, and he has seen things that no one else can reach — including, recently, structures beneath the Archipelago that are too regular to be natural. He has seen what looks like a foundation — a vast, flat stone surface beneath the islands, as if the Archipelago was built on something. He is afraid that his gills are not a mutation but a heritage — that someone in his bloodline was not entirely human, and that what lives beneath the islands is where he came from.

payload.summary: A pearl diver with hidden gills who can reach depths no one else survives. He has seen structures beneath the Archipelago — a vast stone foundation, as if the islands were built on something.
payload.appearance: A lean, deep-chested man with a diver's build and an ease in the water that is unsettling to watch. He moves through the sea as if it is his natural element, which, secretly, it is.

visual_identity.hair: black, cropped short, water-slicked
visual_identity.eyes: grey-green — the color of deep water
visual_identity.distinctive_features: hidden gill slits along both sides of the ribcage — invisible unless arms are raised in water, an unnatural ease in the water that other divers find remarkable but unsettling, a diver's barotrauma scarring on both earlobes that has healed despite the depth he reaches

desires: To dive to the foundation he has seen and determine what the islands were built on — and by whom
To find out if his gills are a gift from something beneath the sea — and whether that something is still alive
fears_or_limits: That his gills mark him as descended from whatever built the foundation — and that the rising seas are calling him home to something that is not human
That someone will see his gills and he will be driven from the community as something other than human

entries.name: Tama-iti Little-Wave
entries.gm_notes: Tama-iti is an eight-year-old boy, the son of a refugee family living on Lani Atoll. He is bright, curious, and always underfoot, and the adults tolerate him with the affectionate exasperation reserved for children who are everywhere at once. His secret is that he has a friend no one else can see. The friend is tall, made of water, and lives in the lagoon. It appeared to him the day he arrived on the atoll, and it has been with him every day since. It does not speak — it shows him things by changing shape. It showed him a picture of a canoe, and the next day a canoe arrived with refugees. It showed him a picture of a storm, and a storm came. It showed him a picture of an island with water rising around it, and he does not know which island it is or when it will happen. He told his mother about the friend once, and she told him it was a dream from the journey. He has not mentioned it again, but he goes to the lagoon every day to see what his friend will show him next. He is eight, and he does not know that what he is describing is a spirit, and he does not know that it is showing him the future, and he does not know that the next picture it shows him might be of Lani Atoll.

payload.summary: An eight-year-old refugee boy who has a water-spirit friend in the lagoon that shows him visions of the future. He does not know what it is — only that it is his friend.
payload.appearance: A small, bright-eyed boy who is always near the water and always looking at it. He wears refugee-donated clothing that is too large for him, and he has the restless energy of a child who has lost his home and is looking for a new one.

visual_identity.hair: black, short, untidy
visual_identity.eyes: dark brown, very bright and curious
visual_identity.distinctive_features: donated clothing that is always too large, a constant proximity to the water's edge — he is always near the lagoon, a habit of watching the water and smiling at things no one else can see, sand always on his feet

desires: To see what his water-friend will show him next — and to understand the pictures it makes
To find someone who can see his friend too — so he can prove it is real and not a dream
fears_or_limits: That his friend will show him a picture of his new home — Lani Atoll — with water rising around it
That his friend will disappear the way his old home did — suddenly and without explanation

entries.name: Rotama Quiet-Weave
entries.gm_notes: Rotama is a sail maker's apprentice who works under Leilani Wave-Singer. She is quiet, diligent, and learns fast. She is fifteen and one of the youngest apprentices in the craft. Her secret is that she can see the wind. Not feel it — see it. The air moves in visible currents to her eyes, colored faintly by temperature and moisture. She has always seen this and assumed everyone did. When she realized that others could not, she said nothing, because the ability lets her trim sails more precisely than any sailor and she did not want to be treated as a freak. But she has been watching the wind patterns change over the past year, and what she sees terrifies her. The wind is not just changing direction — it is being displaced. Something is pushing the air aside, something very large and very high that she can see only as a disturbance in the wind patterns — a shape that is not visible but that the wind flows around. It is north of the Archipelago, high in the sky, and it is getting larger. She has not told Leilani because she does not know how to describe what she sees without sounding insane.

payload.summary: A fifteen-year-old sail maker's apprentice who can see the wind — and who has been watching something invisible displace the air north of the Archipelago. It is large, high, and growing.
payload.appearance: A small, quiet girl with a sail maker's stained hands and a tendency to watch the sky when others watch the sea. She is diligent and eager to please and terrified of something she cannot explain.

visual_identity.hair: black, long, tied back for work
visual_identity.eyes: pale blue — unusually light, almost colorless, which she hides by looking down
visual_identity.distinctive_features: sail-cloth dye staining on both hands, pale blue eyes that are unusual for the Archipelago — she avoids eye contact to hide them, a habit of watching the sky rather than the sea, a tension in her shoulders that has grown over the past year

desires: To find someone who can see what she sees in the wind — or someone who can help her understand the invisible shape displacing the air
To tell Leilani what she sees and be believed — to share the burden of a sight no one else has
fears_or_limits: That the invisible shape in the sky is connected to the rising seas — and that no one will believe a fifteen-year-old apprentice who says she can see the wind
That the shape is growing because it is descending — and that when it reaches the water, it will be too late to do anything

entries.name: Keola Song-Keeper
entries.gm_notes: Keola is a song-keeper, one of the few who maintains the route-songs — the chants that wayfinders use to memorize the star paths and current patterns between islands. She is precise, dedicated, and has a voice like a bell. Her secret is that she has been altering the route-songs. Not the old ones — the ones she teaches to new wayfinders. She has been adding verses that include instructions for routes that do not exist yet — routes to islands that are farther north and higher, routes that follow the new reef channels that Moana Reef-Walker has been mapping. Keola does not know Moana, and Moana does not know Keola. But Keola has been having dreams of new routes, and she has been encoding them into the songs, so that when the time comes, there will be wayfinders who know the way to safety without knowing how they know. She is afraid she is inventing routes that do not exist and leading wayfinders to their deaths. She is also afraid that the routes are real and that the dreams are showing her a future in which the current islands are gone and the new routes are the only way to survive.

payload.summary: A song-keeper who has been secretly encoding new route-songs for routes that do not exist yet — routes to higher, northern islands she has seen in dreams. She does not know if she is prophesying or inventing.
payload.appearance: A precise, clear-voiced woman with a song-keeper's trained memory and a scholar's careful habits. She carries tapa-books of notation and rehearses constantly, her lips moving in silent chant.

visual_identity.hair: black, worn in a song-keeper's braided style with shell pins
visual_identity.distinctive_features: tapa-books of chant notation carried under the arm, shell pins in the hair marking her as a song-keeper, a habit of silent lip movement — she is always rehearsing, a tension between precision and uncertainty that has grown over the past year

desires: To determine whether the dream-routes are real — to find a wayfinder willing to sail a route that exists only in a song
To prepare the Archipelago for a future in which the current islands are gone — without causing panic in the present
fears_or_limits: That the dream-routes are inventions and she has been teaching wayfinders to sail into nothing
That the routes are real but lead somewhere that is not safe — that the dreams are not guidance but a lure

_help: Bonds between people. Keep the shared and private halves separate:
`public_status` is what anyone can observe; `bond` is your assessment and
stays GM-side.
`disposition` is a number from -100 to 100. It is stored today and does
not drift on its own yet (Phase 2, W2.3).

entries.name: Sir Aldrich and the Dragon Order

payload.public_status: A respected senior knight, loyal to the order, though quiet at council meetings.
payload.bond: Aldrich is losing faith in the order's ability to resolve its own crisis. He stays because leaving would confirm the traditionalists' fears, but he is privately sympathetic to the reformers. His silence at council meetings is not loyalty — it is indecision.

entries.name: Cao Shen and General Lu Fang

payload.public_status: Cao Shen trusts Lu Fang with military command. Lu Fang is publicly loyal and has never failed an order.
payload.bond: Cao Shen suspects Lu Fang's loyalty is to the idea of a unified Sangguo, not specifically to Cao Shen. If Cao Shen dies before reunification, Lu Fang may pursue it himself — in his own way, which may be less careful.

payload.public_status: The king's two eldest children, publicly civil, privately competing for the succession. The court watches them and bets quietly.
payload.bond: Elara underestimates Roderick's cunning — she thinks he is a blunt soldier, but he has been feeding her false intelligence through a double agent. Roderick does not know about Elara's dragonbone research, which is the one card she has that he cannot counter. They are siblings and they are enemies, and neither of them has decided which matters more.

payload.public_status: Two jarls who disagree about the frost giant threat. Sigrid wants action; Erik wants restraint. The Althing watches them and waits.
payload.bond: Sigrid thinks Erik is naive about the giants. Erik thinks Sigrid is using the giants to consolidate power. Both are partly right, which makes the rivalry productive and dangerous. If the abandoned village goes public, Erik's position collapses and Sigrid wins — which is why Sigrid has been sitting on the information.

entries.name: Malik Idris and Zuhayr the Patient

payload.public_status: Malik is the heir to the Idris family's oldest djinn contract. Zuhayr is the djinn bound by it. The contract's terms are family knowledge but not public.
payload.bond: Zuhayr genuinely wants to help Malik renegotiate — a willing partner is more useful than a bound servant. But the contract's deadline is binding on both of them, and neither can extend it alone. Zuhayr is the most dangerous kind of ally: one who is on Malik's side but constrained by law from giving him more time. Their relationship is warm in a way that makes the debt more painful, not less.

payload.public_status: A young wayfinder and the chief of Lani Atoll. They maintain professional distance in public, as a chief should not favor one wayfinder over others.
payload.bond: They are mother and son, and both know it, and neither says it in public. Kai respects his mother's governance and does not want to compromise it. Lani is proud of her son and frightened for him — he is sailing toward something neither of them understands. Their private relationship is warm; their public one is careful.

payload.public_status: Nara is training Tari in the shamanic traditions. Tari is young and talented. A normal master-apprentice relationship.
payload.bond: Nara knows Tari is gifted but does not realize how much Tari is hearing that Nara is not. Tari is afraid of being dismissed as too young, and afraid of being taken seriously. They trust each other but are both keeping secrets — Nara about the river spirit's warning, Tari about the multiple spirits speaking to her. The secrets are about the same thing, and neither knows the other already knows.

payload.public_status: No public relationship. A daimyo and a wild kitsune would not be seen together.
payload.bond: Takeda thinks he is using Tamamo to create yokai incidents that prove the shrine network's weakness. Tamamo is using Takeda to weaken the wards she hates. Neither trusts the other. Both believe they are the one in control. They are both wrong.

entries.name: Garrick the Wolf and Maggie Pippin

payload.association: bandit and innkeeper, uneasy mutual tolerance
payload.public_status: Maggie's inn is on the Greywood road, which Garrick controls. He does not rob her. She does not report him. A practical arrangement.
payload.bond: Maggie feeds Garrick information about travelers in exchange for him keeping the road safe from other bandits. She does not approve of his methods but recognizes that his presence is better than the alternative. Garrick is protective of the inn in a way he would not admit — Maggie reminds him of his mother, who ran a similar inn before the war.

entries.name: Skald Ravn and Grimvard the Patient

payload.public_status: A frost giant is sitting outside Skaldvik because the skald's poem got the giants' history wrong. Ravn thinks it is funny. Everyone else is nervous.
payload.bond: Grimvard respects Ravn's skill as a poet — the poem is beautiful, it is just inaccurate. Ravn is beginning to realize that the giant is not threatening but correcting, and that the corrections contain information about the deep mountains that no human scout has brought back. They are on the verge of a conversation that could change Hrafnland's understanding of the frost giants entirely.

_help: The engine of the campaign. A thread is something unresolved that will
get worse if ignored.
`next_possible_moves` is the most valuable field in this file. Write the
two or three things that could happen NEXT if the player does nothing.
It is what stops a scene ending on a still frame, and you should revise
it as the campaign moves.
`pressure` here IS live. `stakes` is what is lost if it resolves badly.

payload.summary: A soul new to Gaia has arrived in the Heavenly Realm. The Guide is waiting to help them choose a nation to begin in. The choice is real and permanent — once they walk down into one of the seven nations, they cannot come back to choose again.
payload.stakes: The player's starting nation determines which conflicts they land in the middle of, which people they meet first, and what kind of life they begin. A wrong choice is not death — it is a different story.
next_possible_moves: The Guide describes each of the seven nations in a sentence or two and asks where the player wants to begin.
If the player hesitates, the Guide offers to describe one in more detail — but only one.
If the player asks too many questions, the Guide gently reminds them that the choice is meant to be partly blind.

payload.summary: In Valdris, no new dragon bond has been made in twenty years. The dragon-bonded knights are fracturing between reformers and traditionalists. The king is aging and the succession is unspoken. Sir Aldrich's own dragon, Verath, has gone silent — a secret he keeps because admitting it would confirm the order's worst fears.
payload.stakes: If the order fractures completely, Valdris loses its most powerful defenders. If the succession crisis hits while the order is broken, the kingdom could face civil war. Aldrich's secret, if exposed, accelerates both.
next_possible_moves: The reformist faction calls a formal vote to dissolve the traditional oath requirements, which the traditionalists have promised to refuse — publicly and loudly.
Sir Aldrich's dragon Verath descends from the mountain roosts for the first time in three years and lands in the Dragonrest courtyard, silent, refusing to speak to anyone — including Aldrich.
The king's eldest son visits Dragonrest to 'inspect the order,' a move the traditionalists see as a threat and the reformers see as an opportunity.

payload.summary: The three-year truce between Jin, Chu, and Wei is nearing its end. One border skirmish has already happened between Jin and Wei forces at the Long Pass. The younger officers at the Great Academy in Jin'an speak openly about ending the truce. Warlord Cao Shen is dying faster than anyone knows and wants reunification before he goes.
payload.stakes: If the truce breaks, the largest war in a generation begins. The last war killed tens of thousands. Sangguo's trade routes feed half of Gaia — a war disrupts everything, everywhere.
next_possible_moves: A second skirmish at the Long Pass — this time with casualties on both sides, each blaming the other.
Cao Shen's court physician is found dead in the palace, an apparent suicide that the warlord's spymaster does not believe was suicide.
Chu's warlord Sun Liang receives a secret envoy from Wei proposing an alliance against Jin — and the envoy is intercepted by Jin scouts.

payload.summary: In the Tide Archipelago, sea levels are rising. Islands are losing their shores. The voyagers are being pushed inward toward crowded volcanic islands. Wayfinder Kai has lost three routes this year and the sea spirits have gone silent when asked about the cause. In Verdania, Shaman Nara's river spirit has sent a warning it does not fully understand — and the two problems may be connected.
payload.stakes: If the rising continues, the Tide Archipelago loses its civilization within a generation. If the cause is something that can be stopped, every month of delay costs islands. If it cannot be stopped, the voyagers become refugees in nations that do not want them.
next_possible_moves: Two more outer islets submerge during a storm, displacing forty families who arrive at Lani Atoll with nothing.
Kai attempts a solo voyage to the deepest water in the Archipelago to sing to the sea spirits directly — and they answer, but not in words he recognizes.
Shaman Nara's river spirit delivers a fragment of a warning that mentions 'the deep place' and 'the old door,' phrases it has never used before.

payload.summary: In Al-Khayzar, Malik Idris is the firstborn of his generation — and his family's oldest djinn contract demands the firstborn of each generation as payment. The djinn Zuhayr has begun appearing to Malik, patient and polite, reminding him that the contract is almost due. Malik has searched secretly for a way out and found nothing.
payload.stakes: If Malik cannot break or renegotiate the contract, he is taken by the djinn — not killed, but bound to Zuhayr's service for the rest of his natural life. If he breaks the contract wrongly, the Pact of the Lamp may fracture, and the peace between Al-Khayzar's city-states dies with it.
next_possible_moves: Zuhayr appears to Malik in the Star Bazaar, visible to other binders for the first time, making the debt publicly known — which Malik's family will treat as a deliberate humiliation.
Malik's younger sister discovers his research notes and confronts him — she is not bound by the contract, but she has her own reasons for wanting the family's debts exposed.
A stranger arrives in Zaffar claiming to know a method of contract renegotiation that does not violate the Pact — and asking a price that may be worse than the djinn's.

payload.summary: In Tsukuyomi, the shrine network that keeps wild yokai at a distance from settled areas is weakening. Rural shrines are being neglected as the central authority funnels resources to the capital. Miko Sora maintains her shrine alone, but the ward she tends is one of a chain, and links upstream of her are failing. If enough links break, the yokai pressure on the Cedar Road becomes dangerous.
payload.stakes: If the ward chain breaks along the Cedar Road, the pilgrimage route becomes unsafe and the mountain villages lose their protection. Wild yokai are not monsters — they are unpredictable, and people die when the boundary is weak.
next_possible_moves: Sora notices the upstream shrine's ward has gone dark — the keeper there has left, and no replacement was sent.
A farmer from the next valley arrives in Haru's Shrine Town reporting yokai sightings on the Cedar Road — something that has not happened in a generation.
A messenger from the Great Shrine in Tsuki-no-Miyako arrives with an order: Sora is to report to the capital for reassignment. Her shrine will be 'temporarily' unstaffed.

payload.summary: In Hrafnland, Jarl Sigrid believes the frost giants of the deep mountains are preparing to expand southward. She has been quietly building a coalition of jarls who want to push the giants back. The Althing will not authorize action without proof, and proof requires scouting territory no scout has returned from. Her coalition is not as unified as she presents it.
payload.stakes: If Sigrid acts without Althing approval, she splits Hrafnland and may trigger a jarls' war. If she does nothing and the giants are expanding, the northern fjords are overrun. If she is wrong about the giants' intentions, she has spent political capital on a phantom threat.
next_possible_moves: A trader from a northern fjord arrives in Skaldvik with a story: a fishing village was found abandoned, the boats still at the dock, no sign of violence — and no sign of the people.
One of Sigrid's coalition jarls privately withdraws his support, telling her the Althing will see her coalition as a power grab, not a defense.
A scout Sigrid sent into the deep mountains returns — the first to return — and will not speak about what he saw. He has gone white-haired and will not leave the mead hall.

payload.summary: Kuro the Smoke, a cat-folk thief in Tsuki-no-Miyako, stole a document from a daimyo's estate that contains evidence of Takeda's coalition plans. He does not understand what he has, but Takeda's agents are hunting him. The document's trail leads through the underworld of Tsukuyomi and potentially to Sangguo's information broker Zhou Ba, who would sell it to the highest bidder.
payload.stakes: If Takeda's agents recover the document, Kuro is dead and the coalition remains secret. If Zhou Ba sells it to Cao Shen, Sangguo gains leverage over Tsukuyomi's internal politics. If it goes public, the shogunate cracks down on the provincial clans and the coalition goes underground or open revolt.
next_possible_moves: Takeda's agents trace Kuro to the merchant district and close the gates, starting a block-by-block search.
Kuro contacts a middleman to reach Zhou Ba in Sangguo, not knowing that the middleman is also working for Takeda.
Shogun Ashikara's spymaster independently learns that a document was stolen from a daimyo's estate and begins his own investigation — the shogun wants to know what Takeda is hiding.

payload.summary: King Aldran is dying and has not named an heir. Princess Elara backs the reformist faction and secret dragonbone research. Prince Roderick commands the military and is secretly courting the bandit lord Garrick as a deniable asset. The youngest, Tomas, is unaligned. The court is a cold war of positioning, and the king is running out of time.
payload.stakes: If the king dies without naming an heir, civil war. If Roderick wins, the old order hardens and the reformists are purged. If Elara wins, the dragon order is reformed and the old nobility loses power. If Tomas wins — no one knows, including Tomas.
next_possible_moves: The king's physician quietly informs the court that the king's condition is worsening — the information leaks within a day.
Roderick makes Garrick a formal offer: pardon and a commission in exchange for blocking the Greywood road against Elara's merchant allies.
Elara's reformist researchers achieve a partial resonance from a dragonbone artifact — the first proof that an artificial bond might be possible — and someone in her team talks.

payload.summary: Garrick the Wolf controls a stretch of the Greywood road in Valdris. He is being courted by Prince Roderick as a deniable asset. Maggie Pippin at the Copper Kettle has noticed increased armed traffic. The crown's patrols are getting more aggressive. Garrick's men are hungry and loyal, but loyalty has a shelf life.
payload.stakes: If Garrick accepts Roderick's offer, Roderick gains a deniable military asset on the main trade road. If the crown catches Garrick first, his men scatter and the road becomes truly lawless. If Garrick finds another path — a pardon from the king directly, or a war that needs soldiers — the equation changes entirely.
next_possible_moves: A crown patrol ambushes one of Garrick's foraging parties, killing two men — the first blood on the road this season, and it demands a response.
Roderick sends a sealed letter through Maggie's inn offering terms: full pardon, a captain's commission, and control of the road in exchange for blocking Elara's merchant traffic.
Garrick's second-in-command, a woman named Brita, challenges his leadership at a campfire meeting — she wants to accept Roderick's offer and argues that waiting is dying.

payload.summary: Wen Li, the river-folk canal master in Jin'an, has been warning that the canal system feeding the city's grain supply is failing. Two years of ignored reports and diverted maintenance funds have brought the system to the edge. Wen Li is considering sabotage to force the court's attention.
payload.stakes: If the canals fail, Jin'an loses its grain supply within a season. Two hundred thousand people face famine. If Wen Li sabotages a canal to prove her point, the shortage is immediate but the political will to repair is forced. Either way, people suffer.
next_possible_moves: A canal gate fails during a moderate rain, flooding a market district — a preview of what a full failure looks like, and a warning Wen Li did not engineer.
Wen Li's written report is finally read by Strategist Mei Lin, who realizes the canal crisis connects to the truce: military spending has been eating infrastructure budgets for three years.
General Lu Fang orders the canal workers conscripted into military labor, arguing that fortifying the Long Pass is more urgent than canal maintenance. Wen Li is not consulted.

payload.summary: Kaa the Jaguar-kin found a temple door in the deep jungle of Verdania that was not open before and is warm to the touch. Dr. Voss has calculated a convergence point in the same area. Shaman Nara's river spirit has warned of 'the deep place' and 'the old door.' Monk Jian Yi is walking south toward the same location. Volva Helga has seen it in visions. Multiple independent sources are converging on the same point.
payload.stakes: If the door is opening on its own, something is changing beneath the world. If multiple people are being drawn to it independently, the door may be calling them — or whatever is behind the door is. What is behind it is unknown, but everything touching it — river spirits, sea spirits, whales, chi monks, volva, and shamans — is frightened.
next_possible_moves: Kaa goes back to the door alone, drunk and armed, and this time it is open — warm air pouring out of it, carrying a smell like deep water and old stone.

Jian Yi arrives at the Mist Falls trading post on the edge of Verdania, the first leg of his journey complete, and asks a trader about the temple cities — the trader is Amara, Kaa's cousin, who connects him to Iara.
Shaman Nara's river spirit delivers a new warning: the door is not opening because something is pushing from outside. Something is pushing from inside.

payload.summary: Fatima Idris has discovered her brother Malik's research into breaking the family's djinn contract. She wants to use his crisis to expose the binding families' unsustainable contract system and force reform. She has not told Malik what she knows. Judge Tariq is independently worried about the oldest contracts destabilizing. Layla the Spice Queen is watching, ready to pick up the pieces.
payload.stakes: If Fatima exposes the contracts publicly, the binding families lose face and the council fractures — reform or chaos. If Malik breaks his contract badly, the Pact of the Lamp may fail and the city-states' peace dies. If Judge Tariq finds a legal remedy, there is a path through the law — but the law may not have one.
next_possible_moves: Fatima anonymously leaks a summary of the Idris family's oldest contract to a merchant in the Star Bazaar — not the full text, but enough to start rumors.
Judge Tariq summons Malik to his court, not as a defendant but as a consultant — he wants to understand the Idris contract's structure because it is the oldest and may be the first to break.
Zuhayr appears to Malik in public, at the Star Bazaar, visible to other binders — making the debt common knowledge and forcing the family to acknowledge it.

payload.summary: Rashid the Sand-walker has found a working fragment of the Old Road in the deep desert of Al-Khayzar — a two-hour stretch connecting the Mirror Oasis to a point near the Verdania border. The fragment hums like a voice, which is not how Old Roads behave. He is deciding who to tell, and the hum is getting louder.
payload.stakes: A working Old Road fragment is the most valuable secret in Gaia — it could connect Al-Khayzar to Verdania in hours instead of months. If the hum is a voice, the Road may be doing something Old Roads are not supposed to do. If the wrong person learns about it, the secret becomes a weapon.
next_possible_moves: Rashid returns to the fragment to find that the hum has changed — it is now a rhythm, almost a heartbeat, and the air above the Road is shimmering.
A binding family agent notices Rashid's absences and follows him to the Mirror Oasis, not to the fragment itself but close enough to suspect something.
The fragment extends — the Road is growing, clearing itself, pushing back the sand, and the hum is now audible from the oasis.

payload.summary: Fin the Whale-speaker has learned that the great whales are leaving the Tide Archipelago — not migrating, but departing permanently. They are swimming south, past Verdania, toward the open ocean. The images they send him — deep water, a door, something waking — match the warnings from Shaman Nara, Monk Jian Yi, and Volva Helga. Without the whales, voyaging in the Archipelago becomes vastly more dangerous.
payload.stakes: If the whales leave, the Archipelago loses its oldest allies and voyaging becomes far more dangerous. The displaced islanders cannot be relocated if the sea routes are unsafe. Whatever is driving the whales south is connected to the same force that is opening doors and frightening spirits across the world.
next_possible_moves: The last family of whales in the northern Archipelago sends a final image to Fin — a clear picture of the door, from the other side, showing something behind it that is large and moving — then the whales turn south and are gone.
Kai's attempt to sing to the sea spirits at the deepest water goes wrong: the spirits answer, but not in words he recognizes, and the current around his boat changes direction against the wind.
Elder Wayfinder Pua announces to the guild that she will sing the deepest song — the one she has not sung in forty years — and the guild argues about whether it is safe.

payload.summary: Daimyo Takeda Renji is building a coalition of rural clans who feel the shogunate has abandoned them. He has a secret alliance with the wild kitsune Tamamo, who is willing to create yokai incidents to prove the shrine network's weakness. His plans were stolen by the thief Kuro, and the document is now in play. The shogun is dying and the succession is undecided.
payload.stakes: If Takeda's coalition succeeds in forcing the shogunate's hand, the provinces gain power and the shrine network is repaired — but Takeda is positioned as kingmaker. If the coalition is exposed prematurely, it becomes a rebellion. If Tamamo engineers a yokai incident that kills people, Takeda's legitimate grievance becomes a bloody opportunism.
next_possible_moves: Tamamo engineers a yokai breach on the Cedar Road — nothing fatal, but enough to frighten pilgrims and prove the wards are weak. Takeda uses the incident at the next clan council to argue that the shogunate has failed.
The shogun's spymaster traces the stolen document to Takeda's estate and begins investigating the daimyo's coalition — quietly, because accusing a daimyo without proof is a political act.

The shogun's elder son, Ashikara Kenji, confronts Takeda at court — not about the coalition, which he does not know about, but about the yokai incident, which he blames on Takeda's territory being poorly defended. The irony is not lost on Takeda.

payload.summary: Mana the Tattoo-carver believes that wayfinder tattoos are not just records — they are anchors. When a route is submerged and the tattoo fades, the wayfinder feels it as physical pain. She suspects the tattoos are helping hold the sea-routes in existence, and that losing wayfinders and routes may be connected to the rising seas, not just a consequence of them.
payload.stakes: If Mana is right, the wayfinders are not just navigating the sea — they are holding it together, and the loss of routes is accelerating the rising waters. This would mean the Archipelago's crisis is partly self-reinforcing: lose an island, lose a route, lose a wayfinder, lose more sea. If she is wrong, it is a theory that wastes precious time.
next_possible_moves: Mana presents her theory to Elder Wayfinder Pua, who takes it seriously — because Pua has suspected something similar for forty years and has never said so.
A wayfinder carrying a faded route-tattoo collapses during a voyage, screaming about pain in the tattoo — the first time the effect has been visible to witnesses, not just felt by the carrier.
Mana begins carving a new set of route-tattoos on Kai, including a route that was lost last month — to test whether carrying a lost route on a living wayfinder can restore it.

_help: Prose. Religions, histories, laws, languages, how the world got here.
Do not reach for a record here unless something must point at it, be
counted, appear in a panel, or be hidden from the player. Until then a
paragraph in your world/*.md files is better — see MIGRATING.md.
`context_tier` controls whether the narrator may reason about it:
pinned (always) / partial (one line) / searchable / hidden.

payload.summary: Occasionally a person arrives in Gaia carrying memories of another life — another world entirely. These souls are rare, perhaps one in a generation. They arrive in the Heavenly Realm, where a guide helps them choose a nation to begin in. They are called god-touched, and the name is both a compliment and a warning. They often grow into remarkable people, and just as often into troubled ones.

A vanished network of spirit-paths that once connected every nation in Gaia. Walking a working stretch can take you across the world in an afternoon. Most are broken. Some are lost. A few are deliberately kept shut by the people who live near them. Finding a working entrance is valuable. Using one is noticeable — the Roads leave a trace that certain people can follow.

A generation of relative peace across Gaia, following the last great war between Sangguo's states. The peace is uneven — some nations prosper, others simmer. The treaty that ended the war is fraying, and not everyone remembers why it was signed. The current generation is the first to grow up without war, and some of them do not understand what they would be losing.

_help: Objects worth naming. `appearance` feeds the image pipeline; keep story
and provenance in `description`, which the pipeline never reads.

payload.appearance: Small metal discs, about the width of a thumbnail, stamped with the mark of the minting nation. Each is slightly different — Tsukuyomi's carry a crescent moon, Valdris's a crown, Sangguo's a jade-inset square. They are traded by weight, not by origin.
payload.description: The closest thing Gaia has to a universal currency. Accepted across all seven nations by weight. Each nation mints its own, but the metal content is standardized by an old trade agreement that most nations still honor.

payload.appearance: A strip of paper, about the length of a hand, with brush-written characters in black ink. Some carry a red stamp at the bottom. They are usually folded and carried in pockets or pinned to doorframes.
payload.description: The basic tool of shrine magic in Tsukuyomi. An ofuda carries a ward, a blessing, or a command. It must be written correctly and activated by a shrine keeper's ritual. A poorly made ofuda is just paper.

payload.appearance: A carved wooden staff, about shoulder-height, marked with notches and painted symbols that represent star paths, current patterns, and island positions. The wood is dark from salt and handling. Some staves have shells or bone inlays.
payload.description: The primary tool of a wayfinder in the Tide Archipelago. The staff is both a record of routes memorized and an instrument for reading the sea. A wayfinder who loses their staff loses years of encoded knowledge.

_help: The opening. One campaign is created from this; you can make more later
in the app.
`player_name` and `character_class` are the player's, and the engine
builds their character record. `current_location` must be one of the
location ids above.
campaign.title: The Arrival
campaign.current_quest: Choose which of the seven nations to begin your new life in.
campaign.opening_scene: You wake in a garden you have never seen. The air is warm and still, and the light comes from no direction you can find. Floating islands drift in soft mist around you, and flowers bloom in colors that do not belong to the same season. Ahead, through a grove of trees that are not quite real, stands an open pavilion. A figure is waiting there, seated on the stone bench, watching you with patient dark eyes. Below the pavilion, far below, through layers of cloud, you can see a world spread out — green and gold and blue and white. Seven nations. The figure speaks: 'You have arrived. That is well. I have been waiting. Come, and choose where you will begin.'
